What if I told you Brooks Running started out making ballet slippers and bathing shoes? Founded in 1914, the Seattle-based company spent decades making just about everything except running shoes, moving from baseball cleats to roller skates, football cleats, children’s shoes, and softball cleats. It wasn’t until 1972 that Brooks made running its focus, and the company has been refining the category ever since.
Brooks introduced one of the industry’s earliest uses of EVA foam, developed the first running shoe with a breathable GORE-TEX upper, and introduced the Kinetic Wedge, an innovative design tailored to women’s anatomy.
So, while Brooks may not be the trendiest brand, it has built a reputation for dependable support, comfort, and durability. Here at WIRED, Brooks has plenty of fans, especially for trail and gravel running. The company also offers apparel we regularly recommend, including sports bras, outerwear, and running bottoms.
Brooks Running shoes are reasonably priced for performance running footwear, with many models hovering around $150. If you’re in the market for a new pair, I’ve rounded up the best Brooks Running promo codes and coupons worth checking out.
Brooks Running Black Friday Deals
If you want new kicks for the new year, be sure to shop the Brooks Running Black Friday Deals & Cyber Monday Deals section, where you’ll find steep discounts on men’s and women’s running shoes, gear, and apparel. You’ll find deep discounts on popular shoe styles like the Adrenaline GTS 25 and the Glycerin Flex. Plus, when you shop the Brooks Running Black Friday sale, you’ll get a free gift with a $160 purchase.
Score 20% Off Your First Order With Brooks Promo Code
If you’ve never ordered from Brooks’ website before, new customers get 20% off their first order after subscribing to the email list. You can apply the one-time Brooks coupon code to top-selling shoes, like the Caldera 7 and Adrenaline shoes, as well as other gear and apparel. It’s an easy way to save on some of their top products and take your road and trail running game to the next level.
More Brooks Coupons and Offers
Are you already a member of Brooks Run Club? If you sign up, you get member perks like early access to sales, free standard shipping with no order minimum, and free express shipping on orders from Brooks. Membership also includes more runner-specific perks, such as a free birthday gift and the chance to earn prizes by syncing your fitness tracker and contributing research to the Brooks team. You can also win a chance to visit the Seattle flagship store and have your gait analyzed by Brooks’ team. To join, visit Brooks Run Club and register using the Brooks promo code.
If you shop and buy a complete outfit in one transaction from one of Brooks’ recommended buying guides—like Warm Weather Running Outfits or Fall Weather Running Outfits—you can get 15% off automatically applied at checkout. This is a fantastic deal if you only just realized in the past 10 days that you’ve been running in hail in your tiny shorts and cropped sports bra.
Save on Our Favorite Brooks Running Shoes
Brooks makes so many iconic running shoes that it’s hard to list them all. I’m currently running in the Brooks Glycerin Max, which is one of the cushiest shoes I’ve ever tried. I don’t feel particularly stable on uneven terrain, but the padding is noticeably springy and cushy if you’ve been putting in some serious miles. WIRED director Michael Calore is a fan of the Brooks Ghost line, and if you’re planning to hit the trails in the cold, wet Pacific Northwest, I’d suggest the Brooks Cascadia Gore-Tex. The Adrenaline is the company’s most popular shoe.
Preorder Your Favorite Glycerin Now
One of the most anticipated Brooks drops is the Glycerin line. These shoes are built to be durable while allowing freedom of movement and flexibility. The cushioned shoes are comfortable for running and movement on many types of terrain. Many shoes in the Glycerin line are available to pre-order, including the Glycerin Flex, Glycerin 23, and Glycerin GTS 23. Be sure to check out the Glycerin line to see which is best for you.
The Cascadia Elite Is Available Now
Brooks is constantly dropping new shoe styles, ensuring there’s a shoe for every runner. The new Cascadia Elite Brooks Running shoe is unisex and great for trail running, with PEBA cushioning, a Vibram Megagrip Elite outsole, and a MATRYX engineered woven upper with Kevlar fibers to help secure your feet firmly, no matter what terrain you’re traversing. This shoe has light, springy cushioning that helps propel you forward, whether that’s competitive trail racing, Sub-ultras, VKs, or ultras.
Upcoming Brooks Sale Events to Watch Out For
Do you have a runner in your life? The odds are they’re taking stock of their winter apparel and shoes, deciding whether these leggings will make it through another winter. The best time to save is during seasonal sales, with discounts on footwear and apparel, including popular items like the Ghost 16 running shoes.
Do you have running military, nurses, or first responders in your life? Brooks Running also offers 25% off full-priced items for verified community heroes with a Brooks promo code. Sign up here.
Brooks Discount: Shop Pre-Owned Shoes at Brooks
If you’re looking for a new pair of shoes but don’t have the cash to invest in a brand-new, high-end pair, look no further than Brooks’ restock page, where gently used Brooks shoes are on sale at deeply discounted prices. They have both men’s and women’s sections, recently added shoes, and a breakdown of bestselling styles, including the Adrenaline, Ghost, Glycerin, and Hyperion.
Brooks Coupon: 20% Off Join the Brooks Run Club
If you’re looking to shop at Brooks, it’s a great idea to join the Brooks Run Club for additional perks and discounts. Some of the best benefits Run Club offers include a 20% discount on apparel when you join and an annual birthday gift. You’ll just need to log in or join the club to get the discount code.
Brooks Sports Medicine Ambassador Program: 40% Off
If you’re a sports medicine professional, you can save big and get rewarded at Brooks Running. The Brooks Sports Medicine Ambassador Program is a free membership for eligible sports medicine professionals, a way to say thank you for the care they provide to runners and athletes. All you have to do is verify your status by signing in or creating an ID.me account to confirm your qualifications. Then, you’ll get a steep 40% discount on the first $1,000 spent on eligible items in Brooks Running online orders (it resets every January 1).
Brooks Return Policy and 90 Day Wear Test
Brooks knows how important gear is to athletes. So, you can take your Brooks gear for a 90-day trial run, and if you aren't satisfied, return it for free. If you’re at all unsatisfied with your Brooks purchase, you can return it for free with no shipping or restocking fees.

49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
- Published
The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again.
The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1.
They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2.
Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2.
The Chiefs and Broncos could be joined by the Cincinnati Bengals, who conclude week 11 at the Washington Commanders on Monday.
49ers outsmart Vikings defence
Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence.
After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one.
Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot.
The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City.
The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners.
Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown.
With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines.
San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week.
Giants secure statement win
The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games.
Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter.
The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five.
The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win.
It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South.
In his first season as head coach, John Harbaugh could lead the Giants to their first division title since 2011, when 'Big Blue' went on to claim their fourth Super Bowl.
They remain clear of the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys, whose rollercoaster season continued with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans, with Dak Prescott throwing for 325 yards and four touchdowns.
Kelce at the double before tough Chiefs run
Although Josh Allen threw for more interceptions than touchdowns (2-1), the Bills were still comfortable, beating the Miami Dolphins 26-9 for their sixth straight victory.
The Bills have a mouth-watering Thanksgiving clash on Thursday (01:20 GMT, Friday) at home to the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-7.
Travis Kelce had two scores for the Chiefs, claiming multiple touchdowns in the same game for the first time since a play-off win over Buffalo in January 2024.
Emmett Johnson registered a combined 143 yards and a touchdown in the absence of fellow running back Kenneth Walker, who is set to return from a minor groin problem against Buffalo.
That game kicks off a crucial five-game stretch for Kansas City, which continues against the Rams, the Bengals, the Patriots and the 49ers.
The Chiefs are joint top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, who kept the pressure on by beating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 for a sixth straight win.
Fernando Mendoza, this year's first overall draft pick, threw his first three touchdown passes but then a pick-six which allowed Denver to clinch victory, after Jonah Coleman had run in three scores for the Broncos.
Bears and Lions set up Thanksgiving showdown
The home team won all seven of the early games, and they were favourites heading into all but one of those match-ups.
The only underdogs to emerge victorious were the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7), who beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 19-16 to end a seven-game losing streak.
The Bears and Lions both won to remain joint-top of the NFC North, and they have a Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit on Thursday (18:00 GMT).
The Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13, with Chicago's Jeffery Simmons claiming three sacks, taking his tally to five in three games since his blockbuster trade from Tennessee.
On Thursday he will try to stop this season's rushing leader Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for another 98 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The NFL's highest-paid running back has now tied Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns (52) before turning 25 – and Gibbs' birthday is not until March.

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.
In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.
While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has asked all government medical colleges and their attached hospitals across the country to onboard the Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM-RAHAT) scheme to expand access to cashless emergency treatment for road accident victims.
In a communication to deans, directors and principals of government medical colleges and medical superintendents of attached hospitals, the NMC said the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare had requested its intervention to facilitate their participation in the scheme. The request followed a September 24 meeting of the steering committee monitoring its implementation, chaired by the Secretary of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, which emphasised wider engagement with the medical community.
The NMC has asked institutions to accord priority to onboarding, with the National Health Authority (NHA) guidelines providing the framework for empanelment and registration of hospitals.
Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 13, 2026, PM-RAHAT provides cashless treatment of up to ₹1.5 lakh per road accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to ensure that emergency care is not delayed during the critical ‘golden hour’.
Under NHA guidelines, hospitals already empanelled under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) will be deemed eligible. Other facilities can be empanelled under the ‘PM-RAHAT Only’ category, while hospitals capable of providing initial stabilisation can register under ‘PM-RAHAT Lite’.
Designated hospitals must have round-the-clock emergency services, intensive care units, operation theatres, imaging and blood storage facilities, and specialists in trauma care, emergency medicine, general surgery and orthopaedics.
The guidelines also prioritise hospitals near identified accident hotspots, National and State Highways and other accident-prone road networks. State Road Safety Councils will coordinate implementation, while the NHA will maintain the digital platforms for hospital onboarding and claims management.

The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.
Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.
Morales García’s case took that turn as the White House has faced bipartisan criticism for the aggressive mass deportation campaign pursued by Donald Trump throughout his second presidency – widely seen as a factor in the electoral battering his Republican party suffered during the 3 November midterms, costing it control of Congress.
The Denver-born, Mexico-raised Morales García was riding with his boss to his job as an air-conditioning installation technician on 3 April when they were pulled over by state and local officers near Fredericksburg, Texas.
Morales García was his boss’s passenger and did not have his identification on him. The 25-year-old also told the officers that he had his birth certificate and social security card at home, but they didn’t believe him – so they called immigration agents, who detained Morales García.
Court filings recount how Robert Gil Jr, a US Customs and Border Protection agent, consulted records from Mexico that listed a Mexican birthplace for Morales García. Gil Jr also accused Morales García of saying he was born in Mexico and observed that he only spoke in Spanish, according to court records.
Morales García was deported on 7 April, with the Trump administration later accusing him in a media statement of being in the country illegally.
Morales García’s attorneys sued on 1 May, maintaining that he had falsely said he entered the US illegally and signed papers for a rapid deportation in response to threats of imprisonment by agents. His lawsuit, which seeks an unspecified amount of money, also contended that family and friends tried to deliver documents proving his US citizenship before this deportation.
But those efforts were unduly rebuffed, Morales García’s lawsuit said.
The Trump administration denied Morales García’s assertions, saying on Friday that he went to Mexico voluntarily and therefore lacked any basis to sue the federal government for damages. Nonetheless, in court filings on Friday, the administration conceded that Morales García “was permitted entry” back into the US on 30 August after it reviewed “information concerning plaintiff’s place of birth”.
“Plaintiff is a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico,” Justin Simmons, the US attorney for the western district of Texas, wrote in a court filing first reported by the Texas Tribune.
Americans are not required to carry proof of citizenship when going about their daily business. Lawyers across the US have seen cases such as Morales García’s, which begin after an encounter with local authorities demonstrate how those officials are generally not aware of the nuances of immigration policy.
Texas’s public safety department is among many US state and local agencies that collaborate with federal immigration authorities under their 287(g) program.
The judge presiding over Morales García’s lawsuit, Robert Lee Pitman, did not immediately rule on the Trump administration’s request on Friday to dismiss the case. The lawsuit also named unspecified local and state Texas law enforcement officers as defendants.
An October 2025 report by ProPublica found that immigration agents had detained more than 170 US citizens during the first nine months of Trump’s second presidency.
Meanwhile, the media statement incorrectly saying Morales García was in the US illegally is among several related to immigration enforcement under the Trump administration that has unraveled under scrutiny.
A Guardian analysis published in July reviewed Trump administration press releases on 26 cases of cars allegedly being used to assault immigration enforcement agents – and nearly all were either disproven or dropped.

A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.
Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

Just days ago, Jensen Huang’s chances of returning as Nvidia CEO looked increasingly slim, at least according to prediction markets. Earlier this month, Huang resigned from the AI hardware giant following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence services. As more reports emerged about Huang’s alleged bad behavior, Nvidia’s board insisted it had no plans to reinstate him. By early Sunday morning on the East Coast, traders on Polymarket’s US platform put his chances of returning at just 10 percent. But by Monday, Huang was back in charge.
The swings in Huang’s odds on prediction markets offer a window into how his unlikely comeback unfolded and who saw it coming. The New York Times reported that President Trump played a crucial role in convincing the board to bring Huang back. Traders who paid attention to what Trump and his allies wanted appear to have fared much better than those who did not.
On Sunday evening in Washington, Huang’s odds on Polymarket US jumped six percentage points in just 40 minutes after Trump published a Truth Social missive calling for Huang’s reinstatement. The president said he wanted to help revive the stock market, which had plunged following Huang’s scandal, a sign of Nvidia’s enormous influence over the AI industry and broader US economy.
According to the prediction market intelligence firm Betting Intelligence, odds on both Kalshi and Polymarket’s markets largely tracked with public signals about the likelihood of Huang’s return. They rose when Huang said he was open to returning, fell when the board dismissed the possibility, and climbed again when President Trump threw his support behind the former CEO. But there were several large trades that could not be tied to public developments.
Betting Intelligence and the prediction market forensics firm MSR Decode identified clusters of trades on Huang’s return that did not appear to be driven by news or public commentary. Kalshi and Polymarket declined to comment on whether they are currently investigating potential insider trading in markets related to Huang’s return.
Despite these anomalies, Betting Intelligence CEO Dan Zimmermann says the Huang-related markets showed fewer signs of potentially suspicious activity than usual. “The group that could have known the board’s decision in advance was small. So the market was mostly headline chasers and longshot buyers,” he says.
For traders who profited from Huang’s comeback, the lesson is clear: Don’t discount Trump.
Isaac Rose-Berman, a research and policy fellow at the American Institute for Boys & Men and professional sports bettor, says he made approximately $10,000 wagering on Huang’s return on Kalshi. He placed his trade after the Nvidia chief said on X that he was open to reclaiming his old job. Rose-Berman says that he figured that the board would consider Huang’s return if it looked likely to improve the company’s stock performance. (Never mind the concerns about national security or Huang allegedly threatening employees that he would “pee in your brain.”) “It’s 2026 and Trump is president, scandal schmandal,” Rose-Berman says. “Should’ve bet more.”
A pseudonymous prediction market trader known as Domer tells WIRED he cleared approximately $600,000 by placing an early wager last week on Huang’s return. He wasn’t focused explicitly on Trump’s desires, but he says his understanding of power dynamics ultimately guided his approach. “Boards can be very malleable,” he tells WIRED.
Other prediction market “sharps” say that commentary from Trumpworld was the strongest signal available about Huang’s return. As some bettors noted, there was a notable opportunity for profit after Trump suggested to a PBS NewsHour reporter that Huang would be back in power soon, but before Nvidia officially announced his reinstatement. “The key was looking at Trump’s support and the recent performance of the stock market,” says Kalshi trader Caleb Davies.
Aaron Courtney, a data analyst and cofounder of a prediction market analytics firm, says he took a loss on his Huang position. Looking back, he says his mistake was not paying attention to what Trump and other administration officials said over the weekend. “Trump saying he hoped Nvidia would bring Jensen back would be the clearest signal,” he says.

Mumbai: Indian banks are bracing for rising stress among crop-loan borrowers in drought-hit states, offering loan restructuring and fresh credit while easing off on recoveries.
A deficient monsoon, amid El Niño conditions, has prompted six states to declare drought in certain parts, raising concerns over food inflation and pressure on the rural economy. El Niño, characterised by abnormal warming of waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean, can affect the distribution of rainfall across the Indian subcontinent.
The six states—Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Telangana—had a combined  ₹12 trillion in outstanding agriculture loans as of 31 March, accounting for 11% of their total bank credit, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data. A shortfall in rainfall could hurt crop output and farm incomes, putting repayment capacity under pressure. CareEdge Ratings expects the bad-loan ratio for agricultural loans to rise to 5.5% by March 2028 from 5.1% currently, and potentially cross 6% depending on the extent of stress.
There are concerns that lower crop yields in the coming season could strain rural cash flows, said Vineet Jain, senior director at CareEdge Ratings. Combined with elevated inflation, this could put further pressure on rural households and lead to a deterioration in banks’ asset quality.
Bankers said they are rolling out measures to ease the burden on rural borrowers, but have yet to see significant uptake.
“The policies are ready, following discussions at state-level bankers’ committee (SLBC) meetings, but so far not many borrowers have availed themselves of these measures,” said the chief executive of a large public sector bank.
The banker, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said borrowers were likely to approach banks eventually, but were still assessing the extent of the impact on their finances. The banker added that, under the applicable restructuring framework, these loans would continue to be classified as standard, rather than being downgraded to non-performing assets, as can happen with other loan restructurings.
Measures
State Bank of India (SBI), the country’s largest lender, has identified ₹10,000 crore worth of loans as a potential pool for restructuring. Chairman C.S. Setty told analysts on 3 November that past experience showed that relatively few borrowers come forward to seek restructuring. SBI’s agriculture loan portfolio across India stood at ₹4.5 trillion in the second quarter of FY27, up 22.6% from a year earlier.
Over the past couple of months, bankers have met at state-level forums, in the presence of regulatory and government officials, to work out support measures for distressed borrowers. At a meeting of the Maharashtra State-Level Bankers’ Committee on 6 October, for instance, lenders decided to restructure existing short-term crop-production loans, reschedule instalments and extend fresh credit, according to a letter dated 12 October.
In Karnataka, bankers held a special meeting on 10 September to discuss similar measures. They were given until 9 January to implement them.
“The chairperson gave a strong directive that this is not a year for harsh recovery measures or creating panic among farmers,” according to a copy of the meeting minutes seen by Mint. The meeting was chaired by Uma Mahadevan, additional chief secretary and development commissioner, Government of Karnataka.
Bad-loan ratio
CareEdge Ratings’ Jain said that, since the stress stems from a natural calamity, banks can restructure agricultural loans in districts where the state government has declared drought. They have until February 2027 to use this window, he said. As a result, the impact is unlikely to show up in the March 2027 numbers.
CareEdge expects the agricultural bad-loan ratio to improve from 5.1% in September to around 4.7-4.8% by March 2027, supported by growth in outstanding loans and write-offs of bad loans. “However, it will increase by March 2028 to 5.5% and could even cross 6%, depending on the stress,” Jain said.
Analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, said in a note on 4 November that India’s weakest monsoon since 2015 would increase downside risks to agricultural loan quality. Agricultural lending remains the principal source of additional credit risk, the note said.
Bankers, however, remain optimistic that they can manage the impact of the drought. Rajneesh Karnatak, chief executive of Bank of India, said the lender’s September-quarter financials showed little impact on asset quality. Its agriculture loan portfolio stood at ₹1.2 trillion as of 30 September, up 16.3% from a year earlier.
“We feel that with the kind of robust systems that the bank has built, all the banks have built, and the agility with which we are working, we are confident that we’ll be able to tide over these headwinds,” Karnatak told analysts on 23 October.

New Delhi: India has shortlisted 11 candidates for its top drug regulator post, advancing the selection process for the regulator of its $60 billion pharmaceutical sector, as the government steps up scrutiny of drug quality, including medicines meant for export.
The Union health ministry has shortlisted the candidates from 28 applicants for interviews, according to two officials and a document reviewed by Mint. The shortlist has been cleared by a three-member screening panel under revised recruitment rules that expanded eligibility for the post of Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI).
The post falls vacant on 1 March 2027, when incumbent Dr Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi’s second one-year contractual term ends.
The selection comes as India, the world’s pharmacy for low-cost generics and vaccines, faces renewed scrutiny of its drug-quality standards. Over the past few years, Indian-manufactured cough syrups have been linked to more than 140 deaths globally, including in Gambia, Uzbekistan and Cameroon, following contamination with toxic industrial solvents such as Diethylene Glycol (DEG) and Ethylene Glycol (EG).
The government is also sending a team to the World Health Organization to learn best practices and better align domestic drug inspections with global standards.
The shortlisted candidates will now be sent to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for final interviews. The final appointment will be cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), one of the officials cited earlier said.
The DCGI heads the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO), which is responsible for ensuring the safety and efficacy of drugs, medical devices and clinical trials.
Queries sent to the spokesperson of the health ministry and DCGI office on Saturday remained unanswered until press time.
Wider pool, broader expertise
The 28 applicants included officials from the CDSCO, the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), state drug-control departments and academic institutions such as AIIMS New Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, NIPER Ahmedabad, and IIT-BHU.
Applications also came from the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in Lucknow, the National Dope Testing Laboratory, the National Centre for Disease Control, an autonomous state medical college in Uttar Pradesh and the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
The revised Recruitment Rules, 2026, notified in April, expanded the pool of eligible candidates. In a first, the framework allows candidates with master’s degrees in non-pharmacy engineering disciplines, including mechanical, electrical and computer science, to apply alongside those with degrees in pharmacy, chemistry, life sciences and medicine. A doctorate is considered an added advantage.
Applicants must have at least 15 years of practical experience in drug manufacturing, testing, clinical trials or medical-device oversight. The 1 August 2026 recruitment advertisement said the post would be filled on a deputation or short-term contract basis for up to five years, with an upper age limit of 58 years.
“Once the UPSC conducts the final interviews and recommends a candidate, the final appointment will be cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC),” the official cited earlier said.
“Alongside supportive government policies and recent Goods and Services Tax (GST) rationalizations aiding the sector, achieving long-term goals requires shifting from volume to value and maintaining regulatory continuity. It is not about the person; it is about that position. Whoever comes into that place has to ensure that the industry, regulator, and academicians all work together—that integration is more important than anything else,” Viranchi Shah, national spokesperson, Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association (IDMA).

Electric vehicle (EV) giant VinFast is building a dedicated electric two-wheeler production line at its Thoothukudi manufacturing facility in Tamil Nadu. Speaking with Inc42 on the sidelines of the company’s V Creator All Star Summit 2026, VinFast Asia chief executive Tapan Ghosh said that the manufacturer expects its first set of electric scooters to roll out of the plant early next year. Anurag Saxena, the India CEO of VinFast's escooter division, said that the two-wheeler production line is being developed independently of the existing car assembly operations. While the company has not yet disclosed the initial capacity of the scooter line, Saxena said that the facility will be able to churn 10 Lakh units annually at maximum capacity. However, the company does not plan to immediately invest in infrastructure to manufacture 10 Lakh scooters annually. Ghosh said that production capacity will be scaled in line with customer response, market demand and the performance of individual product launches. Besides electric scooters, the Vietnamese EV maker also plans to double down on its investments in India and is gearing up to expand its manufacturing footprint in the Southern state. Ghosh said that the EV maker’s India arm has received approval for the second phase of its broader $2 Bn investment in the country. However, he did not disclose the final investment outlay, the additional production capacity or the implementation timeline. As part of this, the EV giant last year signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the Tamil Nadu government for an additional 500 acres of land. If materialised, the agreement will expand the size of its existing 450 acre Thoothukudi plant to nearly 950 acres. The MoU, signed in December 2025, had outlined a proposed $500 Mn additional investment in the unit, which would pave the way for building dedicated production facilities for electric buses. However, VinFast appears to be recalibrating its electric bus plans. Ghosh told Inc42 that VinFast is not focusing on the electric segment for now, but is rather concentrating on scaling its passenger car and electric two-wheeler businesses. He indicated that the company does not want to spread its resources across too many product categories simultaneously, adding that VinFast rather wants to adequately support the products it has launched. VinFast’s India Journey VinFast commenced operations at its $500 Mn manufacturing facility in Thoothukudi in August last year. The plant, spread across nearly 450 acres, was developed as part of the company's planned $2 Bn investment in India. The facility currently assembles VF 6 and VF 7 electric SUVs via the complete knock-down (CKD) route and has an installed annual production capacity of 50,000 vehicles. For context, a CKD facility is simply a plant where components are assembled together into a full-fledged car. Ghosh said that the facility was constructed within 17 months, with the initial investment directed entirely towards establishing VinFast’s car manufacturing infrastructure. In addition, the EV maker has been steadily trying to increase its foothold in the Indian electric car market. As per the Vahan data, VinFast registered 2,570 vehicles in October 2026, emerging as one of the top five electric passenger vehicle companies in India. At present, its demand is driven roughly by personal electric vehicles, which drive 60% of its sales. VinFast’s electric ride-hailing arm Green SM accounts for the remaining 40% of the sales. Ghosh told Inc42 that the company retails about 1,200-1,300 cars through dealers every month, while Green SM buys about 1,000 more. This translates to about 3,600 car sales every month at the upper end of the spectrum or about 43,200 registrations a year. As such, VinFast’s current monthly sales remain well below its total installed capacity of 50,000 units annually. But the Vietnamese OEM is betting on growing its dealer network and local assembly unit to carve a niche in the Indian EV market, which is projected to become a 132 Bn opportunity by 2030.

We weren't able to confirm, as of this writing, precisely how many barrels of lead azide would be exploded.
In mid-November, a rumor spread online that the U.S. Army had plans to set off two detonations to destroy an old cache of lead azide — a highly explosive compound — in Middletown, Iowa, on Nov. 20.
"The Army found 68 barrels of the explosive that had been stored at the plant for more than 20 years," one Facebook post read (archived). "Lead azide becomes more unstable as it ages and can detonate with slight movement or friction, making it unsafe to move off site."
The claim spread across other platforms, with several Snopes readers also contacting us for answers.
In short, the claim is true. Here's what we know:
Army confirms explosions will take place
The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant launched a campaign to inform the public about the upcoming explosions, including an open house on Oct. 15 and a notice (archived) on Nov. 15 warning people in the affected area to evacuate and inviting residents to shelter at the Armed Forces Reserve Center during the explosions if needed.
In a document titled "Keeping Our Community Safe," the Army described how plans to reduce harm from the explosion by using specialized water misters and cleaning and removing affected soil and debris once the operation ceases.
(U.S. Army)
The public warnings issued by the Army to residents in the area were as follows:
- Consider avoiding the affected area.
- If you are inside of the affected areas, avoid outdoor air by staying indoors.
- Keep windows and doors closed.
- If it is safe to do so, set heating and cooling systems to "recirculate" to minimize outdoor air exposure and maximize indoor air filtration until the plume passes by your community.
- Avoid unnecessary travel through impacted areas.
- After the US Army determines the air exposure period has ended, consider cleaning indoor and outdoor surfaces such as play surfaces for children and windowsills.
- If your car was parked outside, consider washing your car at a car wash to minimize your contact with potentially exposed surfaces.
Is the circulated 'blast zone' map accurate?
In the circulated map shown in the Facebook post above, the blast zone appears to stretch approximately 100 miles northeast from the blast site. We compared this map to maps the Army released ahead of the planned detonations and found they aligned.
(Facebook user Live Storm Chasers and U.S. Army)
As Nov. 20 draws closer, the Army's maps will be updated. Residents in the area were encouraged to regularly check for updates.
What is lead azide and how did it get there?
According to the Environmental Protection Agency, lead azide is a "hazardous waste that exhibits the characteristic of reactivity (energetic) and exhibits the characteristic of toxicity for lead." In a public notice (archived) Nov. 16, the EPA wrote:
The recrystallization of the stored lead azide has increased the material's sensitivity to friction and shock, and disturbing the containers of lead azide could create an unacceptable risk of unintentional detonation. The Army's evaluation of a range of potential alternatives for the treatment of lead azide culminated in the secretary of the Army selecting in-place, controlled, intentional detonation for the treatment of lead azide.
The material is used to initiate munitions, according to a Q&A document the Army published.
It's unclear precisely how the lead azide stores came to be stored at that underground location. While a number of media outlets reported that 68 barrels would be detonated, we were unable to confirm that amount. We contacted the Army seeking more context and information about the history of the lead azide stores and will update this story if we receive a response.
In March, the Army announced that experts were conducting a safety review for the "safe removal of a chemical compound currently at the plant."
On Nov. 17, local ABC affiliate KCRG reported that local activists were planning a "peaceful demonstration" against the planned detonations.
Group organizers were reportedly demanding:
- An immediate halt to the Nov. 20 lead azide detonation, at minimum until affected communities have had an adequate opportunity to review the risks and alternatives.
- Full transparency regarding the potential environmental and public health consequences.
- Independent environmental experts to review the proposed disposal method and evaluate safer alternatives.
- A comprehensive plan for independent air, soil, and surface testing in potentially affected communities.
- A commitment to clean up and remediate any lead contamination resulting from this operation, at no cost to affected residents and property owners.

“Michael” director Antoine Fuqua has been accused of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress by a Los Angeles bar manager following an incident back in February during which Fuqua allegedly pulled a gun on and struck the employee in the head.
In a 10-page civil claim filed Friday in the Los Angeles Superior Court, William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, is said to have denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter because they were “visibly overly intoxicated.” Rosenthal was then spat on by a member of the group, to which Rosenthal told them they needed to leave the bar. An hour later, Fuqua accused Rosenthal of pepper-spraying his daughter, and when the manager denied the allegation, Fuqua “pulled out a handgun” and “struck” Rosenthal in the face. Fuqua then “directed a racial and antisemitic slur” and “threatened to kill him.”
“As Plaintiff staggered back in pain, Defendant Brando Fuqua, appeared and approached Plaintiff and forcefully swung a handgun at Plaintiff’s face,” read the complaint. “Defendants Antoine Fuqua and Brandon Fuqua then pointed their handguns at Plaintiff, placing him in imminent fear for his life, before fleeing down the street.”
Rosenthal is seeking $50,000 as a result of his suffering “serious physical and psychological injuries” which include a nose fracture, head injury, skin lacerations, post-traumatic stress disorder, severe emotional distress and severe scarring, all of which continue to cause him “great physical and mental pain and suffering.” The claim noted that Rosenthal believes said injuries “will result in some permanent disability.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced Monday a $1.62 billion (24,000 crore Nepali rupee) economic assistance package to help Nepal rebuild areas devastated by deadly Himalayan floods in August this year.
In a joint press statement with Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah, PM Narendra Modi said, “We extend our deepest condolences for the lives lost during the recent flash floods in Nepal. India announces a 24,000 crore [ ₹240 billion] Nepali rupees development package for Nepal.”
The August 26 floods in Nepal destroyed roads, bridges, power plants, farms and homes, causing an estimated $4.7 billion in losses, according to Nepali authorities. The UN Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage also pledged about $20 million to support Nepal’s recovery.
As many as 1,500 people were killed and more than 5,200 were missing in the aftermath of the floods.
PM Modi announced the aid after meeting Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah in New Delhi on Monday.
Shah is on his first visit to India since taking office in March, six months after a youth-led uprising over corruption and nepotism forced former Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli from power.
PM Modi said the assistance would help restore infrastructure, rebuild communities and support people who lost their homes and livelihoods.
"Our commitment will be to help affected families get their lives back on track, create new opportunities and further strengthen Nepal’s capacity to deal with future disasters,” PM Modi said.
Shah thanked India for consistently acting as a first responder for Nepal "in times of natural disasters and difficult hours".
"I warmly welcome Indian investors to Nepal to partner in the economic prosperity of our two countries in the coming days," Shah said, and invited PM Modi to visit the Himalayan nation.
The two countries signed agreements to boost their economic relationship.
PM Modi and Shah also virtually inaugurated a hydropower project and an oil storage facility in Nepal, as well as an oil pipeline and a cross-border train service connecting the two countries.
Nepal shares an open border with India, allowing people to cross without passports or visas. India has traditionally wielded considerable influence in the Himalayan nation, but ties have been strained by territorial disputes and accusations of political interference.
China, meanwhile, has expanded its presence in Nepal in recent years, investing in airports, highways and hydropower projects, the Associated Press reported.
Despite growing Chinese influence in Nepal, the landlocked country remains heavily dependent on India for fuel and other essential supplies. At the same time, energy ties have become increasingly reciprocal, with India importing around 1,200 MW of electricity from Nepal.
($1 = 148.6200 Nepalese rupees)

When medical student Emmanuel Oyebadejo went to watch his friend's American football game, he had no idea he would end up being scouted himself for a sport he had never even played.
He wasn't even interested in it. In fact, while still at school in Manchester he'd delivered a speech titled 'I have a dream' in which he outlined plans to do "very well in basketball, return from the NBA and be the prime minister of the United Kingdom".
But now, four years later, he is being tipped to become the first Briton to be a first-round pick in the NFL Draft.
It is a rapid rise for the 22-year-old, who had to learn the game from scratch and win over his parents who "begged" him not to play and instead focus on his medical studies.
His biggest challenge at the start, though, was finding a pair of boots big enough for his size 16 feet.
It was 6ft 6in Oyebadejo's physique that had caught the eye of the coaching staff at Exeter Demons when he was a spectator for his friend's university game that was taking place at the club's home ground, The Crumb.
"I was talking to one of the other coaches, Jack Mullins, and we sort of turned around [and thought] 'that guy's freaking huge! We should go talk to him'," Lydon Ward-Best, one of the Demons' coaches, tells BBC Sport.
Oyebadejo had been a talented basketball player, playing for Manchester Magic - one of England's top junior clubs - from the age of 11 to 18. But by the time he was at the University of Exeter he was no longer playing competitively.
Lydon Ward-Best persuaded him to give a new sport a go.
"He started coming to training and just had the most ridiculous intro to American football I think I've ever seen," the coach adds.
A straight-A pupil, who had also learned the piano, guitar and drums while studying medicine, Oyebadejo had always been a quick learner.
"I always say that American football is kind of like violent chess," says Mullins, the Demons' current head coach.
"[Emmanuel] got the violent bit pretty quickly. He was fine at that - 'I am much bigger than you, watch me go'.
"The chess bit took a little longer because there's all these things that you have to think about."
But as Ward-Best puts it, "he's not just a big sort of jock athlete, he's a smart guy. He is so dedicated and disciplined with everything."
Oyebadejo played for the Demons at the end of the 2022-23 season, before the team went unbeaten in his first full season, 2023-24. When back home he also played for the Manchester Titans and helped them win the Britbowl in September 2023.
By December 2023, he decided he wanted to take things further. Could he make it in the United States? Would college teams be interested if he sent them videos of his highlights?
Coach Ward-Best told Oyebadejo it would be "tough", adding: "You know the percentages are not on your side here, but you are 6ft 6in and 280 pounds (20 stone), so you've got a better chance than most.
"I wanted to be realistic with him," he adds. "But I said I'd do whatever I could to help get him out there."
Emmanuel's father Oladini says he thought it was a "joke" and that he did not support him playing this "dangerous" game, explaining: "He had never played this game before. He'd only done it for a few months, so why would anybody from America want him?"
But they did.
There was interest from several colleges and Oyebadejo ended up at Jacksonville State, where he would study biology and play under legendary college coach Rich Rodriguez, having managed to win his parents round thanks to the influence of an uncle who lived in Dallas and understood the sport.
His first season was hit by injury but, despite coming up against players who have played American football since they were young children, his second was a big success.
As a defensive end, Oyebadejo's job is to get past the offensive linemen trying to block him and tackle the ball carrier or claim a sack - when a defensive player tackles the quarterback behind the line of scrimmage.
He recorded 4.5 sacks, forced two fumbles and had 41 total tackles during the 2025 season.
Now the big college teams were paying attention.
College football is America's most passionate sporting pastime. While the NFL plays on Sundays, the college game dominates Saturdays during the autumn months.
And Oyebadejo transferred to the University of Florida to play for one of college football's biggest teams in the most prestigious conference, the Southeastern (SEC).
The Florida Gators are three-time national champions, have about 50 former players currently in the NFL and get home crowds of 90,000 at 'The Swamp'.
Oyebadejo was undaunted as he burst on to the scene. He had 2.5 sacks in a win at rivals Auburn in September and followed that up by impressing in big wins over Mississippi and Texas, the latter in front of 103,989 people.
After barely being on the radar of NFL scouts at the start of the season, Oyebadejo's form has propelled him into contention to be an early-round draft pick in 2027.
NFL teams do not have youth systems or academies. Almost all players have come through the US college system and they are recruited via the NFL Draft when they graduate.
One of the biggest events in the American sporting calendar, the NFL Draft takes place over three days in April, with the 32 teams taking turns to select players across seven rounds.
First-round picks in April will be guaranteed a rookie contract of at least $19.1m (£14.4m) and they are often fast-tracked into starting roles. The contract values decrease in a sliding scale so, for example, a third-round pick (top 96) will be guaranteed $7.3m (£5.5m).
Among the latest prospects, ESPN's veteran draft analyst Mel Kiper has ranked Oyebadejo as the fifth-best edge rusher (defensive end). That is regarded as the sport's second-most important position behind quarterback - and therefore the second-best paid in the NFL.
The reason is that Oyebadejo has everything needed to be a starting defensive end in the NFL. Firstly, his height and weight are ideally suited for the grappling battle required in what is known as 'the trenches'.
He has very long arms (7ft wingspan), perfect for winning a wrestling match against the kind of enormous opponent he faces, and unusually for a man as big as him, he's extremely quick. That's the money-making trait.
Although he now weighs about 300lbs (more than 21 stone), it is believed he has a remarkable body-fat percentage of about 12%. All his measurables are seen as ideal for a defensive end, if not better.
There are simply very few people with Oyebadejo's physical talent, and given the fast-tracked nature of his rise in American football, he does not look as raw as you might expect.
"He's British and has only played the sport for three [full] seasons," says his mentor and former coach Ward-Best. "You'd therefore think he must be very green, but he doesn't look that way.
"The physical qualities are clearly there but he's worked a lot on mastering aspects of the position as well."
Menelik Watson, also from Manchester, holds the record for being the highest-drafted British player. He was the 42nd pick in 2013 and spent six years in the NFL, earning a total of $16.4m (£13.7m).
London-born Osi Umenyiora, the 56th pick in 2003, enjoyed an illustrious 12-year career - winning two Super Bowls with the New York Giants.
"I have spoken to Osi, he's a really cool guy," says Oyebadejo, who is also of Nigerian heritage.
"To be a first-round pick out of the UK, it would be amazing. It would do so much for the American football community back home."
Oyebadejo impressed again in an upset win at Kentucky on Saturday and has 4.5 sacks with two regular-season games left. Florida could then play in a 'bowl' game, an end-of-season exhibition.
After that, Oyebadejo is expected to participate in a physical-testing event called the 'scouting combine', where he will be assessed by representatives of all 32 teams in March.
The draft then begins in Washington DC on 27 April, and if Oyebadejo hears his name called, he will complete an unlikely journey and make his now fully supportive parents very proud.
"It's mad," says Ward-Best. "I've been doing this for 20 years and I've never seen anything like this. We almost have to pinch ourselves."
Oyebadejo has stayed in touch with his former coaches in Exeter. The Demons hold watch parties for Florida games and there is a real sense of pride over where his journey began.
"It was just complete chance that he wanted to wander up to The Crumb and watch a game, just being there for his mate," says coach Mullins.
"If those things didn't happen, we wouldn't be having this conversation. He would be four years into his medical degree."

What's on the cards for Modi-Shah meet?

The discussions between Modi and Shah will provide political direction for charting the future of bilateral ties over the coming years, they said.
While India has proposed a joint vision for the long-term development of bilateral ties, Nepal has sought a $2-billion economic package, including $1 billion in grants, and aid for the reconstruction of areas devastated by the Bhote Koshi flash floods in August.
Nepal has also asked for the Kathmandu-Mahendranagar air corridor to be made two-way. International flights are currently permitted only to leave Nepal via this route.

The passenger, identified as Singaporean tourist Lim Weng Shang, arrived at Varanasi Junction on Friday aboard train number 22416, the New Delhi–Varanasi Vande Bharat Express.
While getting off the train, the TOI report said, he inadvertently left one of his bags behind inside the coach.
The oversight came to light only after the rake moved to the maintenance yard for routine cleaning and inspection. While checking Coach E1, attendant Anoop Kumar and cleaning staff member Karan Singh noticed the unattended black bag at seat number 35, the report said.
Recognising that it belonged to a passenger, the duo immediately alerted the RPF rather than treating it as ordinary lost property, TOI reported.
Following the alert, an RPF team led by Sub-Inspector Charan Singh arrived at the maintenance yard to take charge of the bag.
According to the TOI report, to maintain transparency and establish ownership, the bag was opened and inspected in the presence of Deputy Station Superintendent (Outdoor) Vakil Singh, revealing a substantial stash of cash across four different currencies.
Around the same time, Shang realised his bag was missing and rushed back to Cantt railway station accompanied by his guide. He approached railway officials and shared specific details about the black bag and its contents.
Using those details to match his claim against the recovered bag, officials verified Shang’s identity and questioned him to confirm ownership before handing over all his belongings intact.

Varanasi station director Arpit Gupta told the publication on Saturday that the bag and all its contents had been handed back to Shang after completing the verification protocol.

Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Monday (November 23, 2026) reacted to the presence of several masked youths in a BJP election rally in Agartala on Saturday (November 21). He said he had come to know this from newspaper reports and subsequently took up the matter with the party leadership.
“I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,” he told reporters.
Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) are due on November 27. The ruling BJP has already won five of them unopposed as candidates from other parties and independents did not submit nomination papers.
The appearance of several masked men at the BJP’s election rally in Agartala stirred controversy, with CPI(M) and Congress registering complaints to the state election commission. The Congress also lodged a complaint at the West Agartala Police Station.
Secretary of the State Election Commission on Monday (November 23) said they received complaints about the issues and forwarded them to the police headquarters for necessary action. He said the commission would ensure free and peaceful elections.
BJP sources said veteran minister and city campaign in-charge Ratan Lal Nath organised the procession. They said the masked youths were actually party supporters from Mohanpur, north of Agartala, home Assembly constituency of minister Nath.
CPI(M) and Congress, however, claimed the masked men were actually anti-socials who were likely to be engaged in creating trouble and rig the elections. They also complained of the silence of the police in initiating action despite registering complaints.

It seems India's fintech investors may have counted their chickens too early. The timeline for the much-anticipated merchant discount rate (MDR) on select UPI transactions has been deferred further down the calendar. The proposed monetisation of India’s UPI ecosystem was expected to be a post-Diwali bonus for digital payment companies, with a promise of a much-needed revenue stream after years of operating in a largely zero-MDR environment. However, uncertainty around the rollout is now weighing on investor sentiment, with shares of Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik enduring a sharp correction. Consequently, the optimism that once buoyed fintech stocks is fading. As of Friday (November 20), Paytm parent One 97 Communications had already fallen as much as 10.8% over the past week, while One MobiKwik Systems declined 6.6% and Pine Labs dropped 9.4% on the BSE. According to a Financial Express report, the implementation of MDR could be deferred until after the 2027 assembly elections in five states, amid concerns over potential pushback from merchants and trade associations. There has been no official confirmation of a revised implementation date. The proposed framework envisages a 0.4% MDR on eligible person-to-merchant (P2M) UPI transactions above ₹2,000, subject to a cap of ₹300 per transaction. Certain categories, including railways, telecom, insurance and fuel, are proposed to attract a flat ₹5 charge, while P2P transactions and specified small merchants would remain outside the framework. For payment companies, MDR represents more than an incremental revenue stream. It offers a route to monetise transaction volumes that have expanded rapidly but historically generated limited direct revenue. Initially scheduled for October 15, the rollout was first deferred until after Diwali. Now, the prospect of a further delay has put the earnings assumptions behind recent brokerage upgrades under scrutiny. With the market jumping the gun on UPI monetisation, what does it mean for companies like PhonePe and Razorpay that are preparing for their public-market debuts? But before answering that, let’s understand how much MDR earnings upside was priced in for Paytm, Pine Labs and MobiKwik. When The Market Jumped The MDR Gun The September MDR announcement had triggered a wave of bullish brokerage commentary on payment companies, with analysts betting that the proposed charges would improve the economics of UPI transactions and open up a new source of recurring revenue. For Paytm, the potential upside was particularly significant. Goldman Sachs estimated that the framework could generate incremental EBITDA of around ₹1,400 Cr for Paytm in FY28 under a high-end scenario. The estimate represented 43–70% of its existing FY28 EBITDA projections, highlighting the potential scale of the earnings opportunity. The brokerage maintained its buy rating on the stock. Jefferies and JM Financial raised their target price to ₹2,150. JM Financial estimated incremental revenue of ₹210 Cr in FY27 and ₹470 Cr in FY28, with incremental adjusted EBITDA reaching ₹440 Cr in FY28. Pine Labs was another expected beneficiary, given its large merchant-acquiring and payment acceptance business. Jefferies estimated an incremental revenue opportunity of ₹160 Cr by FY28, equivalent to approximately 20% of its FY28 EBIT and profit estimates, and raised its target price to ₹235 from ₹180. Emkay, meanwhile, projected ₹155 Cr in UPI MDR revenue for FY28, assuming a realised take rate of six basis points, and increased its target to ₹230 from ₹190. The opportunity was supported by Pine Labs' transaction mix. In its Q2 FY27 investor presentation, the company said more than 70% of its digital checkout point transactions were UPI-led, with monthly UPI gross transaction value (GTV) of approximately ₹20,000 Cr. More than 65% of this UPI GTV came from transactions above ₹2,000, potentially placing a significant portion of its merchant payment activity within the proposed framework. Pine Labs also said its monthly UPI GTV could reach ₹33,000–34,000 Cr by FY28. MobiKwik, too, outlined the potential benefit. During its November earnings call, cofounder Upasana Taku said MDR implementation could add at least ₹100 Cr to the company's payments revenue in FY28, although the charges would be shared among issuing banks and other payment ecosystem participants. Atul Thakkar, executive director at Anand Rathi Investment Banking, believes the recent sell-off in the fintech stocks is largely a reversal of the optimism surrounding the proposed framework. “This is MDR euphoria unwinding, not a change in the businesses,” he said. According to Thakkar, the trigger was the report of a further delay, with no new implementation date in sight. But the magnitude of the correction needs to be seen against the rally that preceded it. In the period around the September MDR announcement, Paytm rose approximately 11%, MobiKwik 12% and Pine Labs 21%. From their November highs, the stocks have fallen 8–11%, with Pine Labs returning to early-September levels. Paytm shares rose 7% to ₹1,903.05 on Thursday, hitting their highest level since listing in November 2021. “The market priced in more than a normal expectation, and that excess is what has come out,” said Thakkar of Anand Rathi. The MDR uncertainty also brings to the fore: how much of the optimism surrounding listed fintechs was fuelled by the promise of the proposed framework, and how much was grounded in the strength of their underlying businesses? Fintechs’ Other Revenue Engines All three fintech companies had reported profits in the latest quarter even without any MDR contribution. The proposed charges, therefore, were not what made their businesses viable. Instead, they offered an additional revenue stream that could improve the economics of payment processing and accelerate profitability. It is particularly relevant for Paytm. Its management has also sought to position MDR as an incremental opportunity rather than a prerequisite for growth. CFO Madhur Deora had said earlier that UPI MDR was an upside to the company's business model, not fundamental to it. The company's financial services revenue, which grew 49% YoY to ₹912 Cr in Q2 FY27, also points to the growing contribution of businesses beyond payment processing. For MobiKwik and Pine Labs, too, the case for growth extends beyond the proposed fee. MobiKwik is looking to build out its financial services business, while Pine Labs has revenue streams across affordability, issuing, online payments and international markets. The larger issue, Thakkar's assessment suggests, is not whether these companies can grow without MDR, but whether investors had begun treating the proposed framework as a more certain and immediate earnings driver than it actually was. Therefore, with the implementation date still unclear, companies may have to demonstrate that their core payment and financial services businesses can sustain growth and profitability without relying on the additional MDR contribution. MDR Overhang For Upcoming IPOs The uncertainty comes at a crucial time for India’s fintech sector, with several large private companies preparing to test the public markets. The correction in listed peers could influence valuation benchmarks of players like PhonePe. Sources told Inc42 that PhonePe is targeting an early 2027 listing (February or March) at a valuation of around $10 Bn. With approximately 45% of merchant payments, the company was expected to benefit from greater clarity on monetising its payments business. A further delay could now cloud those assumptions. Razorpay has also moved closer to its public-market debut. It is also targeting a January–March 2027 listing, with an issue size of ₹5,000-6,000 Cr and a valuation of around $5 Bn. Although Razorpay has diversified into business banking, payroll, lending and cross-border payments, payment acceptance remains central to its merchant ecosystem. Therefore, investors could scrutinise its payments margins and monetisation assumptions more closely if MDR implementation remains uncertain. All in all, the MDR delay may not derail upcoming fintech IPOs, but it could make investors more cautious. For now, companies will have to justify their valuations through profits, not just the promise of future earnings. Kerala High Court sets aside suspension of 16 Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit students
The Kerala High Court directed the university to arrange special examinations for the students within six weeks
The Kerala High Court on Monday set aside the suspension of 16 Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (Kalady) students and quashed a varsity inquiry report against them over a protest on the campus in August.
A bench of Justice PV Kunhikrishnan directed the university to arrange special examinations for the students within six weeks. They were not allowed to take the exams beginning November 4.
“Petitioners shall be allowed to enter the campus of the respondent university and attend regular classes forthwith. Respondent [university] shall hold a separate examination for the petitioners, as undertaken before the apex court expeditiously, at any rate within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment,” the court said.
It underlined that the university can order a fresh inquiry against the students, but they must not be suspended pending inquiry again.
The students staged an indefinite hunger strike demanding their reinstatement and permission to take the exams. They were suspended on September 1 for protests on August 13, during which they allegedly held a mock funeral of the vice-chancellor and obstructed her while she was leaving the campus. The students claimed they held a mock funeral of the campus stage lights, which were not functioning.
Opposition leader Pinarayi Vijayan called the indefinite hunger strike and the legal victory inspirational for students trying to protect democratic values on campuses. “The protesting students maintained the firm resolve that they would not apologise as they had done nothing wrong. This was an extraordinary student movement that refused to bow down to the persecution by those in power and the denial of justice,” Vijayan said in a statement.
The Opposition Communist Party of India (M) criticised the action against the students, mostly affiliated to the Leftist Students’ Federation of India.
In October, a single-bench allowed the students to take the examinations. A division bench stayed the order, saying students did not meet the requisite conditions for attendance, prompting the students to approach the Supreme Court, which refused to intervene and referred it back to the high court.

A graduate student who is a scientific researcher at Princeton University was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement earlier this week while traveling home after presenting research at the annual Society for Neuroscience conference in Washington D.C.
The researcher, Eva Yi Xie, was detained Thursday. Although she has lived in the U.S. since 2016 after moving to the country from China, her visa had expired, according to the New York Times. Her lawyers told a reporter Xie had a pending asylum application and was thus allowed to remain in the country legally.
The news, first posted by a mentor of Xie’s on X, ricocheted across the academic circles on Friday, in part because it seemed to crystalize pervasive fears of non-U.S. academics and international students that traveling to conferences, to present new research and network with colleagues, may be too risky under a second Trump administration that has cracked down on immigration.
“There’s, I think, an open question about whether or not it’s safe for people who are international students visa to travel, because there have been these detentions, and that’s a very scary prospect,” said Caitlin Rivers, who similarly had a staff member of hers detained by ICE earlier this year. A number of conferences have reported smaller attendance at conferences in the U.S. over the past two years, and some have considered the prospect of hosting in other countries.
ICE did not respond to a request for comment as to why Xie was detained. But the administration has been vocal in its desire to reduce the number of foreign-born graduate students in the U.S. In its science blueprint released earlier this year, the White House wrote “America’s over-reliance on foreign students also creates a security challenge.”
Xie is not the first graduate student to be detained, either. Most notably, Tufts researcher Rumeysa Ozturk was detained by ICE in Cambridge, Mass., and later decided to leave the country. A report released earlier this week found that international graduate student enrollment is down by a third at academic medical centers.
“News of Eva’s detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,” Rodney D. Priestley, the dean of Princeton University’s graduate school wrote in a statement, adding the university has provided Xie with legal representation. “We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton.”
Xie’s work lies at the intersection of neuroscience and artificial intelligence; she uses a combination of experiments on mice and large datasets of neural recordings to understand how different portions of the brain work together to make decisions. While only a third-year PhD student, she is viewed as a rising star by some of her colleagues.
“I think it speaks to how exceptional of a researcher Eva is that she can work on projects that really span multiple disciplines, that require that she go and learn the foundations, not just of AI and machine learning, and not just computational models of the brain, but also understanding how do you run the experiment on the mice. She’s in the lab actually doing the surgery on the mice, gathering the data from the mice, analyzing those data, and running the AI experiments,” said Benjamin Eysenbach, a computer scientist at Princeton and one of Xie’s three advisers.
As an example of the respect she commands among peers, he cited a workshop she convened at last year’s NeurIPS conference, one of the premiere machine learning conferences. Not only did she present research of her own, but she brought together leaders in AI and in neuroscience to see how the two could collaborate.
It was an opportunity both to “introduce these important questions about the brain to folks in AI that might be equipped with new methods, and to help folks working on neuroscience questions define what are the right AI tools,” Eysenbach said.
Krithik Ramesh, a fellow researcher, is among those who has benefitted from her guidance. The two had overlapped at science fair competitions throughout high school, and when he was considering transferring to the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where Xie had completed her undergraduate degree, he turned to her for counsel. He learned about Xie’s detainment after a friend saw a post on social media. His immediate reaction was disbelief, followed by a sense of unmooring as a fellow researcher.
“We academics exist for the benefit of the public,” he said. “We are very privileged as a country to have people like Eva continue to pursue academia at the highest level, and to share that with other people. That’s literally the nature and reason why we go to conferences to present stuff. It is appalling to me that she cannot do that with reasonable certainty that she can’t be detained.”

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.
Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). The findings align with research showing adolescent girls endure very high rates of intimate partner violence.
“These are really sad figures,” said Jean-Paul Murunga, a lawyer with the global human rights organisation Equality Now. “Especially given that the continent of Africa as a whole has adopted the Maputo protocol, which sets [binding legal standards for] equality between women and men. We still have a lot of work to do to ensure women and girls benefit from these commitments.”
The Maputo protocol, a landmark treaty adopted by the African Union in 2003, guarantees women’s rights and obliges states to protect women from violence. It affirms that marriage must be based on full consent and guarantees women’s right to health.
“The underlying principle is unambiguous: sexual intercourse without free and voluntary consent constitutes sexual violence, including within marriage,” said Murunga. “Marriage does not create perpetual or implied consent. A woman retains the right to decide whether, when and how she engages in sexual activity”.
He said that as a first step rape laws across the continent needed to change. According to Murunga’s 2024 report, rape within marriage is not criminalised in some African countries. Seven countries expressly exempt husbands from prosecution for marital rape, including Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia and South Sudan. Some countries, such as Tanzania and Eritrea, only criminalise marital rape when the couple do not live together.
In countries where child marriage is permitted and marital rape is not criminalised, children are left unprotected. A legal loophole is created for what, outside marriage, would be classed as rape, and young wives have few options when it comes to protecting themselves from sexual violence and exploitation. In Gabon, for example, when a man has married a child he abducted, he can only be prosecuted after the marriage is annulled.
Underpinning these laws is the mistaken belief that marital rape does not exist as a concept because, by marrying, wives are assumed to have permanently consented to sex with their husbands. In many areas, religion plays a key role in affirming these beliefs.
Alimatu Dimonekene, founder of A Girl At A Time, an organisation supporting adolescent girls in Sierra Leone, said a conversation around consent in marriage had yet to begin in Africa. “We’ve not even started the conversation [around marital rape],” she said. “Women will never call it rape; they make excuses for it or even blame themselves.”
She added: “In west Africa, sex is seen as an obligation in marriage. You must do whatever your husband demands.
“Once he has paid your bride price [a traditional marriage custom in which the bride’s family are paid money, livestock or goods by the groom], he owns you and you cannot reject his demands. Whatever he wants, he gets, including in terms of intimacy, finances and raising the children.”
