The Mundka monitoring station of the Delhi Pollution Control Board recorded a PM2.5 concentration of 3,744 µg/m³ at 2 am on the Diwali night, which is 60 times the standard measure. Yes, you read it right. 60 times. Reports emerged the next day that 93 of the top 100 cities with worst AQI were from India following Diwali celebrations on November 8. AIIMS pulmonologist Vijay Hadda told ANI on November 9, “I am honestly surprised that we are still alive. I do not think this kind of air is suitable for human survival.”
In any country with a functional government, this would warrant the environment minister to at least make a statement, even if not take direct accountability. Not in India.
Union minister of environment, forest and climate change, Bhupender Yadav, has remained conspicuously silent on the country’s deteriorating air quality before or after Diwali.
From the days preceding Diwali to four days after the festival when this article is being written, Yadav neither issued a single public appeal urging citizens to responsibly engage in celebrations, nor used his social media handles to spread awareness about the environmental consequences of bursting firecrackers or to address the mounting pollution crisis affecting major parts of the country.
Did Bhupender Yadav go Missing from Public Platforms?
Far from it. Yadav remained active on social media throughout this period. Between November 1 and November 12, he made 29 posts on his X account. Not one of them addressed the worsening air pollution, deteriorating air quality across Indian cities, or the need for public awareness and precautionary measures.
The days before Diwali are also crucial because pollution levels skyrocketing on the day of the festival and immediately after has become an annual phenomenon. It is reasonable to expect the minister holding the environment and climate change portfolio to make a public appeal ahead of Diwali, more so because firecracker pollution has been a matter of contention and has reached the Supreme Court in recent years.
Clearly, the Alwar MP thinks otherwise.
Modi Reigns Supreme on Yadav’s X Timeline
On November 7, observed as Chhoti Diwali, and November 8, the main day of Diwali, Yadav shared nine posts. These included amplification of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Diwali greetings to citizens, Modi’s Diwali celebrations and interactions with jawans at the CoBRA (Commando Battalion for Resolute Action) Operations Base in Karanpur, in Chhattisgarh’s Bastar district, as well as Yadav’s own festive greetings.
On November 7, Yadav shared a video of Narendra Modi greeting fellow citizens with wishes for Diwali and shared that, like every year, he would celebrate Diwali with the “veer jawans” of the country.

Thereafter, he shared a video of Uttar Pradesh tourism celebrating Diwali at Ayodhya Ram Mandir.

The next five posts were devoted to PM Modi’s Diwali celebrations with the security personnel in Bastar, including his interactions with the jawans stationed at the CoBRA base. (View them here: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
Updates on Political Assignments etc
A review of Yadav’s remaining social media activity during this period shows that he continued to document his political engagements, meetings with public representatives, participation in political programmes and official engagements.
On November 1, Yadav attended the “Save democracy, remove anarchy” rally alongside the Maharashtra chief minister and deputy chief minister. The following day, he met the Governor of Uttarakhand. On November 3, he met Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami and Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary in Delhi.
On November 5, he shared another post about his participation in the ‘Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy’ protest in Darbhanga, Bihar. He also posted about his visit to the residence of senior BJP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Dr Ravindra Kishore Sinha, where he met Sinha’s son, Rituraj Sinha, and other family members and paid his respects.
On the same day, Yadav addressed the media in Patna on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, alleging that ‘planned attacks are being carried out on the country’s constitutional institutions by the Congress’.

On November 9, he attended the funeral of Dr Jaswant Yadav, the MLA from Bahror and former Member of Parliament, alongside the Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma.
His latest post, on November 12, documented an interaction chaired by him with Indian LeadIT (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) member companies and project partners in New Delhi.
In addition to these engagements, five of Yadav’s posts during the November 1–12 period were dedicated to sharing decisions taken by the Union Cabinet on various policy matters.
Despite maintaining a steady stream of updates on his political engagements, official meetings and public appearances, the environment Mminister’s X account offered no indication of concern over the environmental consequences of the widespread bursting of firecrackers during Diwali. Neither before it. Nor after.
Incidentally, on October 30, Yadav posted about an integrated command and control centre in Delhi to review and monitor air pollution real-time across Delhi-NCR.
The Firecracker Pollution Debate was Raging Since October 25
As early as October 25, Delhi Police had shared a video on its X handle urging citizens not to burst crackers this Diwali. The post said: “This festive season, let tails wag, not tuck. Say NO to crackers, YES to a greener Diwali.” Soon after it was posted, social media users predicted that it would be taken down. Delhi Police proved them right, deleting the post within hours.
The episode sparked a debate, with a section of the Right-wing putting forward what has become its usual pre-Diwali stance on firecracker pollution: that any call to shun firecrackers or celebrate with restraint is an affront to Hindu faith. The debate intensified when Bengal Police did much the same thing, posting about “responsible celebrations” before deleting the post, and the Mumbai civic body took down a similar post featuring actor Dia Mirza.
Yadav, it appears, has been blissfully unaware of all this.
There were no cautionary appeals ahead of the festivities urging citizens to celebrate responsibly or remain mindful of the deteriorating air quality and the environmental and health hazards associated with firecrackers. Nor did Yadav acknowledge the worsening situation in the aftermath of the celebrations, when several Indian cities were engulfed in thick layers of smog, and the country dominated global rankings of the most polluted cities.
Alt News has reported that on the morning after Diwali, the front pages of all major English dailies were dominated by news about severe air and noise pollution in most cities in north and central India.

Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
- Published
An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.
The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government.
The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.
Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said.
Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC also shows a boat on fire at 05:47 GMT at the Benghazi port.
US-based intelligence firm Vantor collected high-resolution images that it said showed Project 20380 Steregushchiy-class corvette (Merkury) - a Russian navy ship - moored in the port on Saturday, and on Sunday showed most of the same ship capsized and sunk with only the forward bow still visible.
The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship - which it did not name or identify - was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.
Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.
GNS condemned the attack on a ship inside a Libyan port, and called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty. It said Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.
Separately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.
GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".
Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.
Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.
Although it has not been officially confirmed who was behind the attack, there is little doubt, according to Jalel Harchaoui, Libya specialist at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).
"Ukraine is the only actor brazen enough to pull something like that off," he told the BBC. "If I were to bet my own money, I would bet that it was the Ukrainians."
If confirmed, it would not be the first time Ukrainian forces had carried out an operation of this sort. In March, Russia accused Ukraine of targeting the Russian tanker Arctic Metagaz in the Mediterranean between Libya and Malta with "uncrewed sea drones" launched from the Libyan coast.
As well as having an economic impact on Russia, hampering the ability of their so-called shadow fleet of tankers to export oil and gas, attacks like this are seen as humiliating to the Kremlin, according to Harchaoui.
But it is not only Moscow that will want to react to this latest incident. The ship was in the region as part of a deal with the government of eastern Libya - allied with Khalifa Haftar, commander of the Libyan National Army.
Harchaoui said Haftar will take the attack as a personal slight. "You're going to have a response by the Haftar family. They will ask questions about who is hosting the Ukrainians."

US Army to detonate tonnes of unstable explosives in Iowa despite court order
- Published
The US Army plans to move ahead with detonating five tonnes of degraded explosives in Iowa despite a ruling to halt it indefinitely, a new court filing shows.
"To protect its personnel and the surrounding communities, the Army needs to take swift action," the justice department notified the court on Saturday. "Protection of human health and the environment demand action now, not delay."
The court had ordered a pause after environmental groups sued to stop the detonation, arguing the army failed to consider safer alternatives.
The detonation was originally scheduled for Friday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. The army now plans to act by 24 November under an emergency exemption.
In the new filing, the Department of the Army argued that a controlled detonation was necessary to protect the public from an unplanned explosion, a risk it said would become more likely as temperatures were set to fall in the coming days.
"There is an immediate risk that the lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant will explode as temperatures are expected to drop below 30 degrees Fahrenheit (-1C) in the next several days," the filing states.
It argued that the army had removed the doors to the bunker where the barrels were stored in preparation for the detonation and that made the explosives more "vulnerable to temperature changes".
The government has not released details for the rescheduled detonation.
Earlier, the army had warned residents to leave their homes for six hours on the original scheduled day of the explosion, for the duration of the explosion and until the dust settled. An advisory warned "all humans" to avoid being outside in the affected areas while the demolition detonation was set to take place.
Lead azide is a highly volatile compound used as a detonator. Earlier this year, the IAAAP found that the material had degraded over time to the point where it was now too risky to move the material, according to Iowa Public Radio.
On Friday, the military said it was working with the Department of Health and Human Services and the EPA to ensure the explosion was done in the safest manner possible.
Military and environmental officials determined that detonating it in place was the safest way to eliminate the explosive safety hazard.
The EPA, which granted an emergency permit to detonate 68 drums of the material, said it did so because the explosion risk "presented an imminent and substantial threat to human health and the environment".
One of the Environmental groups suing to pause the detonation, the Iowa Environmental Council, argued that many Iowans living within the risk-zone were unaware that the explosion was scheduled to happen.
"There is no safe level of lead exposure, and Iowans were given just days to prepare for the November 20 detonation," the organisation said in a press statement.
The Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club, which filed the lawsuit on Thursday that prompted the court-ordered pause, filed a new motion on Sunday in response to the army's filing.
The group asks the court to pause proceedings so that it may submit additional information before the scheduled detonation.
The motion includes declarations from environmental experts and local officials who support pausing the detonation, citing a lack of public notice and questioning the Army's claim that delay would cause significant risks.

An August 14 summit is unlikely to have seen participation by India at any level.The only significant visit to Pakistan from India after the April 2025 Pahalgam attack was by MEA additional secretary Alok Dimri for a meeting of the SCO national coordinators in September – shortly after Pakistan assumed presidency – to firm up the calendar of events under Islamabad's stewardship.After what is officially called Meeting of Ministers of Culture (SCO-MMC), Pakistan will also host more high-profile meetings of the SCO defence and foreign ministers in the run up to the Islamabad summit in August.
The meeting for cultural cooperation among SCO member-states in Pakistan is a relatively low-stakes event for India that keeps political commitments minimal, unlike the foreign and defence high-level gatherings which might raise the political temperature at home.The last minister to visit Pakistan was S Jaishankar for a meeting of the SCO foreign ministers' meeting in October 2024, well before Pahalgam.Amid criticism by the Opposition for hosting Pakistan minister Musadik Malik for the Modi-proposed civilisational dialogue last week, India reiterated there was no dilution of its position on the Indus Waters Treaty that was "put in abeyance" after the Pahalgam attack. India has administered more than one crore doses of the HPV vaccine in less than nine months since the launch of the nationwide campaign in February 2026.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2124707476616675534
According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, India has administered more than one crore doses of the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine in less than nine months since the launch of the nationwide campaign in February 2026.
The campaign provides free, safe and voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination, with parental consent, to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities. The initiative aims to protect adolescent girls against HPV infections that can cause cervical cancer.
The campaign has achieved nearly 87 per cent cumulative coverage against the identified annual target cohort of approximately 1.2 crore girls, based on the Registrar General of India (RGI) 2021 population estimates.
The Ministry said that reaching the one crore-dose milestone within nine months reflects the scale and momentum of the initiative, supported by coordinated efforts of States and Union Territories, healthcare professionals, frontline workers, teachers, parents and local communities.

Wells Fargo is set to enact an updated agreement with millions of customers, specifically about AI agents, starting on Tuesday. The bank’s warning to early adopters could not be clearer. “Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK,” read Wells Fargo’s new terms.
AI agents, which automate online tasks and click on your behalf, have stumbled through 2026. They remain nascent technology, but a growing subset of power users latched onto the personal bots this year. Sometimes these early adopters enjoyed the efficient help of automation, and other times they publicly embarrassed themselves when the AI agents made major mistakes, like posting bank details for everyone at work to see.
Builders of these AI tools often market agents as the ultimate tool for shopping decisions, whether that’s putting together a grocery order, finding accommodations for a vacation, or discovering specific holiday gifts for your parents. I’ve used an agent to help shop for a new couch, comparing options within a specific budget and tracking price drops.
Some users value these agents so much that they are oblivious to the overarching security concerns, pairing account credentials and granting permissions for the agents to take sweeping actions without forethought. Although the segment of online transactions completed by these autonomous tools remains minuscule, US-based banking institutions are already sick of third-party AI agents.
It’s not just banks; AI agents are igniting turf wars around the web. Amazon, one of the largest online retailers, blocked Meta’s Muse, one of the most widely used AI agents, from making purchases on its platform. Travel companies are also pushing back—United recently announced that personal bots would be blocked from purchasing flights on your behalf.
As the end of the year approaches, multiple banks have enacted new policies around agents or sent warnings. In late October, JPMorgan Chase changed its terms to ban third-party agents that log in with your credentials. That same day, Bank of America warned its customers not to share login info with agents. Along with the announced change coming from Wells Fargo, Citibank and PNC have also changed their terms to include warnings about agents.
The automation, which remains a central selling point of always-on agents, is exactly what may get users in trouble. “Consumers authorize goals, not every click,” says Kacy Kim, an associate professor of marketing at Bryant University who studies consumer behavior and emerging tech. While Kim expects some consumers to feel like it's unfair to be held accountable for their agent’s mistakes, she doesn’t expect these policy moves by financial institutions to scare off the early-adopter crowd already in deep and using the tools as part of everyday life.
Banks appear to be trying to get ahead of major issues, in case agentic tools stick around and don’t just disappear as another tech fad. “All of our data shows that most people don't even know what agents are, much less use them,” says Sucharita Kodali, a Forrester analyst who focuses on ecommerce and consumer behavior. She sees banks as fundamentally risk-averse, so taking proactive measures now makes sense, even if most agentic issues remain edge cases.
“The banks see risks with everything,” she says. “From the security of transactions to automated withdrawals that could happen to the detriment of account holders.”
Even though outliers exist, many users are aware of the risks and are only comfortable handing over so much control to an AI agent, and only for certain shopping tasks. “People are very comfortable with AI buying toilet paper,” says Luca Cian, a professor at the University of Virginia who studies consumer psychology and AI.
He sees consumers as increasingly comfortable turning to AI tools for shopping advice but often only automating boring buys, like household supplies. Shoppers are less comfortable automating away dynamic, big-ticket purchases that require additional care and discretion.
Cian gives a hypothetical scenario where a customer’s AI agent accidentally buys 10 roasted chickens from the supermarket. Who’s to blame? The retailer would likely argue that they completed a valid order that you placed. The AI builder may claim that they just provided the software, and even included disclaimers about potential mistakes. And now your bank is making it clear they don’t want to be held responsible either. Hope you need the protein, because it looks like you just bought 10 hot chickens.
Certain credit cards, though, are looking into limited protections for shoppers. Mainly, American Express announced that some agentic mistakes, like ordering too many of a certain item, may be eligible for reimbursement in the future through the card provider if you can't get your money back from the original retailer.
Banks are pumping out reasonable warnings about third-party agents, but don’t get it twisted. These banks are all-in on first-party tools. “Banks are doing two things at once,” Cian says. “They're locking the door to outside agents and building their own.” Users have interacted with Wells Fargo’s tool that answers questions using generative AI over a billion times. Bank of America revamped its new EricaAssist agent this year to help employees. Citigroup even launched an internal development platform specifically centered on agents.
Despite all the hype, Kodali remains skeptical about whether all of this hoopla is even necessary. “The issue with agents and shopping is that, first of all, it is not difficult to buy on Amazon or Walmart or anywhere else,” she says. “In most of those transactions, you don't need an agent.” Agentic shopping often seems to be a solution in search of a problem. Or at least an attempt by AI builders to find a way to earn affiliate revenue, eventually, from their software tools.
Whether AI agents grow in popularity for shopping automation or slowly fade into the digital graveyard, banks are already resolute on the matter. It’s your bot, and your problem.

California Democrat Rep. Gomez resigns following ethics report on sexual misconduct allegations
Rep. Jimmy Gomez, D-Calif., says he is resigning from Congress after a bipartisan investigation released Monday found "substantial evidence" he engaged in sexual misconduct toward a House staffer.
The House Ethics Committee concluded Gomez violated House rules by "making unwelcome sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct towards a House staffer and disregarding the power imbalance inherent in his relationship with House staffers."
The report also says the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.
Gomez has served in Congress since 2017 representing parts of Los Angeles. He lost reelection this fall to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres. California uses a system where the top two vote-getters no matter the party advance to the general election. Gomez says his resignation will be effective Dec. 1.
Lisa Banks and Sarah Nesbitt, attorneys for the unnamed House staffer, wrote in a statement that their client testified to the committee truthfully and at personal risk.
"She sacrificed her own sense of safety and privacy to help reveal the ongoing misogyny and debauchery that permeates Capitol Hill," Banks and Nesbitt wrote. "Representative Gomez seems to believe that the power he wields, both as a man and as a member of Congress, makes him untouchable. Today's findings are a meaningful step toward dismantling that belief."
In a statement announcing his plan to resign, Gomez wrote that he cooperated with the investigation, but has strong disagreements with the report and its conclusions.
"Among other significant deficiencies and omissions, the report does not include key portions of my testimony that are essential to a full and fair understanding of what occurred," he wrote.
"I also have serious concerns about the process. In my interview, I answered the Committee's questions only to see my statements selectively quoted, disparaged, and disregarded throughout the final report, to which I was given no opportunity to respond."
The House Ethics Committee, which includes five Democrats and five Republicans, opened its investigation into Gomez in August following a press report of Gomez kissing a staffer from another Congressional office at a party. Gomez denied those allegations.
The committee asked Gomez to disclose whether he "ever engaged in a romantic or sexual relationship or made sexual contact with a congressional staffer." Gomez disclosed interactions with two women — telling the committee the encounters were all consensual. Both women spoke to the committee.
One denied "she had ever had a nonconsensual sexual encounter" with Gomez. The other, described as Witness 1 in the report, said she had more than one encounter with Gomez and she did not consider them consensual.
She told investigators that Gomez made sexual contact without her consent at a bar in February 2024 and then was forceful with her and tried to kiss her at his congressional office in July 2024.
Gomez denied the interactions were nonconsensual. The staffer, described as Witness 1 in the committee report, eventually left her job on Capitol Hill.
"Here, the House lost Witness 1 as a competent and able staffer because of Representative Gomez's misconduct and because of a broader culture of disrespect and toxic sexual behavior toward staff that permeates life on the Hill and is long overdue for correction," the committee wrote.
The report comes amid a broader conversation about how Congress deals with the behavior of its members, especially when it comes to sexual misconduct.
In April, Democrat Eric Swalwell of California resigned his House seat amid allegations of sexual assault and misconduct. He also denied the allegations. Rep. Tony Gonzales (R-Tex.) also resigned from the House after admitting to an affair with a former staff member.
Rep. Chuck Edwards (R-N.C.) dropped his reelection bid earlier this year after the House Ethics Committee recommended he face a censure vote for allegedly harassing two young female staffers. Edwards denied the allegations.
Republican Reps. Max Miller of Ohio and Cory Mills of Florida also face House Ethics investigations stemming from allegations of domestic violence. Both deny wrongdoing.
Miller lost his reelection bid this fall and Mills lost his GOP primary.
Last week, the House Ethics Committee adopted new rules with the aim of speeding up investigations into sexual misconduct and improving transparency.

Just ask Japan's Ryo Hirakawa, who only last month achieved his "dream", external when he got behind the wheel of a Haas at the Mexican Grand Prix following Esteban Ocon's controversial departure from the team.
"I just need to taste this moment. I'm really happy," Hirakawa said after scoring a point - admittedly, following a few demotions for others. "Just enjoy this moment and see what we can do."
Within a week there was nothing the Toyota factory driver could do as Haas' 2027 driver Rafael Camara was drafted in for the American team early, for the rest of 2026.
Hirakawa is a reserve driver for Haas as a result of the team's association with Toyota - the Japanese being in the right place at the right time.
The percentage of F1 test and reserve drivers who make it to the grid is typically low, and those who do tend to be drafted in for one shot at very unlikely glory.
The days of the aristocrat who fancies a pootle around the track are gone, and years of preparation are required even to be standing in the pit garage.
Injuries, sponsorship fails and outright cheating are just some of the reasons why it does not work out for some hopefuls.
Needell, known better for his time behind the wheel on Top Gear and other auto TV shows, got his big break at the 1980 Belgian Grand Prix. But his journey to the paddock was initiated a few years earlier - in the media.
"I won a car in a magazine competition," he says. "I was the kid on the terraces, on the fences - and made it on to the grid. We had no money at all in our family, so I was a working civil engineer five days a week and a mechanic in my garage five nights a week. At the weekend I was the van driver, the mechanic and the racing driver.
"I bumbled my way up to the top of the national scene and then got offered a professional drive in Formula 3. And after two years of that I moved up into the [long since defunct] Formula 1 British championship.
"I was out at the Nurburgring trying to get an F1 drive when I got the call. I was hanging around the paddock trying to chat up an F2 team, trying to say I had a sponsor, which of course I didn't.
"Ensign called me and said: 'This weekend would you like to drive?' I rushed home from the Nurburgring in my orange Ford Capri, had half a day's test at Donington and on to qualifying for the Belgian GP at Zolder.
"I got my chance because Clay Regazzoni crashed and hurt his back at Long Beach.
"A lot of that in the olden days was due to injuries - chances would come up when someone had crashed and got injured. It was dangerous back then."
Needell was in, but this was old-school F1 where you had to pre-qualify to show you were fast enough to qualify for the Grand Prix itself.
"There was something like 30 drivers trying to pre-qualify, and somehow I made it to the back of the grid - 23rd in the Ensign. It was so much cheaper then - aluminium chassis and a Cosworth DFV engine and away you go."
While the back of the grid beckoned, a 29-year-old Needell was in very good company in the form of double world champion Emerson Fittipaldi, who was having a bad weekend in his Skol Fittipaldi car.
"I found myself on the back row of the grid, sitting by one of my big heroes. It was all a bit of a dream," says Needell.
In contrast to today's VIP treatment, Needell's parents and his girlfriend (now wife) drove to Belgium in the family car and watched from the crowd as he lined up on the grid.
"When the mechanics started the engine and left me sitting there - me and Emerson - I actually started humming the theme tune [to Fleetwood Mac's The Chain]," Needell says.
"For 12 laps I battled with Emerson for the honour of being last place at the 1980 Belgian Grand Prix. Then the engine broke."
A failed attempt to qualify for Monaco a week later put the brakes on his F1 dream and eventually resulted in Needell pursuing a career as a Le Mans racer and TV presenter.
Often the reason F1 careers could be so fleeting would be of a driver's own making.
Hans Heyer did not qualify for his one and only race - the 1977 German Grand Prix at Hockenheim - but he thought he would contest it anyway, starting from the pit lane for the ATS team in a car that was never supposed to be there.
The German may have achieved his dream at his home race, but it came with disqualification after he had already retired with gearbox failure on lap nine.
And what of Marco Apicella? It has taken 73 years, since Alberto Ascari triumphed, for Italy to celebrate one of its own F1 world champions in Kimi Antonelli as he secured the 2026 title in Mexico last month.
For a country and a Ferrari team so important to the sport, that is a long time to wait - and Apicella was a good example of why it may have taken a while.
Rushed in at the last minute after only two hours of testing to replace a disgruntled, if experienced, Thierry Boutsen in the underwhelming 1993 Jordan, Apicella lasted approximately 800 metres of his home race after a multi-car collision during the first lap of the Italian Grand Prix at Monza.
That was the end of Apicella's F1 career and he would end up embarking on five unsuccessful attempts to win Le Mans.
1 of 5
So what's the best any of the one-hit wonders have done in their first and only grand prix?
There have been a smattering of points finishes over the years, and Dorino Serafini's shared second place on the podium with legend Ascari at Monza in the final race of F1's maiden season is difficult to top for an F1 one-shot.
But Germany's Markus Winkelhock is surely up there as one of sport's super-sub icons of the modern era.
A last-minute replacement in the newly acquired, yet painfully slow, Spyker team's car at the 2007 European Grand Prix at the Nurburgring, the touring car driver took up the F1 super sub's favoured qualifying position on the grid: last place.
F1 ran in Winkelhock's family - father Manfred contested 56 grands prix in the eighties before his death from a crash during a sportscar race in 1985.
But Markus went one better than his uncle Jo, who never contested an F1 race despite trying to qualify seven times.
But, by his own admission, Winkelhock was a long way from ready. "I had one day testing in Silverstone and one day in Paul Ricard," Winkelhock told Motorsport magazine., external
"The first couple of laps it felt like a PlayStation - so unreal, everything was so fast. You're accelerating till you reach the braking point.
"But after all the [practice] sessions I could feel my neck already.
"I told my mechanics to put some beddings on the side of the headrest, in case the neck is completely done, to lean on with the helmet."
Then came some early rain from the Eifel mountains and an inspired decision from the pitwall of a team with very little to lose.
Winkelhock was on exactly the right tyres, at exactly the right time, as the rain came down, and Lewis Hamilton and Jenson Button slid helplessly into the gravel trap along with several others.
Winkelhock's orange Spyker simply danced through the rivers of rainwater flowing across the tarmac, sitting 33 seconds ahead of the field - a country mile for F1.
He said: "I didn't know it was for the lead. I was just driving. At the point they told me, 'You're P1'. I really didn't understand anything that was going on because this race was really crazy."
But when the rain stopped, so did Winklehock - first swallowed up by the faster cars on a drying track, and then by a hydraulic issue on lap 15, having led for six laps.
Make no mistake, a lost F1 career is very often a driver's glittering career in the making in sportscars at Le Mans, or on the ovals of American Indycar.
But even back in the day when other sporting codes, such as rallying's frighteningly fast Group B, were at the height of their popularity, F1 was the pinnacle for most.
"Being a grand prix driver was where you wanted to go," concludes Needell. "But I always had my eye sideways for any other drives.
"Single-seaters are the best cars to drive and they are made and designed to race. And the ultimate is the grand prix car. Everything else is second best.
"I was so proud I got there on no sponsorship and no money. I suppose I was a bit annoyed I couldn't stay for longer.
"But as I always say, 'unluckier than a few, but luckier than millions'."

Early in Shakespeare’s tragedy Julius Caesar, the title character is publicly offered a crown as a symbol of absolute power. Caesar refuses it three times, dramatically fainting after the final try. Scholars say that Caesar’s “falling sickness,” as his eventual assassin Brutus put it, masked his true intention to rule. His effort to win over the crowd with his humility only intensified the momentum to grant him more power. Indeed, after his refusal, his adherents became even more impassioned, setting the stage for his eventual claim to kingship. “If Caesar had stabb’d their mothers, they would have done no less,” said a Roman senator of the sycophantic crowd.
Jensen Huang was not so strategic. He did not even wait until a crown was offered before grabbing for it. On November 12, Nvidia’s cofounder had resigned from his post as CEO, promising to work to heal his family and earn back trust. The reasons were obvious. He had been engaging in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Under his leadership, billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia’s sales had gone to her formerly obscure company in Singapore, which, in a potential violation of export regulations, the company used to power Chinese AI efforts. In addition, he was carrying on an affair with an Nvidia subordinate (or was it two?), itself a fireable transgression. Nonetheless, because of his success in building Nvidia, Huang has been receiving a noisy groundswell of support from Silicon Valley and Wall Street, with the same loyalty as the crowd that would have idolized Caesar even if he’d stabbed their mothers.
Huang, used to exercising power, seemed as energized as the mob supporting Caesar had been. Social media was exploding with memes portraying him as a hero whose return would result in Homeric redemption. Silicon Valley leaders like Travis Kalanick, Tim Sweeney, and Elon Musk called his removal an injustice that must be addressed. One of Huang’s talents is moving fast. So perhaps he used state-of-the-art Rubin GPUs to dispatch an armada of AI introspection-bots, fast-tracking what formerly would have taken months of moral cleansing into a few days. In any case, on November 17, when the pixels on his resignation message had barely settled, he returned to X to announce that he would be honored to reclaim his position if offered.
It was not to be. Within hours, Nvidia’s board threw more water on Huang’s overture than a Texas data center consumes in a year. During a scheduled earnings call, chair Harvey Jones said, “The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation but does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.” Nvidia’s interim leader, Colette Kress, who had been its long-time CFO, ended the call with a devastating kicker: “We’ve got this.” Et tu, Colette?
The search for a replacement will proceed. But even after the board presumably closed the door, and Kress told employees in an all-hands meeting once again that “we got this,” the push to restore him has not quieted. The president of the United States hasn’t retracted his opinion that Huang should resume his post. A petition called “Stand With Jensen” now has over 200,000 signatures. Hedge funder Bill Ackman zinged out a hysterical X post this week charging “major governance failures by directors.” (Clearly, Ackman’s view of ideal governance is no governance.) Most alarmingly, Semafor has reported that Huang himself had spoken to at least one board member about his reinstatement and that several directors may still be open to the possibility. At press time, Huang has not given any public indication that he is no longer angling for a triumphant return.
At the New York Times DealBook conference, held a day after the earnings call, the Jensen affair dominated the discussion, even as Anthropic was readying the biggest IPO in history. On stage, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Greg Brockman expressed admiration for Huang but did not recommend his reinstatement. But Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey said that “nobody can take Jensen’s place in this critical juncture” because “his personal relations are the reason everyone is willing to do business” with Nvidia. Elon Musk reaffirmed his outrage that Huang had been forced out, saying it was like the Chicago Bulls firing Michael Jordan in his prime during a playoff hot streak. In my informal conversations during breaks, I found people on both sides of the divide. One person was a substantial Nvidia investor who showed me pictures of themselves with Huang. Like many with a financial stake in the company, this individual was eager to see Huang back in charge.
Everyone is in agreement that the Huang story is tragic. But the outcry for Huang’s reinstatement is a broader tragedy, revealing how greed has eclipsed ethics and patriotism. Those clamoring for reinstatement have one argument: that Huang’s leadership was so singular and superlative that he must keep his job. Not doing so would dishonor his previous efforts and degrade Nvidia’s future performance. Essentially, it’s an ends-justify-the-means rationale incompatible with corporate oversight and even fidelity to law and national security.
The push to reinstate Huang is also a grotesque extension of the cult of the founder, which assumes that those who built a company have unique abilities to run it and should be unconstrained in how they do so. (Serious question: If founders are so great, why do the vast majority of startups fail?)
There’s no question that Huang has built one of the greatest companies ever and delivered historic returns to shareholders. But one irony of the Bring Back Jensen Movement is that this crisis has exposed him, in some respects, as an erratic, even a lousy, CEO. His personal indiscretions cost shareholders almost a trillion dollars! He lied to his board. He pursued a strategy that seems to have violated the spirit if not the law of export regulations. He gave senior executive posts to family members who pursued a passion in the chip business later in life, including his daughter (trained as a chef), son (went to art school and owned a cocktail lounge), and son-in-law (former professional skier). In a public company, nepotism comes at shareholders’ expense.
On top of that, he failed in a critical duty of a CEO—preparing a succession plan. Nvidia has none, solely because Huang acted as if he would run it forever. At DealBook, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, after the obligatory expressions of empathy toward Huang, threw some shade on leaders who don’t plan for their departure: “People get old and die,” he said. “If a company will succeed, it needs someone to take over. I’ve never trusted a leader, founder or otherwise, who says the institution after I left was completely gone. Like, then what did you build?”
Finally, if Huang were so passionate about Nvidia’s future, why is he still angling for a return? The possibility, even a remote one, that he will be reinstated may discourage the best candidates from considering an offer to lead Nvidia. Huang would best serve Nvidia by shutting down the talk from his Silicon Valley cronies and demanding that the Bring Jensen Back petition be scrapped.
Ultimately, by giving up his quest to reclaim the crown, Huang would better serve not only Nvidia but himself. His energy should be devoted first to mending his family relations and then working with lawyers to maintain his reputation, fortune, and maybe even freedom. There’s an additional bonus to his departure. He will be leaving Nvidia at a peak for high-powered GPU chips and AI’s economic power. If the bubble does pop, Huang will avoid being the face of AI when the fall comes. Remember, things didn’t work out too well for Julius Caesar.

The Prince of Wales’s Earthshot prize will host its forthcoming annual awards ceremony at a venue owned by the billionaire Ambani family conglomerate, drawing criticism from conservationists over their fossil fuel businesses and their foundation’s controversial mega-zoo.
A spokesperson for the Earthshot prize, which awards £1m to five winners every year to invest in conservation work, confirmed to the Guardian and the news outlet Mongabay that this year’s ceremony will be held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai on 17 November.
The venue is part of Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, which also owns Jamnagar, the world’s biggest oil refinery in Gujarat on India’s western coast. The group’s philanthropic arm funds the 1,400-hectare (3,500-acre) private zoo Vantara, which was founded by Mukesh’s son Anant Ambani and inaugurated by the Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, last year. The zoo is embroiled in a long-running controversy over its vast collection of more than 150,000 animals, which reportedly includes some of the world’s most endangered species – from the radiated tortoise, native to Madagascar, to the Spix’s macaw, endemic to north-eastern Brazil but now considered extinct in the wild.
Megan Carr, of the Wildlife Animal Protection Forum South Africa (WAPFSA), warned that using a venue owned by Reliance “could lend an unearned environmental prestige to a corporate group currently under question by the global conservation community”.
Conservation groups, including WAPFSA, have raised concerns about the speed with which Vantara has amassed so many animals, and about how they were sourced. The site, near the family’s oil refinery, houses more than 2,000 species of animals.
This week, the 32-member committee that governs Cites, the UN-administered body that regulates trade in endangered species, requested that India submit another report on the steps it is taking to address concerns relating to its imports of protected species.
The committee also requested the Cites secretariat review 11 cases where there are unresolved questions over how animals were sent to Vantara.
Joanna Swift, the executive director of communications at the Earthshot prize, said it had not sought a philanthropic partnership for its award ceremony venue and that it was paying the standard commercial rate to rent the space.
“The [Jio World Convention Centre] was selected because it allowed us to host the event in Mumbai while meeting the practical requirements of an event of this size. It offers world-class facilities, technical infrastructure and experience of hosting major international events, including environmental ones,” Swift said. “In February this year, JWCC hosted the first ever Mumbai climate week.”
Vantara, Kensington Palace and JWCC have been approached for comment.
Vantara has previously denied allegations of wildlife trafficking and says its purpose is “to rescue wild animals in distress, provide treatment along with lifelong care, and rehabilitate those fit for the wild”.
“With regulatory approval, we also breed select endangered or extinct-in-the-wild species, serving as a modern Noah’s Ark to ensure their survival under human care and restore wild populations through reintroduction,” Vantara says on its website.
Last year, India’s supreme court cleared the zoo of allegations that animals had been acquired illegally or mistreated.
A later Cites fact-finding mission raised concerns about India’s compliance with international rules on animal imports in 2025. It recommended temporary restrictions on India, although the recommendation was later withdrawn.
Susan Cheyne, the vice-chair of the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s small apes section, said that Vantara’s model has not yet been shown to support conservation and “may be driving demand for wild animals in trade”.
“For gibbons and other primates, this matters a great deal. Moving animals out of their range countries into a private facility does nothing for wild populations unless there is a transparent, credible plan for those animals: for welfare, for any conservation breeding with clear goals, and for return to range states where that is possible. Real rescue and sanctuary work for primates is done by underfunded centres in range countries,” Cheyne said.
Daniela Freyer, co-founder of the German NGO Pro Wildlife, added: “Our planet is increasingly threatened by the overexploitation of wildlife and by climate change driven by fossil fuels. This week, the Cites Standing Committee, which oversees international wildlife trade, decided to keep India under its compliance procedure, as questions remain about the origin of some of the world’s rarest animals imported to Vantara. A prize whose goals include protecting nature and fixing our climate should be careful not to lend its reputation to these questions.”
Vantara had sought to lobby the UK, the chair of this week’s Cites meetings, attempting to persuade officials to take a more sympathetic view of India’s handling of imports to Vantara, the Guardian and Mongabay reported earlier this month. Ministers were advised not to engage formally with Vantara, internal documents revealed.
The Earthshot prize, founded by Prince William in 2020, is billed as the most prestigious environmental award. William appeared on the BBC’s Graham Norton show last month to promote the prize, saying it was designed to “talk about urgency and optimism together”.
Swift said that it was vital to host an edition of the Earthshot prize in India.
“Mumbai is the sixth largest city on earth. It is home to exceptional environmental solutions and the people behind them, with an impact felt in India and around the world. Spotlighting progress like this, to the largest possible audience, is why the Earthshot prize exists,” Swift said.

An 18-second-long video has been circulating on social media, which shows Sandeep Khirwar, Special Director General (SDG) of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), making a remark regarding the transportation of the bodies of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in a dumper truck.
In the viral clip, Khirwar can be heard saying, “All military trucks and vehicles in the area were occupied. So we had no choice but to transport the bodies of our two martyred SPO personnel in a dumper truck. But the real issue is not whether they were transported in a dumper or a garbage truck. Their families received the bodies of their loved ones. What more could they possibly want?”
X user @cutegirlindia21 shared this video and wrote, “Kashmir Police Chief has stated that the bodies of 2 martyred Kishtwar Police officers had to be transported in a garbage truck. The bodies were placed alongside garbage after the Indian Army refused to provide an ambulance to the Kashmir Police.”
🛑 Heartbreaking 💔 😢
Kashmir Police Chief has stated that the bodies of 2 martyred @KishtwarPolice officers had to be transported in a #garbage truck. The bodies were placed alongside garbage after the #IndianArmy refused to provide an ambulance to the Kashmir Police. https://t.co/Jm9i7bScN0
— A N U S H I ❤️T I W A R I🇮🇳 (@cutegirlindia21) November 16, 2026
According to an NDTV report published on November 14, the bodies of SPOs Bobby Chand and Rashpal Kumar — who lost their lives in a recent terror attack in the Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir — were transported to their native village Kiyar in a dumper truck without coffins. This incident sparked significant outrage among locals, with many questioning the manner in which the bodies were transported.
Against this backdrop, the purported video of SDG Sandeep Khirwar began to circulate. Several other users on X, including @RedDeFactoIND, @NetaNamax, and @unknownnewss, also shared the video with similar claims.
The video is also circulating on Facebook with similar assertions.
Fact Check
To determine the authenticity of the viral clip, Alt News used relevant keywords to search for information regarding statements made by Khirwar. We did not find any credible news reports or official statements that substantiate the claims made in the viral clip.
We observed that the viral video bears an ANI logo. Performing a ‘reverse image search’ using keyframes from the clip, we found the original video, which was posted by ANI on its official X account on November 16, 2026. In the video, Sandeep Khirwar, SDG of the CRPF’s Jammu & Kashmir Zone, is seen speaking to the media in Srinagar regarding the deaths of two SPOs in Kishtwar.
#WATCH | Srinagar, J&K: On the mortal remains of two missing SPOs recovered in Kishtwar, SDG, CRPF J&K Zone, Sandeep Khirwar says, “Every loss of life to any jawan in the security forces is a huge loss to all of us… We stand with their families, and we will make sure that they get justice.”
— ANI (@ANI) November 16, 2026
While the visuals of the video matches, the audio is different. In the original footage, Khirwar states: “All I can say is that, every loss of life to any Jawan, of any security forces are huge loss to all of us and we owe our utmost respect to all the fallen. And we stand with their family. We will make sure that they get justice, the families get justice.” He does not make any mention of the bodies being transported in a dumper truck, nor did he claim that the families were ‘grateful’ upon the recovery of the bodies.
Further, we found that the Khirwar’s voice and manner of speaking in the viral clip does not match the way he is heard speaking in the ANI footage, indicating that the original audio has been digitally altered or manipulated. We ran the viral clip through AI-detection Hive Moderation, which revealed that it is 98.9% likely to contain AI-generated speech.
On November 17, the official X handle of the CRPF’s Srinagar Sector addressed the viral claim. They stated that the video had been digitally tampered with and that false statements had been attributed to Sandeep Khirwar, clarifying that no such statements were made by him.
This claim is false and misleading. The video was digitally manipulated, with fabricated remarks attributed to CRPF Special DG Sh. Sandeep Khirwar, who is not the Kashmir Police Chief. The original footage contained no such statement. This is an attempt to spread misinformation and create an anti-India narrative.
— Srinagar Sector CRPF 🇮🇳 (@crpf_srinagar) November 17, 2026
Thus, the viral clip has been digitally manipulated using AI, falsely attributing statements about the transportation of SPOs’ bodies in a dumper truck to Sandeep Khirwar. The original footage by ANI does not carry any such comment.
Sajahan Ali is an intern at Alt News.

Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
Nearly 72,000 people have been evacuated from areas of Odisha in eastern India as Tropical Cyclone Akvan approaches land. Akvan is expected to make landfall on Friday between Narsapur and Puri, prompting cyclone warnings from the India Meteorological Department for north Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and south Odisha coasts. Peak wind gusts are expected to reach 70mph, with rainfall totals through Friday and Saturday potentially exceeding 200mm for northern coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
Following a Yellow Level 2 severe thunderstorm warning by the South African Weather Service on Tuesday, torrential rainfall and large hail were reported across parts of Johannesburg. The storms triggered flash flooding and caused infrastructure damage in the township of Soweto. One person died, while another remains missing after the severe storms.

A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta has killed three people with 36 remaining missing, an Indonesian rescue official says.
Drone footage showed large parts of the factory destroyed, with the roof collapsed in places and smoke still rising from the complex. Photos and videos shared by rescuers show officers entering the charred building in search of the missing victims on Sunday, with small fires still burning in some spots.
Relatives of the missing victims flocked near the factory’s entrance, seeking updates about their loved ones, footage aired by local broadcasters showed.
The Fonusa Agung Mulia factory, located in Cikande in Indonesia’s Banten province about 50km from the capital, caught fire on Saturday afternoon, search and rescue official Rizky Dwianto said on Sunday.
“All elements of the joint SAR [search-and-rescue] team are making maximum effort to locate the victims while prioritising the safety of personnel in the field,” he added.
Rizky said four people were injured and taken to a nearby hospital and health clinic.
Firefighters were alerted about 4.30pm on Saturday and found the building already engulfed in flames when they arrived, fire official Tubagus Machfudz told local broadcaster Kompas TV.
“When we arrived … a large area was already on fire. So we could not determine whether the company’s protection system was functioning properly or not,” he said.
The Banten province governor Andra Soni told reporters overnight that an estimated 60 people were inside the factory when it caught fire.
The cause of the incident is still under investigation, the local disaster agency said in an Instagram post on Sunday.
Deadly fires are not uncommon in Indonesia.
In December last year, a blaze that was likely caused by a drone battery explosion tore through a seven-storey building in Jakarta and killed at least 22 people, police said.
In 2023, at least 13 people were killed in the country’s east after an explosion at a nickel-processing plant.

Industry body Bharat Web3 Association (BWA) has submitted its recommendations to the finance ministry ahead of the upcoming Union Budget 2027. It has sought a fairer taxation framework and greater regulatory certainty for the Indian cryptocurrency sector. “The BWA submission focused on the need for a fair, balanced and effective taxation framework that encourages compliance, strengthens investor protection, enhances tax revenues and supports the growth of India’s domestic Web3 ecosystem,” said the industry body in a post on X. BWA urged the ministry to consider the following recommendations for the Indian virtual digital asset (VDA) sector while drafting Budget 2027: Level the playing field by clarifying and strengthening the applicability of Indian tax provisions, particularly TDS obligations, to offshore VDA platforms serving Indian users Reconsider the existing 1% TDS, permit set-off and carry-forward of losses, and review the 30% tax rate (on profits from sale of cryptos) to encourage greater user participation Improve the enforcement of registration and reporting obligations Ensure offshore entities serving Indian users are subject to appropriate Indian legal and regulatory requirements Provide regulatory clarity for FIU-registered crypto exchanges, which seek access to global liquidity through offshore exchanges BWA also noted that clear and consistent guidelines for cryptocurrencies would provide much-needed certainty to compliant Indian platforms and strengthen the domestic ecosystem. “A framework that encourages activity within compliant Indian platforms can strengthen oversight, improve tax compliance and support innovation and investment in India,” added BWA. This comes as the Indian cryptocurrency sector has been constantly appealing to the Centre to reduce the TDS on VDAs for the last four years. They have also been seeking tax breaks for the development of blockchain security infrastructure as well as tax holidays for early-stage Web3 platforms. However, the finance ministry has largely unheeded these demands and has opted for a heavy-taxation approach towards crypto platforms. Meanwhile, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) remains a steadfast opponent of digital currencies. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra last year even said that cryptocurrencies could potentially affect the country’s financial stability. A Parliamentary standing committee on finance recently also termed the asset class as “high risk” citing rampant money laundering, trafficking, radicalisation and suspicious crypto transactions. The recommendations also come as the Indian crypto ecosystem continues to be under strain. Over the past few months, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has also intensified scrutiny of crypto-related financial flows and raided multiple crypto exchanges over alleged unauthorised cross-border transactions. Making matters worse has been the recent spate of delays and disruptions in withdrawals at major crypto exchanges including Coinbase India, CoinDCX and Zebpay. While the three platforms have cited issues at banking partners for the disruption, industry insiders pointed to heightened scrutiny of intermediaries handling crypto-related financial flows as a possible source of pressure on banking and liquidity arrangements. As if this was not enough, many crypto platforms have been hit by data breaches and hacks amid a surge in AI-assisted cyberattacks.

Kyiv – President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.
The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its strikes against Russia far from the front lines.
But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts.”
“It all took place off the coast of Libya. Our warriors deployed seven Ukrainian-made naval drones. Despite all the enemy’s efforts to counter the attack, the Russian corvette Merkury was sunk,” Zelenskyy wrote on X.
The Ukrainian leader claimed the Merkury was “one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war.”
“Our second target was the Russian dry cargo vessel MV ANGARA, which the enemy used to transport weapons. Result: target hit,” he added.
A Ka-27 combat helicopter was also destroyed in the strike on the Merkury, Zelenskyy said.
Sunday’s strikes came after a drone hit a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea on Saturday, close to the waters of Finland, whose border guard said the strike was Ukrainian.
The U.N. mission in Libya expressed “serious concern” over the attacks, calling for “an immediate, independent and transparent investigation.”
“Libya cannot afford, and must not become a battleground for foreign conflicts,” the UNSMIL wrote on X.
In March, a Russian liquefied natural gas carrier sank off the Libyan coast following an attack, which Russian President Vladimir Putin blamed on Ukraine.
The vessel was part of what is known as Russia’s “shadow fleet” of tankers that carry its oil and gas around the world, skirting Western restrictions.
Ukraine has at times admitted to attacking Moscow’s shadow fleet, including in the Mediterranean last December.
The Tripoli government said it rejected any attempt to turn Libya into “an arena for international conflicts” and the use of its territory “for any military or logistical activities that could jeopardize” national security or sovereignty.
Libya has been beset by violence and instability since the overthrow of longtime ruler Moammar Gadhafi in 2011.
It remains divided between the government in Tripoli led by Prime Minister Abdulhamid Dbeibah and a rival administration in the east backed by military commander Khalifa Haftar.

Team science — or collaborative science across disciplines and institutions — is essential for scientific progress as modern problems are too complex for a single person, laboratory, or even field to solve alone. Some of the best work happens when scientists from different countries collaborate.
However, U.S. policies in place and in development increasingly curtail this vital foreign collaboration. There are foreign funding restrictions, visa and entry restrictions for researchers, mandatory institutional compliance and audits with respect to foreign collaborations, and tight export controls. These policies were implemented as biosecurity measures to protect from “countries of concern,” including China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.
Meanwhile, proprietary scientific research is easily accessible to anyone, including foreign actors, through a policy meant to protect Americans’ right to government information. In other words, we are locking the front door while the back window is still wide open.
How does this happen?
The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) is a U.S. federal law enacted in 1966 in response to concerns that the government was too broad and unaccountable. FOIA gives anyone the right to request access to records held by federal government agencies.
This means that through FOIA, anyone — U.S. citizens, noncitizens, and foreign nationals — can access U.S. government-funded science by completing a simple online form and paying a minimal fee. While FOIA is an incredibly important tool for citizens in a free society, it was never intended to allow anyone around the globe to access proprietary U.S. science.
People are readily climbing in through the open back window. As a scientist in the U.S., I personally experienced the impact of such a FOIA request. I was notified by a FOIA coordinator at an NIH institute that my scientific ideas, supported by a funded grant from the U.S. government, were being requested by a Chinese entity through a simple online request form. They only had to pay a $25 fee.
By law, I had to comply and release the grant to them. The requester was listed as a “Consultant” and identified by a generic email address and physical address in China that could not be verified.
I am not the only one to have this experience. The FOIA coordinator told me offhand that this specific individual had a track record of requesting numerous grants from different NIH institutes every year. More broadly, over a decade, the NIH received more than 13,300 requests for grant proposals through FOIA. (Meanwhile, journalists’ FOIA requests often face major delays and other hurdles.)
This loophole has significant negative ramifications on our society. Scientific grants contain unpublished scientific data and sensitive intellectual property. The release of this material could:
1) harm personal and institutional financial interests by divulging patentable ideas, product concepts, and precompetitive information;
2) mislead the public through exposure to unvetted and untested hypotheses and preliminary data;
3) ruin careers and livelihoods of U.S. scientists; and perhaps most importantly,
4) damage U.S. interests by allowing foreign nationals or foreign corporations to be the primary beneficiaries of work funded by the U.S. taxpayer.
Our policies are fundamentally not aligned to protect science. We say we are blocking competing foreign interests, yet through FOIA, anyone can access this science.
If the U.S. truly wants to protect science, Congress needs to close the open window that FOIA affords. Proprietary U.S. science should be exempt or excluded from FOIA. Failing that, those who can access our material must be scrutinized.
Almost exactly four years after receiving the FOIA request, a research team from China published findings that closely matched my team’s original hypothesis — one our own later experiments did not support. While I cannot say whether the FOIA request, my grant, and this recent publication are related, the timing has made me think more about how research, including my own, is ultimately used in these situations.
Francesca E. Duncan, Ph.D. is the Thomas J. Watkins memorial professor of reproductive science in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology in the Feinberg School of Medicine at Northwestern University. She is also an associate professor in residence at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging. The views presented here are her own.

At midnight on Thursday, when Grand Theft Auto VI finally launched, India was just another market waiting to play the game. But it was not long before the game became a vital part of the week’s spectacle. Popular YouTubers Carry Minati and Mythpat streamed GTA VI for nearly 10 hours each drawing over 13 Mn views apiece by Thursday afternoon. Gaming cafes, which typically see footfalls on weekends, remained open 24/7 as fans queued up to log their first minutes on GTA after 13 long years. Even Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a few ministers from the union cabinet joined the conversation around the game on social media platforms. For a country where gaming has largely been synonymous with smartphones, free-to-play titles and real-money gaming (RMG), the frenzy around a console-first AAA game was telling. It indicates that India’s gaming audience is increasingly looking beyond casual mobile gaming, with AA games becoming a cultural marker. There is another reason why GTA VI’s launch should matter to India. It is reported that over 1,600 developers at Rockstar Games’ Bengaluru studio contributed to the making of the game, which is more than 25% of the development team. In other words, Indian developers were a vital part of one of the world’s most ambitious gaming productions this century. India can help build GTA VI, so why can’t an Indian company build its own GTA? Despite a massive player base, a growing pool of developers and gaming focused investors such as Lumikai, India has yet to produce an original AAA gaming franchise with a comparable global footprint. “India has proved it can help build the world's biggest games. The next challenge is building games the world wants to play, with the IP owned in India,” says Shruti Verma, CEO of the Game Developers Association of India (GDAI) A number of companies, including the likes of Mayhem Studios and LightFury Games had raised expectations around India’s premium gaming ambitions, while Tara Gaming Limited is another venture pursuing the opportunity. Yet, the journey from announcing an ambitious project to shipping a commercially successful global title remains a difficult one. So, what exactly is holding India back? The first assumption that needs to be challenged is that India lacks the talent to build sophisticated games. The Talent Is Here. But Who Owns The Game? Industry stakeholders argue that Indian developers have already demonstrated their capabilities through work on global productions. The bigger problem is that much of this expertise has been built within overseas studios, production pipelines and intellectual properties. Anurag Choudhary, founder and CEO of Felicity Games, believes Indian developers have spent years building expertise but working on the creative vision set by companies in the US and Europe. “Most Indian developers have built deep craft inside someone else’s vision and pipeline. Very few have owned the creative and commercial risk of an original title end to end,” he says. Building assets, environments and technical components for an established franchise such as GTA is different from conceptualising a one-off game. Even though both involve developing characters and narrative, building its world, managing production and taking the final product to international audiences. The former is still the domain of the West. India has built capabilities in engineering, art, animation and co-development. What remains relatively scarce is experienced game directors, executive producers, narrative designers and production leaders who have taken original games from concept to commercial release. This is the key difference between the AAA gaming industry and the Indian gaming studios. The Dentsu-IWMBuzz India Gaming Report 2026 also identifies this gap. Its Gaming Industry Readiness Barometer places Product & Studio Capability at the Developing stage, while IP & Creative Distinctiveness and Global Readiness remain at the Building stage. What this says is that India has demonstrated that it can make games, but it is yet to establish that it can consistently create, own and scale globally successful gaming franchises. The Money Problem: AAA Games Don’t The VC Funding Playbook If talent is not the primary constraint, is capital the missing piece of the puzzle? By all accounts AAA game development involves years of production, specialised teams and substantial upfront investment, with commercial returns often arriving only after launch. This makes it a difficult proposition for investors accustomed to quicker feedback loops. For instance, mobile free-to-play games can generate retention and monetisation data within weeks of a soft launch. Developers can then decide whether to improve, discontinue or scale a product. A premium console title, on the other hand, could take five or more years to reach the market, making it a significantly longer and riskier bet. As per reports, estimated budgets for the GTA series jumped from roughly $100 Mn for Grand Theft Auto IV, which was released in 2008, to $265 Mn for the next edition launched in 2013, and $1 Bn–$2 Bn for GTA VI which came 13 years after GTA V. That shows that not only do budgets grow but the time between new launches is also longer because each iteration requires much more work to become more successful than the previous version. Investors aren’t being irrational, says Felicity Games’ Choudhary, explaining that premium PC and console games struggle to attract capital compared with mobile F2P titles because of the reality of the Indian market and the VC playbooks. He adds that most venture capital funds have eight-to-10-year fund lives and need to demonstrate progress well before a AAA game reaches commercial release. Consequently, such projects need publishers, strategic investors and larger pools of patient capital. Nitish Mittersain, founder and non-executive director of Nazara Technologies, believes the funding and team-building challenges have persisted in India for years. Pointing to the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA VI, he says building such large games requires substantial budgets and long gestation periods. He also highlights the quality and scale of teams required to sustain such productions. However, the growing involvement of Indian developers in global franchises could help bridge this gap over time. Funcell Games’ Abhishek Malpani believes India needs to address the problem much earlier in the development cycle. “If a small studio struggles to fund a mobile-game prototype, how will it fund a AAA game?” he asks. Specialist funds such as Lumikai, Bitkraft have helped build interest in gaming as an investible sector, but a lot of this has died down after the ban on RMG. No one is even thinking of investing hundreds of millions of dollars in a studio that wants to attempt an AAA title. Having said that, founders and investors believe venture capital alone cannot finance the next generation of ambitious gaming IPs. They say it’s not about talent or capital, but something else, which is an even bigger problem to solve, as we will see. India’s 550 Mn Gamers Are Not AAA Players Is India even the right market for AAA titles? Can Indian studios actually tap into the cultural consciousness of Western audiences while building from India? Within the bubble of the gaming community, India seems like a major market, but it is not a market that has shown consistent growth and high spending as the US, other parts of Asia or Europe. Average revenue per user in India is estimated to be around $3 compared to around $221 for the US and $237 for Japan, this despite India having over 400 Mn estimated gamers compared to around 225 Mn in the US. So India does not have enough paying capacity to support premium gaming. The October 2026 Dentsu-IWMBuzz report estimates that India had 535 Mn people who played pure-play games over the past 12 months. Of these, 332 Mn played in the past three months, while 109 Mn were paying gamers. But this large audience does not automatically translate into a viable domestic market for expensive PC and console titles. BSE-listed Nazara’s Mittersain believes the relatively small home market has historically been another barrier for Indian studios. In larger gaming markets, local developers can build products for domestic audiences, specific cultural contexts, monetise them and gradually scale. India, he argues, has been a difficult market to monetise relative to this and only mass games make money here. Competing directly in markets such as the US becomes even more difficult without an established global publishing and distribution network. For Indian studios, therefore, the answer could lie in building for global audiences rather than depending on domestic sales. But this is not easy. "I would definitely build for a global audience. That's our approach at Funcell too. India has a huge number of players, but downloads and revenue are very different things," Malpani says. Other founders say that it’s not just about building the game for international audiences, but the economic model of a true AAA title must work globally from day one. This means weighing paid games vs free-to-play models. Will AI Change The Game? India’s biggest mistake will be to measure its gaming ambitions against the scale of Rockstar’s latest blockbuster. This is not an attempt to say that a GTA will never come from India, but understanding where the ecosystem lies. Industry stakeholders believe the country needs to build its way up, starting with commercially successful indie and AA games, developing original IPs and creating studios capable of launching titles repeatedly. We are just getting started on these. Verma argues that India need not begin with $200 Mn productions like GTA or Red Dead Redemption. Successful AA games can establish the commercial track record, revenue and IP value needed to attract larger investments. India’s first globally recognised gaming franchise could very well emerge from mobile or a well-executed AA title before eventually expanding into something bigger. But there could be another variable that changes the equation: AI. Mittersain believes AI will bring down development timelines and costs while helping bridge knowledge gaps within Indian studios. He also points to a growing number of Indian studios developing games for PC and console, suggesting that interest in premium gaming is expanding beyond mobile. He is hopeful that the next three to five years could see more Indian gaming breakouts, even if they do not initially match the scale of GTA. That optimism, however, will need to be backed by patient capital, experienced production leaders, global publishing partnerships and the ability to retain learning from one game to the next. Ultimately, GTA VI’s India connection is a validation and reminder. The talent in India has demonstrated that they contribute to the world’s biggest gaming productions. What remains to be seen is whether the other pieces also fall into place. Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam Creatives: Abhyam Gusai
