Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang returned to the company's headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on Monday, receiving a loud ovation from employees after its board unanimously reinstated him as president and chief executive.
“Thank you all for the second chance. I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around,” Huang was heard telling employees in a video shared on social media by Ming-Yu Liu, Nvidia's vice president of research.
His return followed a dramatic turnaround at the chipmaker firm earlier this month. Huang had stepped down amid reports about his alleged extramarital affairs, including two involving Nvidia employees and another with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The allegations remain under scrutiny, and the company is conducting an independent investigation into his reported relationship with Alice Huang.
In announcing his reinstatement, Nvidia's board said it was satisfied with Huang's “candor” on the matter and that his return “poses no national security risk”, citing input from senior US government officials.
“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” board chair Harvey Jones said.
“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company,” he added.
Huang said he was “honored” to return and lead “one of the most consequential technology companies in the world”.
Trump claims credit for Huang's return
US President Donald Trump said he had intervened to secure Huang's reinstatement, claiming he had convinced Nvidia's board to bring the co-founder back. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way,” Trump told CNBC on Monday. “And I convinced them. I made the deal.”
Huang has been an ally of Trump and previously lobbied his administration to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced H200 chips to China.
Nvidia shares surge
Huang's return coincided with a sharp rally in Nvidia shares and the broader US stock market. Nvidia stock jumped 31.48% on Monday, its biggest one-day gain since 2003 and its third-best session on record. The surge added $952 billion to the company's market value in a single day.
The stock climbed as much as 36.6% before paring gains. The announcement helped fuel a wider technology-led rally, with the Nasdaq Composite rising 6.51% and the S&P 500 gaining 4.73%. Both indexes recorded their biggest single-session gains since April 2025.

Nvidia shares jump over 30%, log biggest single-day gain since 2003 as CEO Huang returns
Senate hearing ahead
Huang's return does not end scrutiny of the company. Senate Banking Committee chairman Tim Scott said the Nvidia chief would testify before the panel on December 3, amid continuing questions around national security and the company's dealings involving China.

World chess champion Gukesh Dommaraju insisted he was approaching his first title defense with the mindset of a challenger on Sunday as he and Javokhir Sindarov faced the media ahead of their historic showdown in Geneva, the youngest matchup in the 140-year history of the sport’s most coveted title.
The two 20-year-old grandmasters appeared side by side at the United Nations’ European headquarters in Geneva, where they struck a respectful tone before their best-of-14-games encounter begins on Tuesday at the Fondation Martin Bodmer in Cologny, the affluent suburb overlooking Lake Geneva.
Pressed on whether defending a world championship was more difficult than winning it the first time, Gukesh politely rejected the premise.
“I don’t think I’m here to defend anything,” the Indian said. “I’m here to win it all over again. That’s the mindset I’m in.”
Sindarov, the fast-rising Uzbek challenger roughly six months older than Gukesh who enters the match as the oddsmakers’ favorite despite being a relative newcomer to the game’s highest level, was similarly reluctant to dole out predictions. Asked to assess his chances of becoming world champion, he put them at a diplomatic 50%.
“It’s a hard match and 14 games,” Sindarov said. “Everything can happen.”
The contest brings together two players whose careers have traced sharply divergent trajectories since Gukesh became the 18th and youngest ever undisputed champion in December 2024.
The Chennai native, who was only 18 when he defeated China’s Ding Liren to shatter the age record previously held by Garry Kasparov, has struggled badly for form since reaching the summit. After climbing to a career-high No 3 in the world that month, he has plummeted to No 26 following an extended string of underwhelming performances, making him the lowest-ranked reigning world champion since Elo ratings were introduced in 1971.
Sindarov, meanwhile, has surged from No 25 a year ago to a career-best No 4 after a breakthrough 12-month stretch that included winning the Fide World Cup in Goa last November and an unbeaten masterclass at this year’s Candidates Tournament in Cyprus, where he finished with six wins and eight draws against a stacked field including Fabiano Caruana, Hikaru Nakamura and Anish Giri to earn a shot at Gukesh’s title.
The 22-place gap between them is the widest of any world championship matchup since the title was reunified in 2006. Sindarov also holds a 2½-½ advantage in their three previous classical meetings, with two wins and one draw.
Yet both men played down the significance of past results on Sunday.
“Whatever has happened till now, I think just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1,” Gukesh said. “It’s a completely different match, completely different opponent and different place.”
He acknowledged Sindarov’s sustained run of success, describing the Tashkent-born challenger as one of the world’s strongest players and predicting a formidable assignment.
“Sindarov has just been in very consistent and very good form,” Gukesh said. “It’s for sure going to be a real test.”
Sindarov was equally complimentary about the champion, pointing to his extraordinary performances in winning the title as evidence that his recent difficulties should not be overinterpreted.
“Gukesh’s performance in 2024 is something fantastic,” Sindarov said, adding that he had experienced the Indian’s strength firsthand in January when they played to a 78-move draw at the prestigious Tata Steel tournament in Wijk aan Zee. “Sometimes you have some bad periods.”
The two players also revealed contrasting approaches to preparing for the championship. While Gukesh deliberately pared back his tournament schedule this year, Sindarov continued regularly entering competitions against elite opposition, reasoning that he needed more experience at the highest level.
Sindarov added that he had accepted an invitation to the four-month Grand Chess Tour circuit before winning the Candidates and saw little reason to withdraw afterward.
“Even after I won Candidates, I wanted to have more experience because I didn’t play that many strong tournaments in my career,” he said. “I’m happy with my decision.”
Gukesh said the strategy had not surprised him or his team, who expected the challenger to take advantage of his momentum and accumulate experience against the world’s strongest players. The trade-off was that Sindarov’s busy slate also gave Gukesh and his team a wealth of recent games to study for clues about the challenger’s approach.
The preparations have also given Sindarov an appreciation for the peculiar demands of a world title match. He once found it difficult to believe that players could spend three or four months preparing to face a single opponent. Now, having devoted much of the past six months to the task himself, he wonders whether even that is enough.
“I was thinking six months is enough time,” he said. “But maybe even this six months ... is also maybe not enough to prepare for such a hard tournament.”
The Indian, by contrast, can draw on his experience in the pressure-cooker environment of the world championship stage, where the psychological and physical demands of facing the same opponent for weeks on end can be as punishing as the chess itself. Gukesh said he had been surfing, running and spending time outdoors, while Sindarov has taken up padel, playing regularly during his training camp.
“If I would be, like, 30, 40, maybe it will be tough,” Sindarov said. “But because I’m young, I think it’ll be not very hard, like, physically.”
Gukesh will again work with Polish grandmaster Grzegorz Gajewski, who helped guide his successful 2024 campaign, as well as South African mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton, who was part of the backroom staff for India’s cricket team when they won the 2011 World Cup and the Indian men’s hockey team when they claimed bronze at the Paris Olympics in 2024. Sindarov revealed he is working with Ukrainian coach Roman Vidonyak, although neither player has publicly disclosed the full composition of his team of seconds, the trusted advisers responsible for preparing openings and analyzing the opponent.
The match will be staged at the Fondation Martin Bodmer, a museum and research library housing rare manuscripts and books, including a Gutenberg Bible, a Shakespeare First Folio and a first edition of Isaac Newton’s Principia. Both players inspected the playing hall on Saturday ahead of Monday’s technical meeting.
Unlike most recent world championship tilts, the players will not compete inside a purpose-built soundproof enclosure. Fide has abandoned the familiar transparent cube in order to preserve the atmosphere of the historic venue, relying instead on enhanced security measures and strict limits on the number of spectators and media admitted to the playing hall.
Sindarov admitted that he had expected to play inside the traditional fishbowl, but was impressed by the stage. “The playing hall is really very beautiful,” he said. Gukesh, meanwhile, said he had checked the chairs, lighting and even the floor to ensure he would be comfortable during games that could last four or five hours – and occasionally even longer. As for the rare books surrounding the board, the champion admitted he had barely looked at them. “I don’t think I’ll be reading in between the games,” he joked.
The glass enclosure, designed to shield players from distractions, was first used during Garry Kasparov’s 1995 title defense against Viswanathan Anand at New York’s World Trade Center and has featured in numerous subsequent championships, including Gukesh’s victory over Ding in Singapore two years ago. Sindarov admitted the setting would take some getting used to, having never played a tournament in which there was nobody else competing nearby.
The match carries a $2.5m (£1.9m) prize fund, with $200,000 awarded for each decisive game and the remainder divided equally between the players. Sindarov will open with the white pieces on Tuesday after the drawing of lots at Sunday’s opening ceremony, with the players alternating colors throughout the match. The first to reach seven and a half points will be crowned champion, with rapid and blitz tiebreaks scheduled if the contest finishes level after 14 games. Three of the past five world title matches have been deadlocked after the classical portion and required tiebreaks: 2016, 2018 and 2023.
The winner will join or continue a centuries-spanning lineage stretching back to Wilhelm Steinitz, who became the first official world champion in 1886. Gukesh is seeking to retain the crown he won as a teenager, while Sindarov is attempting to become the first player from Uzbekistan to capture the title.
For now, neither is allowing himself to dwell too much on what victory might mean.
Sindarov, who will turn 21 on 8 December, the scheduled date of Game 12, said he had made no pledges or wagers about how he might celebrate winning the championship.
“I really want to focus on my next 20 days and try to play my best chess,” he said. “Then we’ll see.”
Gukesh, who celebrated his 2024 triumph by fulfilling a promise to go bungee jumping, was more cryptic when asked whether he had another stunt up his sleeve.
“I have a couple of things in mind,” he said, smiling. “I think you’ll get to know in time, maybe.”

Satellite images showed a Russian Navy corvette named Merkury was sunk during the operation, with only its bow still visible above the water.
Zelensky said a Russian combat helicopter was also destroyed when the Merkury sank, and that the other target of the attack was a Russian dry cargo vessel called MV Angara, which suffered damage.
The UN mission in Libya expressed alarm at the attacks, expressing its “grave concern” and stressing that Libya “should not be allowed to become an arena for external conflicts”.
The government also condemned the attack as a violation of the country's sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety and warned that it would take legal and diplomatic measures against anyone found responsible.
Meanwhile, Zelensky also confirmed that a seven-year-old boy had been pulled alive from the rubble 14 hours after a Russian airstrike flattened a residential building in the Ukrainian city of Dymer, killing at least 11 people. Searches for more survivors continued on Monday, he said.

Zelensky says Ukraine carried out 'exemplary' strikes in Libyan port
Volodymyr Zelensky has given the first confirmation that Ukraine targeted vessels in Libya's Benghazi port on Sunday, identifying the targets as a Russian corvette warship called Merkury and a Russian dry cargo vessel called MV Angara.
Zelensky said the strikes involved Ukrainian-made naval drones and called it "an exemplary Ukrainian operation".
He said the Merkury, which sank following the attack, was "one of their newest ships, commissioned in 2023, during the full-scale war", and that a combat helicopter was also destroyed.
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia’s aggression," he wrote on X.
Russia and Ukraine exchange fresh strikes overnight
Russian forces struck energy facilities and infrastructure in the Ukrainian port city of Izmail overnight, the Russian defence ministry said on Monday.
Russia also struck a vessel near Odesa, the ministry said, claiming it was carrying military cargo. Those claims could not be immediately verified.
Meanwhile, the governor of Russia's Perm region said that an industrial site in the Urals province had been damaged in a Ukrainian drone attack.
Dmitry Makhonin did not name the facility that had been struck in his statement on the Telegram messaging app this morning.
Death toll in Russian attack on Dymer rises to 11
The death toll from an attack by Russia on the Ukrainian town of Dymer overnight into Sunday has risen to 11, according to local officials.
Regional governor Tymur Tkachenko said the toll rose on Monday after another body was pulled from the rubble of a residential building.
It comes after Volodymyr Zelensky said a seven-year-old boy had been rescued alive from the site more than 14 hours after a 5am airstrike on a residential building where most people were sleeping inside.
Boy, 7, pulled alive from rubble 14 hours after Russian strike
A seven-year-old boy has been pulled alive from the rubble of a residential building in Ukraine’s Kyiv region, more than 14 hours after it was hit by a Russian strike.
The overnight attack on the town of Dymer killed nine people, according to local officials. A 79-year-old woman was also found alive under the debris and taken to hospital for treatment.

UN mission in Libya condemns Benghazi ship attack: Statement in full
Libya’s eastern-based government has submitted a formal request to the UN General Assembly and Security Council for an international investigation into the attacks on ships in its Benghazi naval port, prime minister Osama Hamad said in a statement.
He called for an investigation into "suspicions that the boats had been launched from western Libya ... and for verification of the presence of Ukrainian experts in the country, as well as formal explanations from Kyiv about their activities."
In a separate statement, the UN mission in Libya said the country must not “become an arena for external conflicts”
Here’s their statement in full:
“The United Nations Support Mission in Libya expresses its grave concern over the attacks carried out on Benghazi’s seaport and off the city’s coast on Sunday, and stresses that Libya’s sovereignty, territorial integrity, and the security of its citizens and resources must be fully respected.
“The Mission calls for an immediate, independent and transparent investigation to establish the facts and hold those responsible to account, expressing its readiness to assist the Libyan authorities in this investigation.
“The Mission also urges all parties to exercise the utmost restraint and refrain from disseminating any unverified information or politicizing the incident while the investigation is underway, warning against any actions or rhetoric that could escalate tensions within Libya or draw the country into broader regional or international confrontations. It stresses that Libya cannot afford, and should not be allowed, to become an arena for external conflicts.
“The Mission believes that these attacks underscore the urgent need to accelerate efforts to unify Libya’s national institutions and strengthen their ability to safeguard the country’s sovereignty and national security.
“While affirming that it will continue to closely monitor these serious developments, the Mission calls on all actors to act responsibly to preserve the country’s stability and build on the hard-won gains in the political process toward a lasting settlement.”
Satellite images show sunken Russian warship at Libya port
Satellite images released by Vantor show what’s left of the Russian warship Merkury after it was struck by a suspected Ukrainian drone attack at a naval base in Benghazi, Libya.
The pictures show that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk on Sunday, with only its bow still visible above water while smoke rises.
Three Russian missiles flew into Poland Friday, prosecutors say
Three objects that flew into Polish airspace on Friday were Russian Kh-101 missiles, Polish prosecutors said in a statement on Sunday.
Drones have repeatedly strayed into the airspace of countries on Nato's eastern flank during Russia's war in Ukraine, fuelling tension with the Western military alliance and stoking fears that the conflict could spread.
Child rescued from under the rubble in Kyiv, says Zelensky
President Volodymyr Zelensky has shared that a child has been rescued from under the rubble in Kyiv following a Russian strike.
“This evening, a child was rescued from under the rubble in Dymer, Kyiv region,” he wrote in a post on X on Sunday.
“The boy is now receiving the necessary medical care. The rescue operation has been ongoing all day. There is still no information about ten people.
“As of now, we know that, tragically, four people have been killed. My condolences to their families and loved ones. A Russian “shahed” struck this building, practically blowing a section of it to smithereens.”
He added: “There was also a strike in Vyshneve, Kyiv region, today – against an ordinary grocery store. Three people were killed and 13 injured. In the Bila Tserkva district, a “shahed” struck a residential building. Constant Russian terror, constant torment inflicted by these scumbags. Jammu, Nov 23: The Border Roads Organisation (BRO) today said that the organisation is carrying out post-Amarnath ji Yatra works in compliance with all applicable safety norms and environmental safeguards.
In a statement issued, it said that BRO takes all measures to ensure safe disposal of excavated material , protect natural drainage and minimise disturbance to surrounding terrain.
The BRO said that that the recently circulating video on social media claims about new works, is incorrect.
Based on experience of previous Yatra and requirement highlighted for wider road for Shri Amarnath ji yatra, BRO has started widening of tracks focusing on stabilising vulnerable stretches and widening the tracks as prescribed to ease congestion and allow safer passage, it said and added, the works are confined to the existing tracks.
BRO’s primary objective is to safeguard pilgrims throughout the Yatra. By making these tracks safer and more accessible for pilgrims, Yatra personnel and everyone else who uses it, the works serve the larger public interest, the statement added.

Ramban, Nov 23: The Srinagar–Jammu National Highway (NH-44) remained open for regulated two-way traffic of light, medium and heavy vehicles on Monday while vehicular movement continued to be slow at several stretches due to ongoing road construction, narrow single-lane sections and vehicle breakdowns.
Traffic authorities said that, subject to favourable weather and satisfactory road conditions, the highway would remain open for two-way traffic on Tuesday as well.
According to officials, slow movement was reported at Dewal in Udhampur district, where a 30–40-metre stretch was reduced to a single lane and the road surface remained uneven. Traffic congestion was also reported along the narrow single-lane stretch between Marog and Kishtwari Pather in Ramban district. The breakdown of two vehicles in the Ramban and Ramsu areas further affected the smooth movement of traffic.
Traffic personnel have been deployed at Dewal to regulate vehicular movement and facilitate the safe passage of vehicles through the restricted stretch.
Meanwhile, traffic authorities have advised commuters, particularly passengers and Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) operators, to undertake their journeys during daylight hours and avoid night travel in view of the risks of shooting stones and landslides, besides ongoing road construction and widening work between Ramban and Banihal.
In view of the widening work being undertaken by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) along the Digdol–Khooni Nullah stretch, the movement of Kashmir-bound oil and gas tankers will remain restricted between 7 am and 7 pm.
Beyond Chenani, tankers carrying inflammable materials will be permitted to pass through the tunnels only between 5 pm and 5 am.
Tanker operators have been advised to strictly adhere to the prescribed timings while planning their journeys. Transporters carrying perishable goods and livestock have also been directed to load their vehicles in accordance with advisories issued by Traffic Police Headquarters from time to time.
The advisory further urges heavy vehicle operators to avoid overloading, ensure that their vehicles are mechanically sound and carry sufficient fuel before commencing their journeys. Commuters have also been advised to avoid unnecessary halts between Ramban and Banihal, particularly at landslide-prone and shooting-stone vulnerable locations.
Traffic authorities reiterated that, subject to favourable weather and road conditions, LMVs, passenger vehicles, private cars and goods carriers, including heavy vehicles, would be allowed to ply in both directions on NH-44.
Traffic Control Units (TCUs) Jammu and Srinagar will remain in close coordination with TCU Ramban to monitor road conditions and regulate vehicular movement accordingly, officials said.

The Directorate General of GST Intelligence (DGGI) conducted searches across Vijayawada and Hyderabad’s Banjara Hills as part of an investigation into around ₹1 Lakh Cr of online gaming transactions suspected to be linked to China. Hyderabad-based firms allegedly worked with Chinese entities to operate four gaming platforms – superwinner, bigrummywinner, bigluckywinner, and rummyruler – and the associated Android platforms, according to the agency. The agency is investigating the firms’ promoters' alleged meeting with a Chinese intermediary in 2023 to set up domestic payment gateway services, while a China-based digital marketing team drove user acquisition. This helped siphon money to China via crypto. It is also alleged that payment aggregators used settlement accounts under dummy merchants, while certain intermediaries onboarded dummy merchants to boost platform fees, floating income, and turnover. The scheme is suspected to also involve potential use of cryptocurrencies such as USDT and suspected syndicate members in Dubai and Singapore. The DGGI team recorded the statement of Gali Kiran Kumar, and are also looking into the involvement of Satyanarayana Itakari, chairman and MD of First Finance Credit Cooperative Society. For context, the same entity was linked to the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation scam where funds intended for the welfare of tribal communities were siphoned and routed to bogus accounts. It won’t be unfair to say that illicit offshore gaming operators have picked up operations across India following a ban on online real money gaming. Head Digital Works, operator of A23 Rummy, alleged that legitimate businesses are suffering while illegitimate operators are booming. The remarks were highlighted before a Supreme Court bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant. Head Digital Works was seeking an early hearing around the real money gaming ban in a challenge brought by several gaming operators including Clubboom11 Sports & Entertainment (Boom11) and Bagheera Carrom. The Supreme Court has agreed to hear their plea on December 2. The ban had brought the industry to a near standstill, triggering mass layoffs and even shutdowns. Gaming startup Zupee constitutes one such example. It had claimed it was pivoting to AI but appears to have laid off its entire workforce and nearly wound up operations. Another prominent player in hot water after the regulatory crackdown is Gamekraft, which is also under scrutiny from the Enforcement Directorate (ED) over alleged money laundering. In total, the ED has attached, frozen, or seized assets worth around ₹2,843 Cr as part of its investigation.

The Delhi Government on Thursday (November 19, 2026) launched the ‘Ehsaas 2026’ Mental Health and Well-Being Policy for schools and higher educational institutions in the national capital. The policy aims to ensure one counsellor for every 500 students, besides providing helplines and mental and emotional support services.
Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa were present at the launch.
The policy seeks to raise awareness about mental health and encourage students, teachers and parents to speak openly about the subject, making mental and emotional well-being an integral part of education.
Under the policy, special attention will be given to examination pressure, academic stress, anxiety, depression, interpersonal relationships and challenges related to digital behaviour. Students dealing with the pressure of board and entrance examinations will also receive guidance and support, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).
The policy also provides for opportunities for students to develop stress-management and social-emotional skills, while sensitising teachers and parents to recognise early signs of mental health concerns. It also emphasises confidential mechanisms for reporting bullying, identity-based discrimination and cyberbullying, timely action on complaints, and protection from harassment for those filing complaints, according to an official statement.
Equal support for all children
The Lieutenant-Governor said making mental health and emotional well-being an integral part of education was the need of the hour. At a time when young people were facing increasing stress, the Delhi government’s initiative was timely and commendable.
Mr. Sandhu said, “Every child’s feelings, aspirations and needs matter. No child should face discrimination on the basis of their background, abilities or circumstances. Children with disabilities and those from disadvantaged communities must be given equal opportunities, acceptance and support.”
He added that responsibility for mental health rested not only with students but also with teachers, parents and school management.
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the policy had been introduced keeping in mind the mental health and overall well-being of students and would be implemented across schools and higher educational institutions in Delhi.
She said ‘Ehsaas’ would give millions of students studying in Delhi’s schools and colleges an opportunity to move forward with greater mental and emotional resilience. “The Delhi government wants every child to progress in life with happiness, positivity and confidence, and to know that the government, teachers and parents will stand by them through every challenge,” she said.
Six-tier mechanism
According to an official statement, the ‘Ehsaas’ policy will have a six-tier escalation mechanism to ensure student safety and address serious mental health crises. The mechanism will include the class teacher, school counsellor/first responder, school head/wellness team, District Well-Being Centre, hospital/emergency mental health services and relevant statutory agencies.
Students will have access to specialised mental health services through District Well-Being Centres established at the district level. These centres will provide psychological assessments, therapeutic interventions and psychiatric consultations.
“Schools will be responsible for early identification, initial psychosocial support and referrals, while clinical assessments and treatment will be handled by trained specialists, ensuring that students who need help receive appropriate care in time,” the statement further added.
Staff to receive training
Education Minister Ashish Sood said the government took up the issue after a school student attempted suicide a few days ago. Following the incident, he wrote to school principals and held discussions with them and mental health experts to work towards a comprehensive policy.
He said the policy was an important initiative to understand children’s emotional needs, listen to them and provide appropriate support. He also thanked the Art of Living, UNESCO, IHBAS and expert institutions for their contribution to developing the policy.
Mr. Sood said teachers, parents, principals, Educational and Vocational Guidance Counsellors (EVGCs), officials, drivers and other support staff would be trained to identify early changes in children’s behaviour and respond with sensitivity and appropriate support.
Four key pillars
The ‘Ehsaas’ policy is based on four key pillars. The first, the “Whole-Institution Approach”, seeks to make mental health part of an institution’s overall culture, with the participation of students, teachers, faculty, institutional heads, hostel staff and parents, according to the CMO.
The second pillar, Proactive and Preventive Care, focuses on identifying early signs of mental health concerns, promoting social-emotional and life skills, and building mental resilience.
The third, System-Level Accountability and Governance, seeks to ensure clearly defined responsibilities within institutions, staff training, capacity building and accountability of institutional leadership.
The fourth pillar, Ethical Safety and Rights-Based Support, will protect students’ dignity, privacy and confidentiality, ensure age-appropriate consent for minors and respect the autonomy of adult students.

Scientists use special tests to understand how autistic people see, hear, and process information. But many of these tests require participants to understand complex spoken rules, speak their answers out loud or fill out long written questionnaires. For instance, a standard perception study might ask a participant to watch a screen and say out loud which direction a cluster of dots is moving. A non-verbal autistic child cannot provide the required response, automatically excluding them from the research.
Now, Boston University researchers have tried to study perception without relying on language or conventional test-taking skills by turning a sensory test originally developed for rodents into a non-verbal online video game that adolescents across the autism spectrum can learn and play.
This holds special promise for India. A non-verbal, remote game bypasses the need to translate complex clinical instructions into dozens of regional languages, and allows researchers to reach autistic individuals far beyond the major metros where specialist centres are concentrated.

Whether planning a country-hopping odyssey or a quick business trip, your journey will go more smoothly with the best travel adapters that allow you to safely charge all your gadgets wherever you land. After many work trips and family vacations I’ve tested several—both universal and basic options—and my favorites will work in most parts of the world.

Travel Adapters: Your Questions, Answered
What Type of Adapter Do You Need?
There are 15 plug types in use across the world. Universal adapters tend to cover all of these types.
- Type A and Type B are used in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Japan.
- Type C is common across Europe, South America, and Asia.
- Type E and Type F are found across Europe in places like Germany, Russia, and France.
- Type G is used in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and a handful of other places.
- Type I is used in Australia, New Zealand, China, and Argentina.
Some countries are not usually covered by universal adapters, such as India (Type D), Israel (Type H), and South Africa (Type M or N). You'll need to buy specific plug adapters for those places. To avoid any surprises when you land, double-check what type you need before you travel.
If you're visiting just one destination, a basic plug adapter that caters to one plug type is all you need. For trips to multiple destinations or for frequent flyers, a universal travel adapter can prove more versatile. The universal adapters I recommend here have the bonus of including multiple USB ports for charging several mobile devices from a single outlet.
Do You Really Need a Voltage Converter?
Voltage converters are big, heavy, and expensive, and they don’t always work—so it’s probably best to avoid them. The reason you might think you need one is that the AC sockets on all of our recommended travel adapters do not convert the voltage coming from the socket. This means plugging into a UK socket will deliver 220 volts at 50 hertz, which is very different from the 120 volts at 60 hertz you can expect in the US. Don't worry! Your gear won’t get fried. You just need to make sure anything you plug into one of these universal travel adapters has something like this printed on it:
Input: 100–220V 50/60Hz
That should include most modern gadgets. If your device or charger can’t handle a variable voltage, it’s probably best to leave it at home. Most places provide hair dryers, irons, and kettles, so there’s no need to take them with you. It’s also often cheaper to buy a set with the correct plug at your destination and save the luggage space and hassle.
If you are determined to try a voltage converter (again, I don’t recommend doing so), the Ceptics 2,000-watt Travel Voltage Converter ($70) seems to work well. It has a special 2,000-watt outlet for hair dryers, but only ones that work via a mechanical switch (anything with an electronic circuit board for automatic switch-off or temperature control won’t work and is at risk of being fried if plugged in). It also has two outlets that go up to 200 watts, one USB-C port, and three USB-A ports, though the ports do not support fast charging.
What About Wattage?
Travel adapters and chargers usually state the wattage they can deliver for USB-C and USB-A ports, retractable cables, and wireless charging. If you're interested in getting the fastest rates possible, you’ll want a charger and cable that can deliver the maximum wattage to your device. A laptop might want 100 watts, while a phone only needs 30 watts. There's no need to worry if the charger can deliver more wattage than is required because the device will dictate how much power to draw. If the wattage is lower than required, most devices will simply charge slowly. You can find out more about charging standards like Power Delivery (PD), Quick Charge (QC), and others in my guide on how to fast charge your phone.
Can Travel Adapters Go in a Suitcase?
Yes, you can pack travel adapters in your suitcase. It may be wise to bring one in your hand luggage for easy access should you need to charge up a device when you arrive at your destination. In fact, devices like power banks with lithium batteries (must be capped at 27,000 mAh) must go in hand luggage, not checked bags.
Can I Buy Travel Adapters at the Airport or Hotel?
You certainly can buy travel adapters at the airport, but like all other goods you buy at kiosks between connecting flights, they will be far more expensive than necessary, and your choice will be limited.
Some hotels have travel adapters, and some even have wall outlets for other countries (or USB-A and USB-C ports), but most do not, so don’t bank on it. You can always check with your hotel or accommodation before you depart, but it’s safer to bring a travel adapter with you.
Should You Test Your Travel Adapter Before You Go?
Seriously, nothing is worse than thinking you’re being very clever by packing light only to get to your hotel and discover that your gadgets refuse to charge. Between the adapter, cable, and your device, plenty can go wrong, so do a quick test on your wall outlet at home with everything you are taking before you set off on an international trip.
How I Test Travel Adapters
Anytime I fly for work or vacation, I take a few travel adapters and chargers with me to test. I also test them for longer periods at home in the UK. I have power stations and power strips with US and EU outlets to test those plugs. I test each charger with a variety of devices (iPhone, Pixel, iPad, MacBook, AirPods). I try charging with every port and outlet simultaneously to see if the charger gets warm. I assess the charging rates, durability, size, weight, and usability of each device. If there are any special features, I test them too.
More Travel Adapters I Like
There is an endless amount of travel adapters out there you could buy. While I wholeheartedly recommend one of the options above, there are some other travel adapters I've tested that just barely miss the mark.
Epicka Pulse for $30: The beveled edges of this travel adapter from Epicka make it more comfortable to hold. The sliders work well and lock in place securely to cover you in around 200 countries. A pair of USB-C and two USB-A ports provide a good mix of port options. This adapter can deliver up to 45 watts from either USB-C port, while the USB-A ports top out at 18 watts. I also tested the newer Epicka Pulse Duo ($130), which can deliver up to 140 watts across three USB-C and one USB-A ports, has an extra US or Japanese socket in the side and boasts a smart display that shows you the current charging status, wattage, and temperature. Cool as it is, it's overkill for most folks and kinda pricey.
Tessan Travel Adapter 009 for $20: This is a similar design to the Epicka Air I recommend above, but the prongs don’t stay in place as securely when unfolded, and you can only draw a maximum of 20 watts from the one USB-A and two USB-C ports. But it is affordable and compact. Tessan also makes good, traditional, slider universal adapters: There's a 140-watt model ($70), and the most powerful travel adapter I’ve tested, the Voyager 205 ($128), which has six USB-C ports and one USB-A to deliver up to 205 watts. If you don’t care about charging speed, Tessan's 20W model ($23) is very reasonably priced and offers two USB-A and two USB-C ports in a small package.
UGreen Travel Plug Adapter for £17: This travel adapter is for UK folks visiting Europe, and it’s a solid option with a fixed plug (no mechanism). It has only two USB-A and one USB-C port for smaller devices, and it’s very bulky. I prefer the OneBeat above for this type of design.
Statik SmartCharge Pro for $80: This is a nice combo device that includes a 15,000 mAh power bank and a 60-watt wall charger. There are fold-out US prongs and slide-on adapters for the UK, EU, and AU. You also get one USB-A port, one USB-C port, a fold-out USB-C cable, and a wireless charging pad on top that works with your iPhone or Apple Watch.
D-Link 65W Multi-Port GaN Charger (DCP-651) for $30: If two USB-C ports and a USB-A port are enough for your travel needs, this affordable D-Link charger could be for you. It comes with interchangeable plugs for different countries. The 65-watt limit is enough for overnight charging a laptop and a couple of smartphones.
Arsmel VisaPro All-in-One Travel Adapter for $80: This chunky power adapter can charge laptops or multiple small devices with a whopping 170-watt maximum output. It works with any outlet in the US, UK, or EU, thanks to sliding plugs that slot in securely, and you can spin the prongs on the US plug to support the total number of countries (more than 200). I love the mecha-inspired paint job, too. There are four ports along the bottom: two USB-C ports rated at 140 watts, with the third USB-C and USB-A ports rated at 18 watts. It supports PD 3.1, QC 3.0, PPS, FCP, and SCP, and has a 10-amp fuse.
Satechi GaN Travel Charger for $120: If you only take small gadgets with you when you travel, a compact, multi-port wall charger is all you need and a great way to pack light. It plugs directly into the wall and comes with four interchangeable travel adapters for the EU, UK, and Australia, plus a mesh bag to store them. There are four USB-C ports that you can plug your gadgets into, including laptops like the MacBook Pro, tablets, phones, and wearables. With support for Power Delivery 3.1, the first two ports can supply up to 140 watts, and the bottom two ports up to 45 watts. However, the maximum output when all four ports are in use is 145 watts.
Baseus 70W Universal Travel Adapter With Retractable Cable for $40: This excellent travel adapter is almost identical to our top pick from Ceptics, offering up to 70 watts, sliding prongs to cover more than 200 countries, and a built-in retractable USB-C cable, not to mention a USB-C port and two USB-A ports. It also has a snazzy black-and-yellow finish. It only misses out because it’s slightly more expensive, but if you can snag one on sale or prefer the colors, it’s a solid option.
Epicka Universal Travel Adapter for $20: This travel adapter from Epicka is still a solid option. The sliding plugs cover 150 countries, and there are four USB-A ports on the bottom and a 15-watt USB-C port on the side. There’s also an 8-amp fuse with a spare, and this adapter is RoHS-, CE-, and FCC-certified.
Masterplug Visitor to UK Travel Adapter (3 Pack) for £12: For visitors to the UK, this simple trio of adapters accepts European, American, Australian, and Asian plugs. They are single-outlet adapters with 13-amp fuses inside, and they work perfectly. These are the adapters I use for long-term testing of devices from the US and elsewhere that lack UK plugs. If you forgot to buy an adapter before arriving in the UK, you can find this affordable three-pack at any Argos store.
Anker European Travel Plug Adapter for $16: One of our favorite portable charger brands, Anker, also makes travel adapters. This one plugs into most European outlets to provide a single grounded US outlet, a USB-A port, and two USB-C ports. Unfortunately, the three USB ports max out at 15 watts total, so it’s best for overnight gadget charging, but I appreciate the temperature and overload protection. There is also a UK version ($16).
Epicka Hybrid European Travel Plug Adapter for $26: This handy adapter turns one outlet into four and includes four USB ports (two A and two C). It has fold-out Type A prongs, but you can also slide on a fold-out Type C plug for use in Europe. While the USB ports support QC 3.0 or PD 3.0, they max out at 20 watts in total. I prefer the OneBeat adapters recommended above.
Travel Adapters to Avoid
You can do better than these travel adapters.
EZQuest WorldTravel GaN 5 Port With PD Wall Charger: This travel adapter has a generous four USB-C ports and one USB-A port with a familiar slide-out prong design that covers more than 150 countries. Bulk Crap Uninstaller (BCU) lets you uninstall multiple Windows apps at once for free. Select unwanted apps, remove them in batches, and clean up leftover files to reclaim storage. It also supports quiet uninstallation, but review your selections carefully before deleting anything.
An easy way to free up storage on your Windows PC is to remove unnecessary apps — ones you no longer need. You identify the apps and delete them one by one. It’s pretty straightforward as long as you’re dealing with a couple of apps. If the number is higher, the method starts to feel tedious.
This is where a one-click uninstaller comes in handy, allowing you to delete multiple apps at once. Bulk Crap Uninstaller (BCU) is one such app. Here’s how it works and how to use it to bulk uninstall Windows apps on your PC.
What Is Bulk Crap Uninstaller, and What Makes It Better Than Other Tools?
Bulk Crap Uninstaller (also called BCUninstaller or BCU) is a bulk uninstaller that makes uninstalling multiple apps on your Windows PC at once incredibly easy. It can scan your computer comprehensively and find everything from Windows Store apps (pre-installed by Microsoft) and third-party apps to Steam games, portable apps, and Chocolatey packages. You can then select what you want to remove. This adds them to a queue, and the app handles uninstallation for you.
Bulk Crap Uninstaller stands out from other bulk uninstallers, including some paid alternatives, in a few ways. First, it can find broken or un-uninstallable programs and force uninstall them. Second, it can scan your file system and find leftover or orphaned items (files, folders, registry keys) left behind by apps you deleted manually. That way, you can safely and easily delete them and reclaim storage space. And third, it offers a “quiet uninstallation” mode that eliminates the need to click through dialog boxes and instead uninstalls the selected apps silently in the background.
How To Use Bulk Crap Uninstaller to Bulk Uninstall Windows Apps on Your PC
Bulk Crap Uninstaller is free to download and use. Go to the Bulk Crap Uninstaller website, and you’ll see multiple ways to download the app there. You can choose any method; the easiest is to download the installer from SourceForge. Next, run the installer and follow the on-screen instructions to complete it. Once installed, the app will require configuration. Configure it per your preference; you can change the settings later if you don’t like them. I recommend enabling the Select using checkboxes and Show items in groups options.
Once configured, Bulk Crap Uninstaller will scan your computer and populate a list of all installed programs, including hidden apps, Windows Store apps, Steam games, portable apps, orphaned shortcuts, and leftover registry keys. You’ll see additional details, such as size, version, publisher name, installation date, and certificate, next to each listing. You can use filters and sort options to filter out and sort items in a specific order.
Go through the list and tick the checkbox next to the apps you want to uninstall. The status bar at the bottom will show how many items you’ve selected and how much space deleting them will free up. Finally, click the Uninstall button at the top. The app will open a dialog box showing your selection. Hit Continue while checking (and changing, if required) the settings, and click Begin Uninstallation.
You’ll see a prompt asking if you’d like to create a Restore Point. Select accordingly, and the app will uninstall the selected apps. While it deletes apps, you’ll see the uninstallation status in a dialog box. At any point, if you want to cancel the uninstallation, click the Cancel button.
Once Bulk Crap Uninstaller finishes uninstalling the selected apps, it will ask if you want to delete the leftovers too. Review the listed files carefully, uncheck the ones you don’t want to delete, and click the Delete selected button to get rid of them. Be sure to back up your registry if you’ll be deleting leftover registry keys.
When you uninstall apps this way, you’ll need to click through multiple dialog box menus to complete the uninstallation. You can save yourself this hassle by clicking the Quiet Uninstall button instead of Uninstall after selecting apps for deletion. Bulk Crap Uninstaller will try — wherever possible — to uninstall apps silently. You won’t see visual confirmation in this mode.
Other Bulk Crap Uninstaller Features You Should Know About
For most people, the standard uninstallation process we checked out above is enough to get the job done. However, Bulk Crap Uninstaller has a few advanced features that can help you get the most out of the app.
For example, Bulk Crap Uninstaller offers a CLI version called BCU-console. It’s a great option for those who want to clean up their PC without dealing with multiple windows. Similarly, it lets you run an uninstallation script with your selected apps to automate deletion. This can be useful for cleaning up new PCs, too. Just feed the app a list of all the pre-installed apps from Windows, and it will remove them. You can go through Bulk Crap Uninstaller’s documentation to learn more about using scripts.
Bulk Crap Uninstaller can also run portably. So, you can put it on a USB flash drive and run it directly. This is handy when you want to uninstall apps on a PC running very low on storage space or one that isn’t connected to the internet and can’t download the Bulk Crap Uninstaller app.
Last but not least, Bulk Crap Uninstaller is highly configurable. As such, you can configure its behavior per your preference. Click the gear icon in the top toolbar to access the app’s settings. Here, you can change things like where to look for apps, which items to show/omit, and how the list appears. You can also configure the default behavior of quiet uninstallation and how many concurrent uninstalls the app can perform, among other things.
What I’m Not a Fan Of
I’ve used Bulk Crap Uninstaller on my PC for a while, and although it does its job well, there are a few aspects that I’m not a fan of and wish were better. The biggest one is that the app’s interface can seem intimidating, especially to first-time users. In other words, it looks more like a developer tool than a regular consumer app. It’s best to spend some time exploring different menus and options the app offers before jumping straight into uninstalling apps.
Then, there’s the risk of over-cleaning. Because Bulk Crap Uninstaller can scan deep system components, too, it’s important to double-check the selection — and not blindly trust the populated list — before uninstallation. You can configure the settings to minimize the risk. Another thing I’ve noticed is that the quiet uninstallation mode sometimes doesn’t work: some apps don’t obey it and keep popping up dialog boxes that require confirmation before uninstallation. Although rare, some users have complained about aggressive registry scanning, wherein Bulk Crap Uninstaller highlights shared keys (those used by other apps too) for removal. You can avoid this by reviewing the registry keys highlighted for deletion.
These aren’t drawbacks of Bulk Crap Uninstaller, though; they’re just a trade-off for its advanced capabilities. For this reason, it’s important to configure the app before you start using it and be completely sure about the actions you perform using it. You should also create a Restore Point when dealing with apps with broken uninstallers or stubborn leftovers. This way, if the cleanup goes wrong and renders your PC unusable, you can roll back to the last working state and undo the action.

Stealing a shiny supercar has always been fun and easy throughout the Grand Theft Auto franchise, but GTA 6 is changing the formula with the new vehicle tracker system. This can alert the cops when a vehicle is stolen and even give away your location. So, follow this guide to learn how to remove a vehicle tracker in GTA 6 and keep the stolen vehicle to yourself.
How Do Vehicle Trackers Work in GTA 6
Unlike the previous releases, GTA 6 introduces different levels of vehicle protection. Depending on the vehicles in GTA 6, you may encounter conventional car alarms, key ignition systems, or GPS trackers that notify the cops of your whereabouts.
The higher-end security systems are particularly common in expensive vehicles found around wealthy locations in GTA 6, including Capri, Vice City Beach, and Leaf Links. So, here are the two main types of GPS trackers in the game as follows:
| Tracker Type | How it works | How to remove | 
|---|---|---|
| Standard (Yellow) Tracker | Alerts the police after the vehicle remains stationary for a few seconds. | Visit a Pay ‘N’ Spray shop and pay the registration fee | 
| Advanced (Red) Tracker | Sends your location to the police if you maintain a low speed for a while | After completing Randy’s mission in Chapter 3 to unlock advanced tracker removal service in Pay ‘N’ Spray shops | 
How to Remove Vehicle Trackers in GTA 6
Removing a vehicle tracker requires different approaches depending on its security level. Here’re some of the ways to remove the standard and advanced trackers in the game:
Remove Standard Tracker
For vehicles with the standard yellow trackers, you can simply visit a Pay ‘N’ Spray and pay the registration fee to make the car yours. This permanently removes the tracker and allows you to store the vehicle in your garage in GTA 6.
Remove Advanced Tracker
The first method of visiting any Pay ‘N’ Spray shops will not work for advanced trackers right away. So, you need to reach Chapter 3 and initiate Randy’s questline. It requires you to bring 18 rare and exotic vehicles from all across Leonida to the desired location.
Once you complete the last drop for the Declasse Mamba GT, Randy will contact you later to let you know that the advanced tracker removal service is now available at all Pay ‘N’ Spray shops across the state.
Now, you can steal any high-end vehicle, reach the Pay ‘N’ Spray shop, repaint it, and pay the registration fee to remove the advanced tracker and make the vehicle yours. Needless to say, this requires an available vehicle slot.
Can You Escape Police Without Removing a Tracker?
Yes, apparently, you can escape the cops even without removing the tracker in the stolen car, but that would just be a temporary solution. Just make sure that it has enough gas, or you might end up refueling the car in GTA 6 while the cops show up behind you.
For yellow trackers, simply avoid bringing the car to a complete stop. As long as you keep moving, the tracking system won’t immediately report your location.
Red trackers are a bit more demanding, as you need to maintain a sufficiently high speed. Slowing down for approximately five seconds will trigger a police notification, giving away your location. Eventually, this can lead them to bust you and the car would be lost as well.
A helpful tip before stealing cars is to use the WAINK app in GTA 6 to scan the vehicles. This will reveal the important tracker information, security level, resale value, and more.
As for keeping the vehicle stored in your garage after stealing it, this is also not a permanent solution. You will eventually need to deal with it before taking it out into the streets.
That is all you need to learn about how to remove the vehicle trackers in GTA 6. So, what other new features can you spot and differentiate from the past releases? Tell us in the comments below.

Children who lived in Brazilian neighbourhoods buzzing with a special kind of mosquito were far less likely to catch dengue or another worrisome virus, chikungunya, researchers reported Saturday.
The major study of more than 5,700 children in one of the world's dengue hot spots offers new evidence that breeding mosquitoes unable to transmit these viruses can be a viable strategy rather than solely relying on pesticides and trying to avoid getting bitten.
In neighbourhoods populated by these so-called Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, researchers found about a 69% reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in schoolchildren compared to similar neighbourhoods — an effect sustained even during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak, said Dr. Sri Edupuganti of Emory University, part of the international research team.
The researchers reported the findings at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.
“This is really exciting,” said David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University who wasn't involved with the Brazilian study. He predicts that pairing more use of these Wolbachia mosquitoes with existing steps to fight mosquito-borne disease could “knock dengue down to much lower levels” in many places.
The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s.
Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa.
Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy.
How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.
Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.
The four-year study compared children living in neighborhoods that all got the same pesticide and other mosquito-control interventions, but half were randomly assigned to have Wolbachia mosquitoes released into the area. There were too few cases of Zika to calculate if the special mosquitoes had any effect on that disease.

Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
Annual open enrollment is underway for Medicare, the federal program that provides health insurance to roughly 70 million people. The coverage choices are complex and often consequential.
Open enrollment runs through Dec. 7. The plan you choose takes effect on Jan. 1, for the full calendar year.
Build-your-own Medicare menu
Medicare provides health insurance to people 65 or older, as well as to some younger people with disabilities or certain health conditions. But it isn't one plan. It's more like a build-your-own-insurance menu.
Roughly half of beneficiaries are enrolled in traditional Medicare, which consists of Parts A and B. Administered by the federal government, the plan covers hospital stays, skilled nursing care, doctor visits, outpatient care, and preventive screenings. Enrollees can typically see any healthcare provider who accepts Medicare, and they rarely need approval for diagnostic tests, such as MRIs and CT scans. However, there's no cap on out-of-pocket expenses in traditional Medicare, and it doesn't cover most prescriptions or dental, vision, or hearing services.
As a result, most traditional Medicare enrollees buy extra coverage from private insurance companies under Medicare Part D, the prescription drug plan. Some also buy a Medigap policy that covers the costs traditional Medicare leaves behind, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance.
Medicare Advantage
This year, the other half of Medicare beneficiaries opted for privately offered, all-in-one managed-care plans known as Medicare Advantage, usually including prescription drug coverage, dental, and vision. The drawbacks are smaller networks and a greater likelihood that treatments and medications will require prior authorization. Like beneficiaries in traditional Medicare, Medicare Advantage participants also pay Part B premiums.
"People really need to do their research before they enroll in Medicare, because there are trade-offs," said David Lipschutz, a co-director at the Center for Medicare Advocacy.
The hassle saves money
Every fall, insurers that offer Part D and Advantage plans send enrollees a critical document known as an Annual Notice of Change. It's a cheat sheet outlining what will be different in the following year: premiums, deductibles, covered drugs. Consumer advocates and Medicare experts say people sometimes make the costly mistake of throwing it out or filing it away without reading it. Can't find it? Call the insurer and ask for another copy.
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services projects that the average Part D premium will increase less than $1 a month for a standalone prescription drug plan, describing the market as stable. But that average doesn't tell the whole story. An analysis by KFF, the health policy research nonprofit that includes KFF Health News, found that enrollees who stay in their prescription drug plan will see a 50% increase on average, from $34 to $51. About 10.4 million people could pay higher premiums, not including higher deductibles and coinsurance costs.
Some beneficiaries who didn't have to pay monthly premiums in recent years will begin paying for prescription drug Part D coverage in 2027. While that change follows the 2025 introduction of federal caps on out-of-pocket drug expenses, it comes as the Trump administration is ending temporary federal subsidies that helped keep premiums down. The cap on out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs in 2027 will be $2,400, a total enrollees can opt tospread out over the course of the year.
Juliette Cubanski, who directs the Program on Medicare Policy at KFF, said people who don't shop around could be leaving money on the table.
"It is worth it to avoid any unpleasant surprises in the form of either higher premiums or higher cost sharing for covered services in 2027," she said.
Some plans no longer offered
An estimated 4.3 million people now have to look for a new Medicare Advantage or prescription drug plan after private insurers left the market. Those who want to stay in Medicare Advantage must select new coverage, or they'll be moved to traditional Medicare automatically. For those shopping for a new plan, low monthly premiums may be appealing, but it's important to read the fine print and add up the other costs.
"There are going to be, often, increases in cost sharing and copays, increases in out-of-pocket caps, and reductions in the scope of some of the extra benefits that Medicare Advantage plans provide," Lipschutz said.
So ask: Is my prescription covered? Is my pharmacy preferred? Is my doctor in-network? What does the dental benefit actually cover?
And pay attention to the out-of-pocket maximum for the Advantage plans, Cubanski said, so you know how much you might have to shell out in 2027.
"Look at that dollar value specifically," she said.
For those moving to traditional Medicare, it won't come with a drug plan, so enrollees must sign up for a new Part D plan if they want most prescriptions covered. Enrollees who miss that step when they are first eligible may not have drug coverage for the coming year, and they may face a late-enrollment penalty on their monthly premiums for life.
When selecting a drug plan, enrollees must also tell their insurer how they want to pay, either by getting a bill in the mail or by having the cost deducted from their Social Security. If you don't pick a payment plan, you could get dropped from coverage.
If enrollees elect to leave their Medicare Advantage plans for traditional Medicare within their first year of joining Medicare, they have a guaranteed right to buy a Medigap plan, with no health screening. After that, all bets are off: Insurers in most states can turn enrollees down or charge more because of a health condition. Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, and New York are exceptions.
Enrollees whose Advantage plans have not been renewed — and haven't been consolidated into another plan — can switch to traditional Medicare and buy a Medigap policy without a health screening, but they need to act before March.
For shopping help, think "SHIP"
Medicare experts advise enrollees to write down all their prescription drugs, as well as any procedures planned in the next year, such as a joint replacement or dental work, to help them decide which plan will cover their needs. Call a favorite doctor's office to see whether they are in-network for the plans being considered. Remember that brokers might earn commissions, especially on Advantage plans, and might not represent every plan.
For unbiased help, every state has a federally funded State Health Insurance Assistance Program that offers free plan counseling specific to your situation, in person and over the phone. To get help, go to the website at shiphelp.org/open-enrollment, email info@shiphelp.org, or call the SHIP National Technical Assistance Center at 877-839-2675.
A SHIP counselor can also help enrollees apply for benefits that help pay for Medicare premiums and prescription drug costs, such as the Medicare Savings Programs and Medicare Part D Extra Help.
KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF — the independent source for health policy research, polling, and journalism.

Adding to the growing threats of cyber attacks, SaaS startup MoEngage has now suffered a cybersecurity breach. The attack involved unauthorised access to a limited part of the startup’s cloud infrastructure via a compromised third-party vendor account. Some customers reportedly faced difficulties accessing the platform for nearly seven days, according to a report by ET. However, MoEngage denied any disruption in its services. It claimed to have identified and contained the incident in late October. It said that it engaged independent cybersecurity experts to validate its findings, remediated the breach and strengthened its security measures. "Fewer than 1% of our customer accounts were affected, and we have notified each of them directly. There was no disruption to our services as a result of this incident," MoEngage said. The incident comes amid growing concerns around cybersecurity risks arising from third-party service providers and vulnerabilities across interconnected digital infrastructure. Recent disruptions involving technology companies and large enterprises, including Microsoft, Apple, JPMorgan Chase and the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), have renewed attention on the resilience of global digital infrastructure amid the growing threat of AI. In this light, Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora warned that AI makes it easier for hackers to target multiple organisations simultaneously. AI can accelerate reconnaissance, identify vulnerabilities and enable attackers to scale their operations across several targets. A key point of entry for compromising major software infrastructures has been their interaction with third-party vendors. Smaller service providers do not maintain security standards comparable to those of their enterprise clients. Compromising a single tech provider can potentially expose multiple organisations that rely on its services. Founded in 2014 by Raviteja Dodda and Yashwanth Kumar, MoEngage provides customer engagement, analytics and messaging software that enables businesses to communicate with users through mobile notifications, email, SMS, WhatsApp and in-app messages. Headquartered in Bengaluru and San Francisco, the company claims to serve over 1,350 enterprises across 75 countries. MoEngage is also preparing for a potential public listing in India. In January 2026, the National Company Law Tribunal approved the reverse merger of its US-based parent, MoEngage Inc, into its Indian arm, MoEngage India Private Limited, as part of its corporate restructuring ahead of a potential domestic listing.
