Hungary’s Magyar says he will visit Ukraine in a sign of mending relations
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar plans to visit Ukraine soon, signaling improved relations between the two countries
BUDAPEST, Hungary -- Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said Monday that he will soon travel to Ukraine in a sign that the icy relations between the two neighboring countries, pushed to the breaking point by former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, are improving.
Magyar's planned visit to the embattled country comes after Kyiv passed a law in October — long demanded by Hungary’s government — that expanded language rights for a Hungarian ethnic minority in western Ukraine.
Speaking to lawmakers on Monday, Magyar did not announce a date for his visit, but said it would take place in the western Ukrainian region of Zakarpattia, home to tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians. It will be the first visit to the region by a Hungarian head of government since 2015.
Magyar denounced Russian strikes that hit the mountainous region last week and said he would travel there “soon ... to personally deliver the support of the motherland to our Hungarian brethren.”
Before Magyar and his Tisza party won a landslide election in April, Hungary's government under Orbán pursued a hostile approach to Ukraine, repeatedly blocking aid to Kyiv and holding up European Union sanctions against Russia, all while maintaining cordial ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Orbán's government had also depicted Ukraine as a threat to Hungary's security, and cast President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as an enemy, using his likeness in taxpayer-funded political campaigns.
Since taking office, Magyar's government has taken a markedly different approach, expressing solidarity with Ukraine and designating Russia a national security threat. In an interview last month with The Associated Press, Magyar said he saw “a chance to open a new chapter in Ukrainian-Hungarian relations.”
On Monday, Magyar expressed his sympathy “to the Hungarians of Zakarpattia and to the entire Ukrainian people, who for nearly five years have been waging a superhuman struggle for their mere survival.”
“I want to make clear what every well-meaning person in the world knows: that Russia is the aggressor and Ukraine, the Ukrainian people, are the victims,” he said. “We stand by our Hungarian compatriots in Zakarpattia and for the Ukrainian people who have come under attack, even if someone in Moscow doesn't like it.”
Magyar also said he would attend negotiations later this week on the EU's next seven-year budget, but that Hungary would insist that the bloc's financial support for Ukraine be handled separately.

British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.
Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.
In the 1840s, Cuba was the most important foreign source of copper ore for the UK. Copper was critical to Manchester’s cotton industry, railways and telegraphy.
Previous research has revealed that dozens of financiers involved in the founding in 1694 of the Bank of England invested in enslavement.
Now, Evans’s research reveals that ties between key figures in the UK’s financial system and enslavement of African peoples continued even after the government outlawed it.
Britain abolished its trade in enslaved people in 1807 and passed legislation abolishing slavery in most of its empire in 1833.
However, as Britain’s Slavery Abolition Act was coming into force, “City of London figures” were developing mining of El Cobre’s copper ore deposits, an operation which depended on enslavement in Spanish-controlled Cuba.
Key players in the highly lucrative operation included the Bank of England directors Charles Pascoe Grenfell (1790-1867) and William Thompson (1792-1854), acting in a private capacity.
Enslaved copper miners at El Cobre were likely to have been trafficked to Cuba by illegal voyages from the Bight of Biafra, in modern-day Nigeria, as Evans details in his book, Slavery’s Long Goodbye – Capitalism, Nationalism and Christianity in the Age of British Emancipation.
The death rate at El Cobre means it is likely that thousands of Africans were exploited there. Their life stories remain largely undocumented. At the time, slavery was legal in Cuba but the importation of enslaved people was not.
As a partner in the Cobre mining and export company, Grenfell was a driving force in enslaved miners’ exploitation.
Cobre was “likely to be the largest slave enterprise in the western hemisphere” by the 1840s, Evans said. Investors who held Cobre shares from the outset received £102 in dividends for every £40 share between 1836 and 1865.
Grenfell was also a partner in a Swansea-based smelter Pascoe, Grenfell & Sons, which bought imports from the mine, in an era when the Welsh port was the centre of the global copper trade.
Meanwhile, Thompson, a former lord mayor of London, exploited enslaved miners through the ore export firm he directed, the Royal Santiago Company.
The UK is facing increased pressure to make a formal apology to Caribbean and African nations for Britain’s centuries-long perpetuation of transatlantic chattel slavery. Commonwealth leaders say “structured dialogue” with the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, will begin in the next year.
While the Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has claimed Britain has nothing to apologise for, scholarship – dating back to the Trinidadian statesman Eric Williams’s 1944 book, Capitalism and Slavery – reveals the global impact of the colonialism and chattel enslavement that was integral to British capitalism’s success.
Evans, a former professor at the University of South Wales, said: “As Britain ostentatiously winds down its own slave system in the 1830s, British capital is boosting slavery elsewhere in the western hemisphere.
“The illegal trade, involving French and Spanish merchants, was flourishing and substantial. There were British (anti-slavery) patrols off the coast of Cuba, but they’re relatively few in number and intercept only a very small proportion of slave ships.”
Conditions at El Cobre were “extremely brutal”, with daily violence and torture. “Slave catchers” were employed to snatch miners who tried to escape to the mountains.
In 1817, under British pressure, Spanish authorities signed a treaty that banned trafficking enslaved Africans to Cuba. But as Cuba’s sugar and coffee plantations relied on enslaved African workers, local colonial authorities ignored it, with 25,000 captives arriving in 1859 alone.
In 1843, pressure from the British and Foreign Anti-Slavery Society prompted legislation intended to prohibit British subjects from owning enslaved people in other jurisdictions, after undercover investigations exposed British mining companies’ activities in Brazil and Cuba, including at El Cobre.
But after lobbying by mining interests, parliament diluted the legislation, allowing companies to retain enslaved workers as their “property” and hire others. The concessions prompted abolitionists to withdraw their support for the law, which failed to end the exploitation.
Neither Grenfell nor Thompson appears to have faced legal penalties for their involvement. Grenfell became the Liberal MP for Preston in the late 1840s, later boasting that his father had been an abolitionist. Grenfell remained a B of E director until 1864.
Enslavement at El Cobre finally ended after Cuban revolutionaries captured the town from Spanish forces in November 1868. The rebel commander proclaimed the miners’ emancipation on New Year’s Eve, and formerly enslaved workers later joined Cuba’s liberation army.
Evans’s book explores Britain’s overlapping histories of slavery, capitalism and missionary Christianity through the lives of Grenfell and two of his cousins.
Evans added: “The British in the early 19th century had started to understand slavery as a national sin.
“In the classical age of abolition, you could do things like abstain from eating sugar from the West Indies.
“But with copper, you can’t do that because it’s embodied in the industrial world, and, in the age of joint-stock capitalism, you have many British people who invest in mining companies who genuinely didn’t know these companies were using enslaved workers.
“Slavery was rendered invisible by the complexity of industrial society. But British engagement with slavery continued long after Emancipation. It involved the mercantile-financial elite of London as well as hundreds, possibly thousands, of rank-and-file investors from the Victorian middle class.”
A Bank of England spokesperson said: “We have previously acknowledged the role of former governors and directors in the slave trade.”

Quick Answer
The Dreame X60 Ultra Complete offers powerful suction, heated-water mopping, a slimmer design, and smarter obstacle handling. At ₹1,34,999, it delivers an impressive cleaning experience with greater convenience, though the value of its premium features depends on your home’s needs.
When I reviewed the X40 Ultra, it was the first robot where I didn’t have to plan a backup round of cleaning. Months later, the L40 Ultra AE beat it on suction and mopping for Rs 20,000 less. The X60 Ultra Complete has to answer a question both reviews left open: what does a Dreame flagship do that the cheaper model does not?
On paper, quite a lot. It also costs more than twice what the L40 Ultra AE did, so the real question is whether the additions change daily cleaning in an Indian home or mostly change the spec sheet.
Table of Contents
Design and Build: Slimmer Robot, Smarter Moves
At first glance, the X60 Pro Complete looks like any other premium Dreame device. You get the familiar circular body, a large docking station, and a design that is more functional than flashy. But there’s one important difference. At just 7.95 cm tall, the X60 is noticeably slimmer than the X40 Ultra and L40 Ultra AE. And that’s thanks to the retractable navigation sensor that pops up when needed and slides back into the body when the robot needs to squeeze under low furniture.
This might sound gimmicky at first (remember OnePlus 7T Pro?), but it has a practical value. In 2026, most robot vacuums already do a decent job of cleaning open floors. The real challenge is getting under sofas, beds, and cabinets without getting stuck. The X60 needs just over 8 cm of clearance to enter these spaces with its sensor retracted.
The price of that slim body is a 235 ml onboard bin, which is significantly smaller than what we saw on the L40 Ultra (395 ml) and X40 Ultra (350 ml). That means the robot keeps returning to the dock to empty the bin more often than expected in heavy sessions, especially if you have a pet at home. Not a big deal, but the trips do add time.
The slimmer body isn’t the only trick up the X60’s sleeve. Dreame has also upgraded its obstacle-climbing system, allowing the robot to lift itself over raised thresholds and door tracks that might stop a regular robot vacuum. This is particularly useful in Indian homes, where bathrooms, balconies, and even some rooms have raised entrances.
Genuinely, this is a big step-up (pun intended) in the evolution of robot vacuums. But you should ask yourself this question: are the obstacles in your home tall enough to trouble a decent mid-range robot vacuum and require a top-of-the-line robot? So while the X60’s climbing ability is impressive on paper (single thresholds up to 4.5 cm and double-layer steps up to 8.8 cm), how much value it adds depends on the layout of your home. If your existing robot already moves between rooms without getting stuck, this upgrade alone won’t justify spending significantly more. In fact, your home’s layout, flooring, and the presence of pets matter far more than the specifications alone. We’ve covered these and other factors in our robot vacuum cleaner buying guide.
The dock is significantly shorter and wider than the L40 Ultra I tested last, and its gold-accented finish looks more at home in a living room than the matte black L40. The trade-off is the capacity: 4.2 liters of clean water and 3 liters of dirty water, down from 4.5 and 4 liters on the L40. The 3.2-liter dust bag is unchanged.
As I pointed out in my earlier Dreame reviews, the company continues to ship its robot vacuums with a bulky 16A plug, and the X60 Ultra Complete is no exception. Most Indian homes don’t have a 16A socket conveniently located where you’d want to place the docking station, making an adapter or a dedicated socket an unnecessary hassle for such an expensive product.
Cleaning Performance: Does the Extra Power Make a Difference?
Dreame has made a big deal of the X60 Ultra Complete’s suction power of 35,000 Pa, and understandably so. But having reviewed the X40 Ultra (12,000 Pa) and L40 Ultra AE (19,000 Pa), I’ve reached a point where raw suction figures don’t excite me as much as they once did. Both those robots were already capable of keeping my floors clean without much intervention. So with the X60, I was less interested in how much more powerful it was and more curious about whether that extra power translated into noticeably cleaner floors.
On tile and stone floors, the X60 Ultra Complete does an excellent job of picking up everyday dust, crumbs, and pet hair. The extending side brush also does a great job of cleaning along walls and around furniture legs, areas where robot vacuums often leave some dirt behind. Hair handling is noticeably better than on the X40 Ultra, which struggled with long human hair and clumps of dog fur.
Obstacle avoidance is something Dreame has mastered, and it’s no different on the X60. In my month-long testing, it easily avoided the usual suspects like cables, socks, and small toys. But that was the case with the cheaper L40 and X40 vacuums, too. While it handled thick carpets well, light fabric rugs were pulled towards its inlet a couple of times.
Two newer touches stand out on the X60 Ultra. The robot maps the house during its first clean, so there is no separate mapping run. Also, its proactive-light dirt detection spots hair and light liquids and adjusts cleaning. Image processing happens on the device, per Dreame, and the app shows when the camera is active.
Mopping Performance: Where the X60 Makes a Stronger Case
When I interviewed Manu Sharma, the head of Dreame India, he made an interesting observation: for Indians, a house isn’t truly clean until the mopping is done. And that’s where the X60 Ultra Complete brings some meaningful upgrades. Unlike the X40 Ultra and L40 Ultra AE, which used hot water only to wash the mop pads at the dock, the X60 actually mops the floor with water heated to 40°C. The pads spin at up to 230 RPM, apply 15 N of downward pressure, and extend towards walls and furniture legs to clean areas that regular circular mops often miss.
For everyday mopping, the results are quite impressive. Footprints, light spills, and the grime that builds up on floors throughout the day are handled well. Even some dried stains can be removed, although older, stubborn stains may need a second pass or a targeted zone clean. This is one area where the X60 makes a stronger case for its premium pricing, especially if you mop your floors daily rather than occasionally.
There is one catch, though. The X60 tends to leave floors noticeably damp after mopping. Not enough to make them dangerously slippery, but enough for water marks to show up on wooden-finish tiles. Thankfully, you can adjust the water level in the Dreame app, and I’d recommend starting with a lower setting before increasing it if needed. For homes with carpets, the mop pads can lift up to 21.5 mm to avoid wetting them. You can also have the robot leave the pads at the dock when vacuuming carpets, which is the safer option for thicker rugs.
Multifunction Dock: Almost Hands-Free, But Not Quite
A big part of what you’re paying for with the X60 Ultra Complete is its multifunction docking station. Once the robot finishes cleaning, the dock takes over. It empties the dustbin, refills the robot’s water tank, washes the mop pads, and dries them with hot air. This also makes the smaller onboard dustbin less of a concern, as the robot can return to the dock and empty itself whenever needed. It’s the sort of convenience that makes you forget how much work goes into keeping a robot vacuum clean.
But don’t mistake this for a completely hands-free system. During my testing, I had to refill the clean-water tank and empty the dirty-water tank roughly every other day. Your experience will vary depending on the size of your home, how often you mop, and the water settings you use. You’ll also need to replace the dust bag occasionally and clean the dock’s washboard and other parts. Then there are the recurring costs of dust bags, filters, brushes, and cleaning solution. Dreame includes a decent number of spare accessories in the Complete package, which is nice, but you’ll eventually need to buy replacements. For my usage of roughly 800 sqft home, that’s like replenishing every 6 months or so.
The dock itself is fairly large and needs a permanent spot in your home. Make sure there’s enough room to remove the water tanks comfortably, and preferably place it somewhere you won’t have to carry a tank full of dirty water across the house. These might sound like nitpicking, but when you’re spending this much on a robot vacuum, even small inconveniences are worth pointing out.
App and Battery Life: Plenty of Features, Room for Improvement
I’ve said this in my earlier Dreame reviews, and I’ll say it again. The Dreamehome app can do almost anything you want, but finding the right setting can sometimes be a task in itself. The X60 Ultra Complete is no different. You can clean individual rooms, set up no-mop zones, save up to four maps, and control the robot using Alexa, Siri, Google Home, or Dreame’s own “OK Dreame” voice commands. There’s plenty to play around with, but the app could really do with a simpler interface. Stain Recognition is still in beta, while Matter support is something Dreame has promised through a future software update.
There are some new pet-specific features, too. The X60 can recognize pet bowls, give extra attention to areas where pets spend time, and even locate your pet using its camera. You can also use the camera for live video and two-way communication. There’s an Apple Watch app for starting cleaning sessions and checking their status, along with phone widgets for quick access to cleaning routines.
As for battery life, the X60 packs a 6,400 mAh battery, the same capacity as the X40 Ultra and larger than the L40 Ultra AE’s 5,200 mAh unit. However, a bigger battery doesn’t necessarily translate into longer cleaning sessions, especially with all the extra features running. The good news is that charging is much faster than on the L40 Ultra AE. In my testing, charging times ranged from around 90 minutes to just over two hours, compared to roughly three and a half hours for the L40. Battery life itself isn’t particularly impressive for a flagship, especially in larger homes, but the robot can return to its dock, recharge, and resume cleaning from where it stopped. So, unless you’re in a hurry to get the entire house cleaned in one go, this shouldn’t be much of a concern.
Dreame X60 Ultra Complete Verdict: Worth the Price?
At Rs 1,34,999, the Dreame X60 Ultra Complete is not an easy robot vacuum to recommend, especially when the L40 Ultra AE costs less than half as much and already does an excellent job of keeping floors clean. But after spending time with the X60, I can see where the extra money goes. The slimmer design helps it reach places other robots struggle with, the improved obstacle-climbing system is useful for homes with raised thresholds, and the heated-water mopping is a meaningful upgrade over the X40 and L40. Add reliable vacuuming, better hair handling, excellent edge cleaning, and a multifunction dock that takes care of most of the dirty work, and you have a very capable cleaning system.
That doesn’t mean it’s without flaws. Despite the improvements, I still noticed some hair around the rollers. Mopping can leave floors wetter than I’d like, and stubborn stains may need another pass. The smaller 235 ml dustbin means more trips to the dock during heavy cleaning sessions, while battery life is good enough rather than exceptional. The Dreamehome app remains powerful but unnecessarily complicated, and the dock still needs regular attention. And yes, Dreame continues to ship a 16A plug, something I’ve complained about in my previous reviews. These aren’t deal-breakers individually, but they are harder to ignore at this price.
The X60 also faces some serious competition. In India, the Roborock Saros 20, Ecovacs DEEBOT X11 OmniCyclone, and Narwal Flow 2 offer their own take on premium robot cleaning. In the US, the Roborock Saros 20, Ecovacs DEEBOT X12S OmniCyclone, and eufy Omni S2 are worth considering against the X60 Max Ultra Complete. I haven’t personally tested these competing models, so I can’t tell you whether they clean better or worse than the Dreame. But based on their features, they’re certainly worth comparing before spending this kind of money.
And that brings me back to the question I raised at the beginning of this review. Does the X60 Ultra Complete do enough to justify its substantial premium over the L40 Ultra AE? For most homes, probably not. The L40 already handles everyday vacuuming and mopping well enough that the X60’s extra suction and smarter features won’t necessarily translate into noticeably cleaner floors. But if you have low furniture, tricky thresholds, pets that shed a lot, and want the most advanced cleaning system Dreame currently offers, the X60 makes a stronger case. You’re paying less for a dramatic improvement in cleaning and more for the ability to clean difficult areas with less intervention.
If you’re unsure which of these premium features you actually need, try our interactive robot vacuum buying checklist. It lets you choose features based on your home and cleaning needs, so you can decide where it’s worth spending more and where you can save.
The X60 Ultra Complete is an excellent robot vacuum, but it’s also a reminder that the best robot vacuum isn’t necessarily the most expensive one. It’s the one that cleans your home well enough that you stop thinking about cleaning. And Dreame had already come remarkably close to achieving that with its cheaper models.

Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.
Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information "if deemed to be appropriate."
The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.
Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.
At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.
A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.
Three people were killed Monday in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.
Also on Monday, the European Commission proposed a new round of sanctions to keep economic pressure on Moscow, targeting dozens of Russian banks, cracking down on crypto platforms and slapping bans on sports teams and athletes competing under the country's flag.
The proposals, put forward by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, must be endorsed by all 27 European Union member countries before they can enter into force. The process can take weeks, and the planned measures are likely to be modified.
The bloc has already hit more than 4,700 people and entities, including President Vladimir Putin, and several energy companies.
Zelenskyy lauds Ukrainian attacks from Siberia to Libya
Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."
"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.
Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.
An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work Monday after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometers (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack.
Russian officials also reported Monday a Ukrainian attack on industrial sites in Russia's Perm region, more than 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from Ukraine. One person was killed in the attack, and 56 Ukrainian drones were downed, Perm Gov. Dmitri Makhonin said.
"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.
Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that the forces also destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter that was on the Merkury.
Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials.
The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital of Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential matters.
Sunday's attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials, although Zelenskyy claimed it was sunk.
Benghazi residents heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defense units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.
The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of an agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.
The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the U.N. Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch the attack.
Libyan officials say 2 sea drones hit Russian warship
Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told AP that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.
At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.
Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition aboard the Merkury.
Hours after the warship attack, another sea drone strike hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel sailing off Benghazi, the Libyan coast guard said.
The Russian cargo ship was sanctioned, Ukraine says
Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, while the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.
The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a "mother ship" near the target, the SBU said.
Russian defenses tried to intercept the attacking drones, it said.
"Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes," the SBU said.

I've been testing smart bird feeders for more than two years in my own backyard, and Birdfy has been—and still is—the brand I trust and recommend most. These feeders are well-made, reliable, and reasonably priced. The brand's app is also excellent; it's easy to navigate and use without shelling out for an additional subscription. Better still, Birdfy just rolled out free lifetime AI ID (which is quite decent) with any bird feeder, including the lowest-priced models. If you don't want to gift a traditional feeder, you might consider Birdfy's smart birdbath and nesting box, each of which comes equipped with the same high-quality camera(s).
Below are the models I've tested—in some cases for years—and recommend, including a couple I personally plan to buy as gifts this year.
Featured Gifts
The One That Started It All
WIRED first reviewed this feeder in 2022. Back then we loved the concept, but felt its AI ID didn't quite cut it. Birdfy has come a long way since then on the AI front. The feeder body is largely the same, but the app and AI ID (now free) are both much improved, offering a seamless and user-friendly experience that makes it easy to sort through which birds visited that day. This once-pricey feeder is now at the lowest price I have ever seen for the version without the solar panel. The 5200-mAh rechargeable battery lasts a few weeks, but I think it's convenient to not have to bring it in to charge, if you want to spring for the extra $20 for that solar panel.
A Solid Budget Option
Birdfy's “beginner” model, this unit is basically a gravity pet feeder with a camera on the side. All you need to do is snap three pieces together, charge the camera, and pair it to the Birdfy app. If you know anyone who loves birds but is intimidated by the thought of having to set up and calibrate a smart bird feeder, this could be the perfect gift for them. However, note that my test unit keeps losing its lid on windy days, and there's no roof to keep the seed from getting wet on rainy days, so it's probably best for summer use. I also just discovered that Walmart carries an exclusive periwinkle color that looks lovely.
New and Improved
Birdfy's Metal 2 4K is the brand's flagship release for this year, with Ultra 4K resolution and dual-band (2.4 GHz and 5.0 GHz) Wi-Fi connection. The metal body claims to resist squirrels, and the muted green color is a welcome change from Birdfy's usual bright plastics. As was the case with the brand's previous flagship, the Feeder 2 Pro, I had some significant connection issues with the Metal 2 4K. This kept it from being a top pick in my guide to the Best Smart Bird Feeders, but the model is still worth a mention here due to its combination of features and build quality, as well as Birdfy's excellent customer service if something does go wrong.
Best Looking
Smart bird feeders aren't always the most aesthetically pleasing thing you could put in your yard, but Birdfy's 2K bamboo model was the first smart feeder I've ever had that actually garnered compliments. The natural wood and waterfall-style black roof complement any landscaping or exterior decor, and the camera and overall setup ran flawlessly for me during my months of testing. Just make sure you apply varnish or urethane regularly to the bamboo, as the finish on mine peeled after only two months in mild weather.
A Smart Birdbath
This interesting product pairs a plastic birdbath (on an optional metal stand) with a solar-powered camera, so you can keep an eye on visiting birds without having to deal with seed mess. When I first tested it, I was worried birds would splash water on the camera lens, but the most popular activity at the bath is by far drinking the water (birds, raccoons, squirrels … anything passing by). I don't love that the basin grows algae quickly and the pump clogs easily, but this is otherwise a very well-made item—it's been in my yard for a year and a half through every season, and while the plastic is starting to fade a bit, it's still going strong.
A Smart Nesting Box
Though I do love a smart bird feeder, Birdfy's Nest Duo is the absolute zenith of bird-watching for me. A black-capped chickadee moved in, laid eggs, and raised chicks (detailed here), and the cameras and app on the Nest stayed working, giving me 24-hour updates with interior night vision and views of the entry hole's exterior to see who was coming and going. A remote control on a 10-foot-long cord lets you reset or charge the camera without bothering the birds (though the auxiliary solar panel worked great for me). Note, however, that the black waterfall-style roof and lack of ventilation do pose a risk of overheating any young birds; during a May heat wave, I had to affix an umbrella and ice packs to the box, but the interior thermometer and hygrometer did a great job keeping me abreast of changing conditions.

Minister alleges political backing for Messi event deal, says probe will expose those responsible
Thrissur , Sports Minister O J Janeesh on Monday alleged that the irregularities in the failed visit of the Lionel Messi-led Argentina football team to Keralam during the previous LDF government were politically driven, and that the SIT probe is in the right direction.
After the UDF government came to power, it constituted a Special Investigation Team to probe the irregularities.
The SIT on Saturday named former Sports Minister V Abdurahiman, his former private secretary C Sathyapalan and former Kerala State Sports Council president U Sharafali as accused in the case.
The SIT had earlier registered the case against the sponsoring company and its managing director.
Sharafali had claimed that his football academy in Malappuram received a ₹2 crore investment from the company that sponsored the Messi event.
Speaking to reporters, Janeesh said the SIT probing alleged irregularities in the event was progressing in the right direction and would bring out who was behind the decisions that led to the agreement.
"It was not something that happened solely because a Sports Council president wanted it or because the Sports Minister's office decided so. There was political ownership behind the agreement. Who provided that political ownership will come out clearly in the investigation," he said.
He said the previous government's political leadership had a responsibility in the matter, as former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan had repeatedly announced that Messi would visit Keralam and assured people that the event would take place.
Such assurances had created confidence among those willing to invest money in the event and facilitated the financial transactions, he said.
Janeesh said the issue was not merely whether the government had suffered a direct financial loss. "The government machinery was fully utilised for this. The time of senior officials and the government system was devoted to the event. That itself amounts to a loss to the government," he said.
He said the most important question was whether the government machinery had been used to facilitate private financial transactions.
If such misuse had taken place, everyone who had assisted in it should come within the scope of the investigation, he said.
The minister also referred to allegations against Sharafali, whose sports academy reportedly received ₹2 crore as an investment from the sponsor of the proposed event.
Janeesh said Sharafali had allegedly signed an agreement between the sponsor and an international agency to organise the Messi event even before the state government granted approval.
The agreement was reportedly signed two days before the government approval, with Sharafali signing in his official capacity as Sports Council president, he said.
He said money was subsequently transferred to an account linked to Sharafali's institution and was allegedly moved to other accounts.
Janeesh said the circumstances surrounding the agreement and the financial transactions warranted a detailed investigation.
He maintained that the government had not interfered in the probe and called for a transparent and effective investigation.
He rejected the Opposition's allegation that the investigation was being delayed, saying the matter required careful examination and could not be concluded in a week merely to satisfy public sentiment.
Janeesh also said the Sports Department's report had pointed to inadequate preparations, shortcomings in the movement of files, and misuse of government machinery.
He said that the lack of transparency surrounding the arrangements was one of the reasons for initiating an SIT investigation.
He said the SIT should examine the allegations and counter-arguments and that the investigation should establish the political and administrative responsibility for the decisions and transactions linked to the failed event.

US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
- Published
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.
The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.
The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.
When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.
Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.
China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.
On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.
On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".
The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.
The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.
China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.
Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.
Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.
Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.
Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.
Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.
That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.
Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.
Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.
Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take.
The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.
In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.
Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

PM Modi, Nepal’s Balen Shah to hold talks today, inaugurate Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link, other key projects
Balen Shah was received on his arrival in Delhi by union minister Jitin Prasada, and his first official engagement was a meeting with EAM Jaishankar.
Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Sunday began his first visit to India, during which the two sides are looking to reset the overall relationship and conclude agreements to deepen cooperation in areas such as energy, connectivity, railways, infrastructure, technology, human resource development and climate change.
This is also Shah’s first bilateral foreign visit, reflecting the importance attached by both sides to their ties, and his talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday are expected to provide political direction for charting the course for the bilateral partnership for the coming years, and explore new avenues of cooperation.
Shah, 36, was received on his arrival in New Delhi by minister of state for commerce Jitin Prasada, and his first official engagement was a meeting with external affairs minister S Jaishankar, who said on social media that India “cherishes the special friendship” with Nepal. The Nepal Prime Minister’s Office said they discussed aspects of bilateral ties, especially cooperation in connectivity, trade, transit, commerce, energy, culture, education and people-to-people ties.

While Modi and Shah have interacted over phone and exchanged social messages, their first in-person meeting on Monday will set the stage for a much-needed reset in the relationship following the Gen Z uprising in 2025 that unseated KP Sharma Oli’s government and led to the rapper-turned-politician and a younger generation of leaders from the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP).
The two PMs will virtually inaugurate India-backed connectivity and energy initiatives that have been completed and lay foundation stones for some new projects, people familiar with the matter said. Several “forward-looking” agreements and understandings in different areas will also be concluded, they said.
The major outcomes are expected to be in areas such as development cooperation, hydropower, connectivity, railways, climate change, disaster resilience, infrastructure, and technology, and a rail link between Ayodhya and Janakpur is also expected to be unveiled.
Shah’s visit comes at an opportune time as there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of India and Nepal in terms of economic growth, social development, infrastructure expansion, adoption of technology, and addressing challenges such as natural disasters and climate change, the people said. The discussions between Modi and Shah will provide political direction for charting the future of the bilateral relationship over the coming years, they said.
While the Indian side has proposed a joint vision for the long-term development of bilateral ties, the Nepalese side has sought a $2-billion economic package, including $1 billion in grants and aid for reconstruction of areas devastated by the Bhote Koshi flash floods in August. Nepal has also asked for the Kathmandu-Mahendranagar air corridor to be made two-way. International flights are currently permitted only to leave Nepal via this route.
Shah is accompanied by a 35-member delegation that includes foreign minister Shishir Khanal, finance minister Swarnim Wagle, several senior advisers to the PM, and business representatives. The Nepal-India Business Forum will be held during the visit, during which Shah is expected to seek more investments from India.
India and Nepal share a unique and comprehensive relationship characterised by open borders, mutual trust, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties. They also have more than 40 bilateral institutional mechanisms to advance cooperation in different sectors.
India is Nepal’s largest trade, transit and investment partner. Nepal enjoys duty-free access to Indian markets, while India is also the country’s biggest export destination and receives almost 80 per cent of Nepal’s exports. India is the largest source of foreign investment in Nepal, accounting for almost a third of the total FDI.
The Indian side has implemented more than 600 high impact community development projects, worth more than Nepali ₹1,662 crores, across 74 districts of Nepal. Major connectivity projects include cross-border railway lines, a petroleum product pipeline, and integrated check posts.
Besides providing support after the Gorkha earthquake of 2015 that resulted in the reconstruction of 50,000 houses, 71 educational projects and 128 health facilities, India provided humanitarian assistance and disaster relief after the flash floods in August this year, including 140 tonnes of emergency supplies.

Staffers at the Internet Archive, the nonprofit “digital library” that runs the Wayback Machine, are voting to join the Communications Workers of America (CWA).
More than 80 of the 124 eligible US staffers voted in favor of unionizing, and they are currently awaiting voluntary recognition of the union from Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle. Kahle did not immediately respond to WIRED’s request for comment. If Kahle does not grant voluntary recognition, employees will vote whether to certify the union in a process run by the National Labor Relations Board.
The Internet Archive, which also offers free catalogs preserving tens of millions of digital and physical media items, was founded by Kahle in 1996. Kahle’s mission was to provide “Universal Access to All Knowledge.” Will Howes, an Internet Archive engineer, says that the organizing process has demonstrated how “aligned” employees are in their passion for Kahle’s goals.
“Frankly, we really see the formation of this union as accepting [Kahle’s] challenge to make this workplace the best place it can be in pursuit of a mission, universal access to all knowledge,” Howes tells WIRED.
Microfiche digitization technician Danielle Leard tells WIRED that the union is “very optimistic” that Kahle will voluntarily recognize it and come to the bargaining table. They add that among the union’s core goals are securing wage increases and additional benefits, and ensuring that these benefits are consistently available to employees across the company.
“We believe the first and most primary goal of our union is to make sure that the Internet Archive reflects the wants and values of the people that work there, and the people that make the archive,” Leard says.
Howes and Leard tell WIRED that the Internet Archive—which claims to have archived more than 1 trillion web pages—employs a highly diverse set of workers, including librarians, engineers, physical media specialists, and facility coordinators who maintain the archive’s building, a former Christian Scientist church in San Francisco. Leard says that the staff’s diversity has made the organizing process, which began in February 2025, “a unique challenge,” but one that’s “really rewarding.”
The vote comes slightly more than two months after staffers at the Wikimedia Foundation, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia, voted to join CWA. Howes says the simultaneous efforts are “very powerful” given that both organizations represent “core infrastructure” of the internet.
Howes says that the union wants to ensure that the 30-year-old project continues to thrive in the long term—and that its workers do too. Leard says this means providing paths for developing skills and getting promoted within the nonprofit.
Leard says that the Internet Archive’s unionization drive is especially important in the present moment, amid waves of tech layoffs and widespread anxiety about “emerging technologies” like AI.
The Internet Archive hasn’t been immune from the consequences of AI. A Nieman Lab report from January found that some news websites, struggling to prevent companies like OpenAI or Anthropic from harvesting their articles, have started blocking web crawlers from the Internet Archive, arguing it gives AI companies a back door to their content. (The archive relies on web crawlers to preserve news articles in near-real time.)
Leard says that ideally, the Internet Archive’s unionization will be “one domino” in a larger process that makes the tech industry better.
“We're hoping,” they say, “that we'll continue to be one of the blueprints that will make it easier for other organizations and companies in the future to continue to unionize.”
Update: 11/20/26 1:43pm ET: This story has been updated to reflect that Internet Archive workers have voted in favor of unionizing, but the union has not yet been recognized by Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle.

Listening to the in-game radio stations while you cruise around in Grand Theft Auto VI, you might hear a recruitment ad for the Vice City Police Department, which makes no secret of the kind of maladjusted psychos it's looking for.
“Have you always dreamed of abusing your power without consequence?” one spot begins. “Well, now you can, when you join the Vice City Police Department, VCPD. You’ll have fun learning the ins and outs of applying excessive force.” The commercial goes on to suggest that cadets will be trained in racial profiling and planting evidence.
Given that blistering analysis of American law enforcement, you might imagine that actual cops aren’t big fans of the latest GTA title, which was released after a 13-year wait on Thursday. Yet as millions of gamers have started to explore every stash house and back alley in the sun-drenched wilderness of a fictionalized South Florida, even police departments have attempted to exploit this monocultural mania to elevate their public messaging or recruit new officers.
It’s a curious strategy given that the series rewards theft and drug dealing while enticing you to run over pedestrians, but evidently the mere presence of law enforcement in the games (as the primary antagonists, mind you) was enough to inspire waves of AI slop celebrating the thin blue line.
An Instagram channel of the San Diego Police Department, for example, on Thursday posted an AI-generated image of an SDPD cruiser set against a sunset over the San Diego Bay. Its neon pinks and purples match the saturated aesthetic of GTA, and in case there was any doubt what the department was going for, the nonsensical phrase “Join San Diego PD VI” appears at the top. “Want to drive a police car, we can make that happen!” reads the caption. “Apply Now!”
Another police department in Washington state shared GTA-like imagery on its Instagram page, encouraging viewers to try “the real-life version” of GTA VI by pursuing a career in law enforcement. “No cheat codes,” the caption advertised. “No respawns. Just real people, real challenges, and a career that makes a difference.” A wave of self-serious GTA slop also flooded the feeds of police departments in Canada, from Edmonton to Toronto—though the Calgary Police Service tried something more lighthearted by having one of their traffic officers react to clips of dangerous and illegal driving maneuvers in the game.
Among police departments that were not seeking to add to their ranks through GTA VI fever, many posted content aimed at reminding people that laws exist in real life. “Keep It In The Game VI,” advised a typical post on the Instagram account of the Glendale Police Department in California, complete with a GTA-fied police cruiser and view of the city. “Follow posted speed limits, respect the law, and keep your wanted level at ZERO!” the caption warned. The Denver Police Department, in similarly scolding fashion, informed followers: “Grand theft auto is still illegal.”
The communications teams for these agencies should have perhaps reconsidered trying to farm engagement and clout from the massive success of GTA VI. As many commenters are noting, the game portrays cops as corrupt and quick to violence. Players have discovered that the Vice City squad will brutalize you if you start filming them during a questionable arrest. One clip showed a cop pulling his weapon on a character who had done nothing worse than stand in the street to take a selfie.
A certain dose of this authoritarian cruelty ought to appeal to the right-wing cranks upset that GTA VI is too “woke” when it comes to gender, race, and politics overall. It’s a little different when the most visible villains of the game are choosing to overlook its vicious take on their profession in order to spam epic social media posts.
Fox News, just for comparison, dutifully took the tired law-and-order line on GTA VI, with talking heads aghast at kids’ exposure to virtual gun violence (never mind actual gun deaths in the US) and an atmosphere of moral depravity. Elon Musk famously declared that he couldn’t play GTA games because they compelled you to shoot cops.
Both stances, however insincere, suggest a modicum of regard for law enforcement that the police departments themselves immediately jettisoned in favor of GTA cringe. They of course won’t win any cool points for it, but at least this way they can pretend to connect with the general population.
More baffling still is that the Russian army has generated its own GTA VI recruitment ads to blast out on its Telegram channel, and NATO has trumpeted its defensive security alliance with military-industrial GTA sludge, boasting that “even the best gamers would have a challenge” eluding fighter jets and submarines. Trying to parse Vice President JD Vance’s depiction of a Trumpian “golden age” with GTA graphics is a fool’s errand. In the most dystopian development of all, a US Army battalion in Georgia granted 43 eligible soldiers four days off to play the new GTA in return for reenlisting for another two years of service.
What do any of these institutions or their missions have to do with a video game where you rob convenience stores in flip-flops? Doesn’t matter. When the zeitgeist is this all-consuming, you fire up ChatGPT and find an angle, no matter how confusing. Surely someone, somewhere, will be tricked into thinking you have anything to do with it.

Zosia Mamet recently revealed that her “absolutely horrible” experience working with showrunner and producer Matthew Weiner on the set of “Mad Men” caused her to quit the series after just five episodes.
“All the other actors were wonderful, but he really was like the Catholic Church back in the day, like that bro rules with fear,” she said while appearing on Dax Shepard’s “Armchair Expert” podcast on Monday. “He would dart every table read with this little speech… and he would talk about how he didn’t want any of us to take our scripts home… And he would be like, ‘If I see that, I’m going to find you, and I’m going to hunt you down. I’m going to kill you. Just kidding. Actually not. He would do this at every table read. And I was like, this not only isn’t funny, but it’s yucky. It’s fucking yucky, man.”
Mamet, who appeared on Season 4 and 5 of the hit drama as Joyce Ramsay, then recounted the moment that pushed her to quit the show, explaining that “he came in and was having a bad day and decided to set his sights on me.” “During a block rehearsal, [he] just fucking went to town on me in front of the whole cast and crew… I called my agents when I left, and I was like, ‘I can’t go back to that set,’” she told Shepard. “He just systematically dressed me down for like 45 minutes. And I was like, ‘I want to kill myself.’”
She continued: “My level of insecurity was so great that I knew that I wouldn’t be able [to]. I was like, I will shut down,” Mamet said. “I won’t be able to function in this environment, and the fear of that happening again was just too great.”
The “Girls” actress had previously written about the showrunner in her 2025 essay collection, “Does This Make Me Funny?,” though she didn’t name him at the time. “I wrote an essay about it for my book where I don’t mention names,” Mamet said. “But I really wanted Matt Weiner to sue me because then he would be admitting to the fact that he knew I was writing about him.”
Reps for Weiner did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), under the Ministry of Home Affairs, has advised users to avoid exchanging official, financial, confidential, or other sensitive information through WhatsApp Web, warning that active browser sessions could be misused to access their accounts. In a recent advisory, I4C’s National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) said such access could allow attackers to read messages, impersonate account holders, and access contacts and group conversations. They could then exploit the account holder’s trusted identity for fraud, phishing, and social engineering. The agency urged users to exercise particular caution on office computers, shared systems, public computers, and devices accessible to other people. It also stressed that closing a browser tab or window should not be treated as logging out of WhatsApp Web. Notably, WhatsApp Web allows users to access the messaging service through a computer browser after linking their account. Precautions For Web Users I4C has recommended the following measures: Avoid sensitive work: Government, organisational, financial, confidential, or other sensitive information should preferably not be exchanged through WhatsApp Web on computers. Limit active sessions: Avoid leaving WhatsApp Web logged in when it is not required, particularly on office or shared computers. Log out manually: Log out after completing your work rather than simply closing the browser tab or window. Use private browsing cautiously: If temporary access is unavoidable, use incognito or private browsing mode on a trusted computer and manually log out before closing the browser. Avoid untrusted computers: Do not access WhatsApp Web from cyber cafes, public kiosks, hotel business centres, borrowed computers, or other untrusted systems. Watch for unusual activity: Treat unexpected messages sent from your account, unusual replies from contacts, or unexplained activity seriously. Keep devices secure: Update operating systems, browsers, and security software, and avoid suspicious downloads, unknown files, pirated software, and untrusted applications. The warning follows an earlier I4C alert about a fraud campaign targeting company directors, finance professionals, and businesspersons through WhatsApp account takeovers. In August, the agency described how attackers circulated malicious ZIP files disguised as account statements or communications from the RBI and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs. Opening the files on a Windows computer installed malware that could hijack an active WhatsApp Web session. I4C advised companies to independently verify urgent fund-transfer instructions or requests to change bank account details through a direct voice call or in-person confirmation before acting. Separately, I4C has also flagged the use of AI agents in attacks targeting financial institutions. The agency recently warned banks, NBFCs, and fintech startups about attackers exploiting unpatched software and misconfigured internet-facing servers to access financial infrastructure. The warnings also come amid efforts to strengthen safeguards on messaging platforms. It was reported last month that platforms including WhatsApp and Telegram were preparing to implement the Department of Telecommunications’ SIM-binding mandate.

Meet the young authors! A literacy program inspires kids in South Africa
JOHANNESBURG — It's an ordinary Saturday morning in Alexandra township, known simply as Alex or sometimes dubbed Gomora, a reference to the biblical city of Gomorrah that was known for its wickedness.
That nickname stems from Alexandra's high crime rates. It's a high-density area, where modest brick houses and tin shacks stretch as far as the eye can see and rotting garbage piles up along potholed streets.
But that image doesn't intrude on an event at a small building at the Kwabhekilanga Sports Ground. There's a palpable sense of excitement. Something different is happening this weekend and community members have turned up for it.
It's a book launch for a collection entitled From Gomora to the World. Stories from Alex. The seven stories in the self-published anthology have been written by children from the township who attend a free weekly literacy program.
South Africa is in the midst of a literacy crisis, with one international study showing a majority of 10-year-olds — some 81% — are unable to read for meaning in any of South Africa's 12 official languages.
The grassroots program Read Alex has been trying to change this, offering a weekend reading club, mainly in English, to instill a love of books in children. Launched by the Run Alex Athletics Club, it has about 50 participants. Among the activities: an annual public speaking competition, two spelling bees and a book drive on Mandela Day every year that brings in about 500 volumes — some of which the kids take home and some of which go to libraries.
Now, not only are the children getting to practice their reading, some of them have tried their hand at writing their own stories.
The newly published authors sit up front, ready to sign the pile of freshly-printed books for sale and answer questions about their process.
Thirteen-year-old Fiona Mogane, the bespectacled author of "Lindani's Modelling Journey," is one of them.
"It's about a girl who discovered a lot of challenges throughout her journey," Fiona explains. One of those challenges is that the main character Lindani's mother is an alcoholic, spending what little money the family has on drink — including government grant money meant for her daughter's welfare. She also shouts at her daughter a lot, and sometimes Lindani worries she will follow in her mother's footsteps.
Fiona writes: "Sometimes a thought intrudes on Lindani's mind, telling her that if she took some alcohol, it would make her feel better and stand up for herself …. However Lindani always pulls herself out of that thought: she knows she is stronger than that."
Phelelisa Somana, one of the coordinators of the book project, says she was impressed with the maturity of Fiona's story.
"When I read her story it had a very deep theme that I didn't expect a child to delve into in a way that she did," says Somana.
It "definitely just reminded me just how much kids are a lot smarter than they think they are," she adds. "They notice a lot more than they think they do."
Learning "Ubuntu"
Fortunately, Fiona's tale has a happy ending. Dreaming of becoming the next Miss South Africa, her character Lindani decides to try and raise the money she needs to enter a modelling contest by baking scones and selling them to her neighbors.
"She believes deep down inside that each one of her homemade scones has something special that makes them really delicious," Fiona writes.
In the end, Lindani makes enough cash to enter the contest. She comes in second place and is crowned "princess."
"She is happy because she has proved to herself that she can make a way when it initially seemed there was none," Fiona writes.
In real life, Fiona — also keen on modeling — is being raised in Alex by a single mom. Alex has high crime rates and poor government services like water and electricity. The young teenager is all too familiar with the problems, but she says there are good things about township life too..
"Alex is a crowded place, but when you're in Alex, you can learn a lot of things," she explains. "You can learn how to have Ubuntu."
Ubuntu is an African philosophy centering on community well-being and shared responsibility. As Fiona puts it: "Ubuntu is to help other people when they are in need."
Fiona, whose favorite subject at school is English, says she'd like to go to university, maybe to study medicine. And there's another dream too.
"One day, if I grow up, I want to build a big house that will be having a room with its own books," she says.
Homes without books
Fiona didn't grow up with books at home. Two-thirds of South African children don't have books at home, according to one study by UNICEF.
They won't necessarily find them at school either.
Only about 15% of public schools in South Africa have a functioning library, according to government data.
The dire state of child literacy has its roots in the home. Many children have weak early learning foundations, according to the UNICEF study, and they have no exposure to books before starting primary school.
"When I became the minister of basic education in 2024 I was confronted by the statistic of 80% of 10-year-olds who cannot read for meaning in any language," Basic Education Minister Siviwe Gwarube told NPR.
The minister says the government is trying to tackle this problem by getting more kids into early learning programs.
"We're investing ten billion rand [$58 million] over the next three years on a massive haul out of early childhood development centers," Gwarube says.
Tebogo Selekane, an English teacher at Kwa-bhekilanga secondary school, says the weekend program at Read Alex has helped some of her students a lot. Two of her students have stories in the book.
"They are doing very well in reading," says Selekane. "There's a lot of change in them... they will respond back with confidence."
A country of storytellers
At the book launch, Wandile Mathe, a 21-year-old South African writer and joint coordinator of the project, says despite South Africa's poor literacy rates, the children he coaches come from a nation of storytellers.
"I think South Africans are natural storytellers," he says. "There's always gossip going around anyway."
"In the taxi, at the line, in a shop, wherever you go, there's always someone willing to tell you a story, whether about their personal life or the things that they're seeing around," he laughs. "We're huge social commentators. Nothing will pass by and we will not comment."
The kids who contributed to the book are true to this storytelling tradition, borrowing from their lives and what they see daily in the township. As well as Fiona's story about poverty and alcoholism, there are tales about peer pressure, dangerous men on the street, losing parents and inability to pay school fees.
But it's not all doom and gloom. The heroes and heroines all find ways to overcome the obstacles, learning important lessons and making friends along the way.
For example, one of the young authors, 13-year-old Anita Maloka, wrote a story about a rural girl who moves to Johannesburg to attend school and dreams of becoming a scientist. But the school is not what she hoped.
"Sometimes two students had to squeeze together on one chair. Textbooks were scarce," she writes. The family doesn't have the money to send her anywhere better though, so the character works toward earning a scholarship at a school that "has a real science lab and an entire room just for learning to program computers and building robots."
Like her character, Anita, who dreams of becoming a marine biologist, is also working toward getting a scholarship that will take her out of the township.
But she stresses that life in Alex is "not just about struggle."
"It's about children who want to travel, to explore and dream and make their dreams come true," she says.
