Two attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have killed 4 workers responding to the Ebola outbreak and injured 5 others.
The attacks occurred overnight on a shared living camp in Biakato Mines and an Ebola response coordination office in Mangina.
“We are heartbroken that people have died in the line of duty as they worked to save others,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organization Director-General. “The world has lost brave professionals.”
The dead include a member of a vaccination team, two drivers and a police officer. No WHO staff are among those killed, one staff member was injured.
“My heart goes out to the family and friends of the first responders killed in these attacks,” said Dr Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa. “We are doing everything possible to bring the injured and front-line workers in the impacted areas to safety. These constant attacks must stop. We will continue to work with the DRC Government, partners and MONUSCO to ensure the security of our staff and other health workers.”
In the last week, there were 7 cases of Ebola, down from a peak of over 120 per week in April 2019.
“Ebola was retreating. These attacks will give it force again, and more people will die as a consequence,” said Dr Tedros. “It will be tragic to see more unnecessary suffering in communities that have already suffered so much. We call on everyone who has a role to play to end this cycle of violence.”
The situation is still evolving. WHO will provide updates as new information comes in.

Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario. That includes Mother's Day, her birthday, Christmas, Hanukkah, or any other holiday in your family's life that includes gift-giving. The holiday season is right around the corner, and I've added a few gift ideas with that time of year in mind.
If you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love. From wellness gadgets that can improve her skin to the best tote bags I've tried, and even a device that puts her digital calendar in an IRL device, moms everywhere can get a ton out of these gifts. Many of these are items I've given to my mother, or other WIRED staffers have given to theirs. Or they might be at the top of my own wish list as a mother of a 4-year-old.
Updated October 2026: I've added new gifts to this guide, including Nora Fleming stoneware, jewelry from Gorjana and BaubleBar, Rumpl’s Gametime Puffy Blanket, The Zero Proof's Pampered Pregnancy Pack, and Mina Baie's Emmy Diaper Bag, and have ensured up-to-date links and prices.
Featured Gifts
Next-Level Skin (and Scalp) Care
The must-have gadget for women of almost any age is an LED mask. These masks promise to use red light to erase wrinkles, brighten your skin, and keep acne at bay. I haven't seen much change in my wrinkles in my year-plus of regularly using a red light mask, but I can confirm it makes my skin brighter and calms down acne and scars much faster when I'm regularly treating my skin. HigherDose is a favorite mask of mine because the three-strap design lets it hang on my head rather than squeeze it, making it one of the most comfortable masks I've worn.
My other favorite LED tool actually sits on my head and also comes from HigherDose. The brand's Red Light Hat treats your head with red light to rejuvenate your scalp and hair follicles for better hair growth, and as someone with a sensitive scalp and a hair-pulling problem, using this cap regularly genuinely improved my scalp and hair. It's the healthiest it's ever been, and my scalp is the least itchy, too. I love that this hat also has a battery pack, so I can comfortably wear it anywhere while I treat my head.
A Cool Tote
Look, nothing says mom life like looking for the perfect bag. I'm in a massive tote phase of my life; I somehow need to either lug an armload of items for myself and my son (or just myself!) or I only need a tiny belt bag. There's no in between.
The Yardsale Day Bag has been my go-to for a variety of needs, from a stylish personal item for a flight to a gym bag to the aerial studio. It's got a waterproof bottom that makes me happy to bring it to the zoo's splash pad, and a magnetic middle separator you can flex to separate the middle of the bag into two medium sections to better divide all your items. Plus, there are a handful of side pockets inside, but none are large enough for my massive Owala water bottle. I have the 30L in Butter, but there's also a smaller 20L version if you're looking for something a little more compact.
If your mom wants something a little more stylish, the Alex Mill totes are always on my mind. They come in a variety of gorgeous colors and are made of coated canvas, so they can put up with daily adventures, and you can customize them with your mom's initials (or even just the word “mom”!) with Alex Mill's hand-painted letter service. It's a simpler tote with no other pockets, but you can use the top snaps to let out the sides or tuck them in, depending on how much space Mom needs on a given day. The weathered color and vibe of these bags also feel perfect for the fall season.
Her Google Calendar IRL
My latest favorite family planning gadget is a digital wall calendar. These handy devices take the Google Calendar I live by (and just about any other digital calendar, if your mom isn't a Google girl) and put it on a physical device I can quickly tap into without needing to grab my phone or bark at Alexa. The Skylight Calendar 2 is my favorite, because it not only includes to-do lists, meal planning, and a recipe book but also doubles as a digital photo frame. That means it displays cute photos of my family most of the time, and then, with a simple tap, it opens the calendar or whatever page I was last on to show me what's on my family's schedule. It does have a subscription fee, though, to get the digital photo frame feature and a few other options, like meal planning. But I think it's well worth it to get so many features in a single device. You can also gift her kiddo a Skylight Buddy ($140) so that she doesn't have to remind them to check the main calendar for their chores; it'll appear on their own device if they have a Buddy.
For the Hostess Mom
If Mom loves entertaining—or just being festive—but doesn’t want to have to store a million different dishes, Nora Fleming’s modular serving-tray system is for her. First, pick a base—there are trays, baking dishes, utensil crocks, and even salt and pepper shakers. Then, pick one of dozens of hand-painted “Minis,” or ceramic accents (sold separately). There are holiday themes, sports team themes, and even ones for specific events like mah-jongg or BBQs.
Each base has a hole into which you can attach the Mini with a little rubber stopper. I tested the cracker tray with a harvest-themed Mini, and you wouldn’t know the tray didn’t come with the accent already attached. At the end of next month, I plan to swap it out for a Christmas tree Mini, and so on. Best part is that if Mom likes this setup, you’ll be set on gifts for the foreseeable future, provided you can keep finding new Minis you think she’ll like. —Kat Merck
Personalized Jewelry
For years, the go-to gift for a woman in my family, mother or not, was shopping in the jewelry section of a department store. My mom even helped orchestrate this for the rest of the aunties and grandmas, but now, as a mom myself, I find myself interested in jewelry that tells a story about my family and children instead of just any old set. (Except extra earrings for my earring stack, a gift I'm thrilled to get, because there's never enough.)
I love these pieces from Gorjana and BaubleBar that you can customize. Gorjana has a ton of charms you can add to its necklaces or bracelets to reflect Mom’s kids’ initials, birthstones, or anything else; I paired a charm of my son’s first initial ($48) with the Wilshire Adjustable Necklace ($65). If she's more of a ring gal, BaubleBar's Toi et Moi ring ($78) lets you choose two birthstones to display. I chose my and my son's birthstones, but luckily his sibling-to-be will also have a red birthstone, so it'll remain a perfect reflection of my kids and me for years to come.
For the Sports Moms
This item was literally made for sports moms: a padded stadium cushion with a wearable blanket inside. My son plays on three sports teams, so I do a lot of sitting outside on bleachers and turf sidelines—and often at night, when it’s freezing. I’ve tried many things to keep warm, from heated jackets to HotHands, but nothing has worked as well as this water-resistant blanket, which unfurls to 50 x 70 inches and sports a clip at the front so you can wear it like a cape. It can also be used for picnics or as a spot for younger siblings to sit and read during tournaments. It’s also not hard to fold it back up and fit it inside the seat part (which is 1 inch thick without the blanket inside). It comes in six colors, so you can be sure to find one that matches your giftee’s kid’s team or school colors. —Kat Merck
If She’s Going Non-Alc
If a mom in your life is exploring her nonalcoholic drink options, The Zero Proof has some gift sets perfect to give so she can try out several things at once. I'm currently grounded from drinking any cocktails while I'm pregnant, but moms (and people in general) can have all kinds of reasons to want to explore unique, interesting drinks that are sans alcohol. I really liked this set for how many cool drinks it exposed me to, from bottles of nonalcoholic wine to knockoff cocktails. If you're looking to spend a little less, my favorites so far have been the Château del Ish Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Espumante ($20) and Lapo's Non-Alcoholic Melograno Mule ($20 for four).
For the Reader
Look, I love a Kindle, but if you want to get the best e-reader for your buck (or maybe she just wants an e-reader that isn't a Kindle), the answer is actually a Kobo. My favorite is the Kobo Libra Colour. It's cheaper than the Kindle Colorsoft and can also double as a digital notebook if you add on the $70 stylus. I also prefer Kobo's annotating options: You can write right on the pages instead of in weird pop-up margins and boxes only on Kindle. Kobo also has a page-turner remote ($34), which I love to pair with a pillow stand holder so I can lean back and relax without holding up my e-reader while I read. I gave a similar pillow stand to my mom, and now I can spot her last reading spot easily because that pillow is resting there.
You could also gift her one of the new Kindles if she's a Kindle addict. Many of my friends are drooling over the new purple Ube color of the 12th-gen Kindle ($149), but my personal favorite is the Kindle Aluminum (I just wish it were cheaper!). There's also finally going to be a Kindle page-turn remote, the Kindle Click ($35).
A Beautiful Diaper Backpack
I love a backpack when I'm on the move with my 4-year-old, but one thing that annoys me is that things are hard to find inside, because packs are typically so deep. That's why I adore the Mina Baie Emmy Diaper Bag: It's a wide, shallow bag instead of a long one, making it easy to open and see most of what I store in it without digging around. I'm not toting diapers at the moment, but I've used it to pack a ton of snacks, toys, and spare clothing for my kid.
I'm intrigued to see how using it with two kids goes—I chose the Emmy Midi, which is the midsize bag, but if you're a pumping parent or need to carry a ton of bottles with formula, you might want to try the larger Emmy Full. The stylish bag is made of vegan leather and can be converted from crossbody to tote to backpack mode, depending on which straps you use. Mina Baie doesn't include a changing kit, but sells one separately ($59) if you'd like to include it in your gift (or buy that as the gift to upgrade their existing bag of choice).
For the Expecting Mom
I'm expecting again, and this time I'm on a mission to find a good pregnancy pillow. I tried a large body pillow on the advice of another site for my first pregnancy, and it was honestly an awful experience—the pillow was too large and firm for me to comfortably use, let alone have room for both it and my growing midsection in my bed. Plus, it was heavy, which is annoying when your body already feels too cumbersome to move around.
So far, using the Wildbird Pregnancy Pillow has been the opposite. It's slim and light with just enough squish to add a little support under or around my belly without being difficult to get comfortable. It’s beautiful and easy to maneuver around. Wildbird also suggests it for other support positions postpartum, and I'm curious if those will work for me. But it makes for a beautiful gift for any expecting mom and will be one she's excited to put on her bed and curl up with at night.
For the Gamer Mom
Once my kiddo is asleep, you can find me parked on the couch playing video games. I upgraded to a Nintendo Switch 2 ($499) earlier this summer so I could finally buy and play Pokopia ($70), since it's exclusive to the new console, and I already can't wait to use it to play the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ($60) remake coming out in November. It's also quickly become an experience I can share with my son now that he's 4; he's been helping me and my husband replay Tears of the Kingdom, but he mostly requests we help him build monster-hunting robots and cook food for Link like he's a starving Tamagotchi.
If you're not looking to upgrade her console just yet but need a Switch-friendly cozy game for her, Stardew Valley has another big update in the works and only costs $15. I'm also hoping we see Fields of Mistria ($14) come to the Switch eventually, but the full launch came out in August for Steam users and has major quality-of-life improvements if she has played Stardew one time too many. My husband also upgraded his gaming setup this summer with a Steam Machine (from $1,049), and I have big plans to start using it often for Fields of Mistria. If your mom loves games, she'll love any one of these new devices or new games if she already got herself the new gadget like I did.
For Ultimate Everything Showers
For most moms, showers are sacred—especially for moms of babies or younger kids. However, heavy metals, sediments, chlorine, and PFAS can cause health problems not just in drinking water but in water that touches the skin, as well. They can also cause buildup on hair and shower surfaces, making them harder to clean. Many municipalities—including mine—treat water with chlorine, and when I asked him which filter he'd recommend for my own shower, former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage suggested the Weddell Duo. It's the only US filter he's found that has certification for chlorine and lead removal from NSF International, and it also cites third-party testing by IAPMO R&T showing it can remove PFAS, though there's no corresponding certification.
Still, the Duo has a 2.5-gallon-per-minute flow rate and can remove most chlorine from over 8,000 gallons' worth of showers. It's an in-line filter, so it's easy to install in minutes—just screw it in between your pipe and showerhead. It even comes with a little roll of waterproof tape to ensure a leak-free fit, and because of the horizontal orientation, installation won't affect the showerhead height. The filter needs to be replaced every three months, but refills only run about $25 each, compared with competitors like Filterbaby or Rorra, which can cost $40 to $45. —Kat Merck
For Moms With a Full Camera Roll
As a mom, I take a lot of photos of my family. A lot. And sometimes it feels like all those great photos of my son's milestones go to my camera roll and photo storage to die. There are two solutions I love for this that are incredibly giftable: a digital photo frame she can instantly upload images to, and a printed photo book where you can take the best of the best and put them at her fingertips. I have and love both for different reasons.
I love the digital photo frame to add all the photos from a fun weekend at the San Diego Zoo or Renaissance Pleasure Faire for me to relive again and again, but I also love being able to pull a photo book from the bookshelf and relive a specific moment I know is waiting there for me. Aura makes my favorite digital photo frames (followed by Skylight and the Calendar 2 if you want a multipurpose device, but Aura has no subscription fee if you only want photos), while Mixbook has been a favorite of mine for a while when it comes to printing photos, and has great starting prices for its photo books.
A Bird’s-Eye View
If you know a mom who loves to bird-watch (I know one!), you can upgrade her bird feeder to a smart one. Smart bird feeders add a camera to the feeder so she can see a close-up feed of the birds that come to hang out in her yard, and they're adorable to boot, for a little smart curb appeal. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck recommends the original Birdfy feeder as a great gift; it's her favorite smart bird feeder and comes in adorable colors to brighten your mom's yard and catch the eye of neighborhood birds. But the one she and I both have our eye on (her for her mother, me for myself) is the Birdfy Nest Duo, which is actually a birdhouse with two cameras so you can see the birds entering the nest outside and raising a family inside.
Compression Care
There's a wellness gadget for everything now. Rings that track your sleep and blood oxygen levels, masks to make you look younger, massagers to relax your muscles, and now boots to improve circulation. WIRED reviewer Boutayna Chokrane says her mom loves these compression boots from Therabody to improve circulation, which is a common problem for many of our aging parents. These boots combine compression, vibration, and LED therapy into a single wearable device that comes with eight preset routines to focus on legs, knees, and joints. It's a unique option if she wants better recovery for her legs or better circulation for her health.
Better Espresso
The DeLonghi Rivelia is the best and easiest and most user-friendly superautomatic espresso machine I have tested. What’s superautomatic mean? It means you pour whole beans into the hopper, put milk in the milk carafe, and select the drink you want to make on the touchscreen menu. Then you let the machine do most of the rest. The style of espresso made by a superautomatic machine like this Rivelia is generally a bit smoother and less intense than the sort you get in a café. But the process is also less finicky; you won’t be dealing with coffee grounds and portafilters. What’s especially nice with this Rivelia is the ability to make multiple “profiles” for different coffee drinkers in the house, each with their own favorite drinks—and the ability to swap out bean hoppers to make decaf coffee in the afternoon. The Rivelia is also the machine my own mother, a drinker of lattes and dark-roast beans, loves unreservedly. Like others on the WIRED Reviews team, I often ask colleagues and those close to me to test my top-rated machines over long periods to see how they hold up over months or years of regular use. My mother thanks me nearly every month for letting her test the Rivelia. —Matthew Korfhage

The clip was shared by X handle @Deshmukh_0 on November 13 at around 6:07 pm, with the claim that the members of the RSS raided and vandalised the restaurant following an altercation with the owner over non-payment of dues. The RSS men had eaten there but refused to pay, the post claimed. (Archive)

The post garnered 106,700 views and over 2,000 reshares.
The 25-second-long clip shows a mob breaking glass panes and ransacking the space. The caption, written in Hindi, says when the owner asked for payment, the RSS members accused the restaurant of wrongly serving them chicken.
The same clip was shared by X user @yadavanoop08, with the claim that certain “RSS goons caused a ruckus” at a restaurant in West Bengal after they were asked to pay their bill. (Archive)

सालो की औकात अगर बिल देने की न हो तो खाना ही क्यों खाते है। https://t.co/o3KquCIEn7
— PDA परिवार (@yadavanoop08) November 13, 2026
Several other users also shared the video with identical claims on X.
Fact Check
In order to determine the veracity of these claims, first, we ran a reverse image search on some of the keyframes of the viral clip. This led us to images of a restaurant called Durbin Bangla located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Below is a comparison of a frame from the viral video and an image of the restaurant we found online.
The viral video also contains footage of the incident shot from outside the restaurant. We examined keyframes from this clip and compared them with photographs of the outside facade of the restaurant available online. See below:
These comparisons prove conclusively that the restaurant shown in the viral clip is not in West Bengal, but in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Further, the viral clip shows a police officer in a green uniform in the midst of the chaos. This matches the uniform worn by Bangladesh police.
A keyword search then led us to several news reports (The Daily Star, The Financial Express and Dhaka Tribune) on a mob attack and vandalism at Durbin Bangla restaurant in Dhaka’s Mohakhali on November 13, 2026.
The Daily Star reported that a disagreement over a vacant seat at the restaurant eventually escalated into a heated conflict, followed by a clash with the restaurant employees and vandalism at the restaurant.
To sum up, the viral video is from Bangladesh. It shows an incident at Durbin Bangla restaurant in Dhaka. The claim that a group of RSS members is seen vandalising a restaurant in Bengal over non-payment of bill and being served chicken is false.

EXCLUSIVE: Greg Hovanessian (The Mist, Cardinal) and Lindsey Normington (Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Anora) are set to lead the new psychological thriller Nightwaves, from writer and director Kristian McKay (Do Not Open, Kill Trip) and Obscura Film. Cherie Currie (Foxes, Twilight Zone: The Movie) and Shane Coffey (Pretty Little Liars, Good Girls) will also star.
Set against the dark, desolate highways of Texas, Nightwaves unfolds over the course of a single night, following Mason (Hovanessian), a young man driving alone whose unexpected phone conversation with a mysterious woman (Normington) offers an initially welcome escape. As their exchange shifts from flirtation to increasingly unsettling questions, the woman on the other end of the line begins to threaten everything Mason is desperately trying to leave behind. With each passing mile, he finds himself moving closer to a confrontation he cannot simply hang up to avoid.
Currie and Coffey’s roles are under wraps.
Watch on Deadline
Production is currently underway in San Antonio and the surrounding Texas landscape.
“There’s something incredibly intimate about talking to someone in the dark when you can’t see their face. You start filling in the blanks, and that can be seductive or terrifying,” shared McKay. “With Nightwaves, I want the audience to feel that connection tightening until it becomes a trap. Greg and Lindsey bring the vulnerability and unpredictability these roles demand, and having Cherie and Shane in this world gives the film such a distinct personality.”
Obscura Film touts in a release how “McKay will bring a distinctive visual approach to the thriller, allowing tension and performances to unfold in extended, uninterrupted moments. Using the empty stretches of highway, passing headlights, and the confined interior of a moving car, the film transforms an ordinary phone conversation into an increasingly claustrophobic psychological experience, where what remains unseen may be more terrifying than anything in view.”
The film is produced by Obscura Film partners Daunesh Alcott and McKay, alongside Jose Corres. Executive produced by Gustavo Oliveira.
Nightwaves expands Obscura Film’s growing slate of independently produced genre features. The project follows Kill Trip, acquired by Quiver Distribution and released in 2026, and Do Not Open, McKay’s supernatural thriller starring Freddy Carter, Lulu Wilson, Mark McKenna, John Ford Coley and Stelio Savante, which is currently in post-production.
Hovanessian is repped by Robert Stein Management and Clear Talent Group. Normington is repped by Innovative Artists and Authentic Talent & Literary Management. Coffey is repped by Industry Entertainment and Pakula/ King.

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.
Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on Thursday.
Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return. Her supporters are protesting against the government’s rejection of that request.
To deter violence, 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, considered to have many Hasina supporters, a spokesperson said.
Police said former interim leader Yunus’ ancestral home in Chattogram, about 300km (186 miles) south-east of Dhaka, was set on fire late on Wednesday.
It is likely that flammable substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, police told Reuters, adding that Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, are safe.
Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre thinktank that speaks on his behalf to seek comment. Yunus and his government, which led Bangladesh after Hasina’s ouster, have faced hostility from her supporters.
During the last 10 days of protests, police have reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles being set afire in at least 28 districts, injuring several police officials and members of the public, media have said.
Late on Tuesday, an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest near Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj, police said.
On the same night, a crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of cultural affairs minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added.
On Wednesday morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said.
Tuesday marks a year since Hasina was sentenced to death by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising against her in 2024. She has lived in exile in neighbouring India since fleeing Dhaka.
On Thursday, authorities detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who faces charges over several killings during the 2024 protests, from his house in Dhaka, police told Reuters.
At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires since 10 November, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday, the bank said.
On Tuesday, the home minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of inciting supporters to destabilise Bangladesh and torch property, adding that those involved in violence would be identified and prosecuted.
Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment.

The Department of Medical Education is preparing to start two new government medical colleges in Ramanagara of Bengaluru South District and Puttur of Dakshina Kannada District for the academic year of 2027-28, and a proposal will be submitted to the National Medical Commission (NMC) soon.
“The construction work for the medical college on the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) new campus in Ramanagara is progressing rapidly. The tender for the medical college in Puttur has been finalised, and the construction will commence shortly. We will apply to the NMC to start these colleges from 2027-28 with a capacity of at least 50 seats,” Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil said.
“There is also a proposal to start medical colleges in Vijayapura and Kolar districts. The cabinet will decide on that soon,” he added.
The government has decided to start a medical college in every district of the State. There are 25 now. If colleges are established in Ramanagara, Puttur, Vijayapura, and Kolar districts, only Tumakuru, Bengaluru Rural, and Udupi districts will have to have a government medical college of their own.
Currently, there are 76 medical colleges in the State, comprising 25 government and 51 private institutions, with a total of 15,745 seats available for the 2026-27 academic year. If the Ramanagara and Puttur colleges are approved for the next academic year, with 50 seats each, this will go up to 78 colleges with 15,845 seats.
Will NMC approve this year?
The NMC has rejected the State’s applications for starting medical colleges in Kanakapura and Ramanagara four times from 2023-24 to 2026-27, for want of infrastructure, including teaching and non-teaching staff. Will the commission approve the proposals this year at least is the moot question.
In this context, the State government decided to construct a medical college and hospital in Kanakapura at an estimated cost of about ₹550 crore, and the construction work is in progress. However, the work of the medical college planned to be built on the proposed Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) campus in Ramanagara is only 70% complete. Therefore, the government has decided to start the medical college using the district hospital.
“The construction of medical college on the RGUHS new campus in Ramanagara will be completed soon. Consequently, steps have been taken to shift the university to the new campus within the next three to four months. Meanwhile, the construction of a medical college and hospital in Kanakapura is progressing rapidly, and once the work is complete, a proposal will be submitted to the MNC for the commencement of the college,” Mr. Patil said.

Jensen Huang was ousted from Nvidia amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. Yet it was “multiple issues” related to Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying” that ultimately moved the board of directors, according to two people familiar with private discussions among the chair and other members.
While Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang on November 8, the board couldn’t determine in the moment whether she was an intelligence operative for China, these sources say. That same day, the board announced an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting” that their CEO had “been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has rejected allegations that Alice Huang was a spy.
But in the following days, once allegations of other affairs surfaced, including one reportedly with a direct report, “what could be determined was [Huang’s] lying, and that spanned a year, from October 2025 through recent events,” a source close to the board told WIRED, who requested anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak on its behalf.
According to sources, members of the board had asked Huang about Alice Huang after The New York Times first reported in October 2025 that Nvidia had an unusually robust business relationship with a Singapore-based data center company named Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked. Jensen Huang at the time denied any inappropriate relationship with Alice Huang to the board, sources tell WIRED.
After the affair came to light, the board was incensed, these people say. A source familiar with the board’s thinking told WIRED that while these board members view issues of national security as “important” and “ongoing,” the primary driver behind Huang’s ouster was “the lying.”
“It was a matter of integrity and trust,” this person said.
In recent days, board members, including chair Harvey Jones, have tried to quell the discourse about Huang’s possible return to Nvidia by emphasizing that Huang's behavior flew in the face of Nvidia’s policies and corporate governance rules, sources tell WIRED. While previous reporting by WIRED and other news outlets have outlined factors that Jones has said played into the board’s decision, the primary motivation hadn’t been previously specified.

|---|
| Are you a current or former Nvidia employee who has information to share? We’d like to hear from you. Using a nonwork phone or computer, contact WIRED reporters securely on Signal at ChaoticGoode.12 & Peard33.24 | 
Board chair Harvey Jones did not respond to a WIRED request for comment. A spokesperson for Nvidia, John Rizzo, declined to comment. John Fisher, vice president at the communications firm Trident, which is representing Huang, declined to comment except to say that Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions at Nvidia.
For Nvidia’s board, the possibility that Alice Huang was working on behalf of the Chinese government poses a bigger problem than an executive’s personal misconduct. If she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, the scandal isn’t just about Huang’s alleged “lack of candor,” but a potential security and governance crisis.
Already the scandal has given China hawks grist to call for tighter controls on US business dealings with China. In addition, multiple government agencies and offices have called for investigations into what the former Nvidia CEO may have known about the company’s chips getting into China. The company’s general counsel Tim Teter has also been called to Washington, DC to testify, as government officials try to find out more about Nvidia’s possible flouting of export controls.
Nvidia and Huang are also facing several shareholder lawsuits, alleging the CEO and the company made misleading statements about dealings with Alice Huang and Megaspeed. Other Silicon Valley investors have publicly raised concerns about insufficient corporate governance and executive oversight by the board.
In the company’s all-hands meeting on November 18, board chair Jones said it was “not an easy decision to accept [Huang’s] resignation,” according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. “However, the disclosure of personal behavior and a lack of candor inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and values made this a necessary decision.”
Meanwhile, fans and supporters of Huang, including thousands of Nvidia employees and Elon Musk, have continued to call for his return to Nvidia. Huang himself has said he would be “honored” to come back as CEO. On Friday, US President Donald Trump renewed his call for Huang to have another chance. “He made some bad decisions, but he is a brilliant person,” Trump told reporters. “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology.”
The news outlet Semafor reported that a small faction of Nvidia’s board of directors has pushed to bring Huang back as well. Jones has not responded to WIRED’s inquiries about the board’s reported division on the topic of Huang’s return.
Some employees are miffed at how quickly the board accepted Huang’s resignation, insisting the longtime leader must have been the victim of a coordinated campaign intended to unseat him. “We feel like they forced his hands to resign,” says one person on the business side at Nvidia. “We don’t understand why the board is so adamant about not giving him a second chance.”
At the all-hands meeting, interim CEO Colette Kress said employees’ biggest concern was Nvidia’s falling share price. The next biggest concern was the board’s decision to oust Huang. But while she addressed the first by moving up pay raises, she offered no promise on sharing results of the board’s investigation into Huang or its deliberations about him.
“The ship has sinked but there’s no plan to be transparent about what happened,” says one computer scientist working at Nvidia. “It feels like a black box.”

These dead pets were meant to be cremated - then their bodies appeared on a livestream
- Published
The livestream begins.
A man – bald, goateed, wearing red-tinted sunglasses – walks down a cracked back road, guiding the camera towards a cluster of plastic-wrapped objects that spill out of the tall grass.
Names are written on the packages – Brandon; Ira; Lucky; Sweet – and numbers. One says 29kg (4.5 stone). Another says 2.5kg. Through the plastic you can make out what appears to be fur, claws and a flattened ear.
It's a mass dumping, the man explains. "We have about 25 animals here that have been dumped in bags. A couple of cats, some dogs."
"Purebreds," says the woman filming.
Warning: This story contains images some might find upsetting
In the weeks since that video was streamed on Facebook, Chris and Geraldine Taylor, who run animal rescue NGO Luna and Furry Siblings (LAFS), say they have uncovered 15 dumping sites in the suburbs of Bulacan, near the Philippines' capital of Manila.
In total they've unearthed the remains of some 170 dead pets. Belgian Malinois, golden retrievers, pugs, puppies and cats have been found dumped off service roads, sealed in septic tanks, floating in rivers and buried in vacant lots.
Many of these animals are thought to have been sent to cremation businesses in the expectation they would be turned to ash.
Now, many grieving owners are having to confront a distressing reality: their beloved pets may not have received the send-off they paid for. The urn in their home may not contain their pet at all. And they may in fact see their so-called fur child again, jettisoned like common waste on the side of a highway.
One saw the livestream and wrote on Facebook: "I think one of those pets is mine." Below, they attached a photo of a beaming Alsatian.
170 carcasses found
When Chris arrived on that back road three weeks ago, he couldn't have known he was uncorking a scandal that would see at least one business reportedly shut, four people placed under investigation, and a personal invite to sit down with a senator to discuss animal-cruelty laws.
Chris, a former police officer, and his wife are retired, but only formally. For the past three years, they've been running an animal rescue shelter out of their home in San Jose del Monte, 30km (18.6 miles) north-east of central Manila.
On 30 October, he'd driven into town to report a case of animal neglect at the local district office. When he arrived, he was told the official in charge had just left to respond to another complaint: a report of dumped animals on a nearby roadside.
Chris had seen this once before: 14 dogs that were found and soon reburied. This time, he followed the official to the scene and started documenting – taking photos, scanning the bodies for microchips and uploading footage to his Facebook page.
"I figured there's got to be more to this," he explains. "So we put out word: if anybody knows anything, any other dump locations... just report it. Let us know."
In the days that followed, tip-offs started trickling in. More dumpsites emerged.
"The long vacant lot on the left side... that's where the smell comes from," read one message.
"When we ran to this place it smelled of rotting animals," read another, accompanied by a photo of a map with a location circled in red.
By crowdsourcing intel in this way, and collaborating with authorities, LAFS has so far uncovered a total of 15 dumpsites, containing an estimated 170 animals. "Some of them were just bags of bones," Chris says. "Others were liquefied."
LAFS has meticulously documented the crime scenes. Often wearing little more for protection than an N95 mask and rubber gloves, Chris crouches in the underbrush and slices open discarded plastic bags, picking through the contents while Geraldine holds the camera.
Their Facebook videos have racked up more than 30 million views. Commenters ask Chris if he has seen their pet among the bodies, or if he can turn a carcass over so they can check for identifying marks.
Some are successful. On that first night in October, all 25 bodies were returned to their owners.
There's a question which hangs uncomfortably over every dumpsite: who would do something like this?
As more owners came forward, a common denominator emerged. Many said they'd taken the animals to be incinerated at the same place: a crematorium called Ahjay Paws in the city of Bacoor, not far from Manila.
"So I posted: anybody that's had Ahjay's services... these might be your animals," says Chris. "And man, it just flooded in."
'God knows what was inside those urns'
The Philippines has long been a dog-loving nation, but since the Covid-19 pandemic the "fur parenting" community has exploded.
A 2021 study found the country had the highest rate of dog ownership in the Asia-Pacific. Since then, the pet dog population has increased 4.7% year on year, according to another study, exceeding 21 million in 2025.
As the numbers soar, businesses have stepped up to address an inevitable implication: more deaths.
"Cremation here in the Philippines has become quite a big thing with the boom of the pet industry," says Anna Cabrera, director at the Philippine Animal Welfare Society (Paws). "There's even a ceremony where they hold wakes for the pets."
These events offer grieving owners a last chance to see their beloved pets before they're taken to a crematorium and transmuted into an urnful of ashes.
Or not, as the case may be.
Revecca Calling, who lives south of Bulacan in the city of Cavite, says she paid Ahjay Paws 8,500 Philippine pesos (£100; $133) to cremate her dog Olaf in January. The price was calculated according to weight, and included a 30-minute viewing where she could say her final goodbye.
Calling says Ahjay Paws told her they couldn't record the cremation, as it might endanger the staff. They took away Olaf's body, and a few days later handed back a small urn that purportedly contained her cremated remains.
When nine months later Calling heard that dozens of animals' bodies had been found dumped on an empty plot of land, potentially at the behest of a pet cremation business, she was devastated.
"Pet owners entrust these services with something very important: the remains of a beloved family member," she says. "We need to know what happened."
Earlier this month, the Philippines' National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed criminal complaints against four individuals in connection with dumped pets. Among them is the owner of Ahjay Paws and two people who ran Bulacan's Pet HPHT Crematory.
According to the NBI, Ahjay Paws had initially arranged to acquire a cremation machine from Pet HPHT – but when it didn't arrive, they opted to send the pet remains to Pet HPHT instead. When the volume of those remains became more than Pet HPHT could handle, that firm paid a third party to bury them.
One interpretation is that the dumping incidents are a result of logistical failures: two businesses that bit off more than they could chew and took desperate measures to make the problem go away.
But there's another theory: that the dead pets could be evidence of a lucrative racket, with people's money taken to incinerate their pets but the animals then being dumped instead.
There is a word for this kind of deception in Philippine law – estafa; where a perpetrator knowingly misleads a victim to financially defraud them – and the NBI say they are investigating it as a possibility in this case.
Two weeks ago, Ahjay Paws' owner denied responsibility for the dumping in San Jose del Monte, according to local media. The company is apparently no longer operating, and the BBC has been unable to contact it.
The BBC has also reached out to Pet HPHT and invited it to respond. On Facebook, the firm said the dumping allegations were "completely false and have no basis".
Another grieving pet owner, Emelia Legada, says she paid Ahjay Paws 10,000 Philippine pesos (£120; $160) to cremate her dog Harvey six months ago.
"I just can't accept the pain of not knowing what might have happened to him," she says. "I really want to confirm whether Harvey was properly cremated, and whether the ashes I received were truly his."
Many are wrestling with the same uncertainty. As Cabrera puts it: "God knows what that was inside those urns."
In response to those anxieties, a veterinarian in nearby Quezon City has started offering complimentary forensic ash testing. For those whose pets have been found among the bodies, other crematoriums have offered to do the job properly, and for free.
The animal welfare society, Paws, is volunteering legal services to help people file complaints with the authorities, and has received more than 150 requests so far. It is also calling for a nationwide audit of all pet cremation businesses.
Animal-cruelty law 'doesn't apply'
On 2 November, Percival Vilar Cendaña of the Philippines' progressive Akbayan Party appeared on national television. He was there to speak about the pet-dumping scandal, which, in the span of a few days, had flared into a national disgrace.
"Our worst fears have been confirmed," he told the Bilyonaryo news channel. "Now we see that these are not isolated incidents. It is true that this is a syndicate that is conducting widespread operations."
Neither the police nor the NBI have confirmed that the dumpings were carried out by a "syndicate", nor that they were "widespread". Many details surrounding the case remain murky. But the hysteria is real – and Cendaña was giving voice to a common sentiment.
"Those who deceived these poor fur parents should be jailed," he said.
At least three individuals have surrendered to the NBI and been charged with violating the city's Code of Sanitation, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, and the Sanitation Code of the Philippines.
But many feel this doesn't go far enough, and say it fails to hold anyone liable for the way the animals' remains were treated.
Cabrera says the country's animal-cruelty law doesn't cover the treatment of animals after death. And "there's no crime if there's no law".
The scandal has prompted a groundswell to change that. Lawmakers like Cendaña are pushing for a national commission on animal welfare to ensure their dignity in life and death.
Meanwhile, Cabrera says Paws will seek "moral and exemplary" damages on behalf of aggrieved pet owners.
One woman whose dog was suspected to have been found among the dumped bodies told the BBC she couldn't speak about it because she was "feeling weak".
"I haven't slept for three days from all the crying," she said.
Chris has also been losing sleep, taking calls from grieving pet owners who have watched his videos. "Hundreds of people call me in tears, just sobbing," he says.
"They're in so much pain. And half the time you're telling them: 'you're not going to find your pet. It's been too long; we're not going to be able to identify it.' And it just crushes them."
As well as new laws, Chris wants stricter enforcement of existing rules. He wants to know how he managed to unearth so much in the space of a fortnight, and why people keep coming to him saying they don't trust the police to take their concerns seriously, he says.
The BBC contacted Philippine National Police (PNP) for comment, but didn't hear back. Earlier this month, PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr said authorities were determined to hold accountable those who allegedly took advantage of grieving pet owners, saying such exploitation "must be addressed with the full force of the law", according to ABS-CBN.
"Fraud is not measured solely by the amount of money taken, but also by the damage inflicted on the people whose trust has been betrayed," Nartatez said.
"To the affected pet owners, we recognise the pain and distress this incident has caused your families."
Yet the police themselves have come under official scrutiny.
On Monday, the National Police Commission announced an investigation into officers in Cavite and Bulacan after they suggested LAFS might be involved in the pet dumping because they were often first on the scene. The officers did not present evidence for their claims. The investigation also covers reports that officers visited the Taylors' home and took photographs.
Meanwhile, countless grieving pet owners are suspended in purgatory: desperate for closure on what happened to their dogs and cats, and calling on authorities to do more.
"We want the case to be properly investigated and those responsible to be held accountable," says Calling. "I believe that no secret remains hidden forever."
Legada, for her part, says: "I just want to find out what really happened to Harvey and where his remains are. I want to know whether he was properly cremated."
She also wants people to know: "You can't trust anyone these days."

When discussing cervical cancer, what often gets left out is that it is one of the most preventable of cancers. Despite this, cervical cancer continues to be a cause of thousands of deaths among women every year, not only in India, but in many parts of the world. In many such cases, the condition is detected far too late, leaving limited room for intervention. The issue therefore, is not a gap in science, but a gap in awareness
The main culprit in cervical cancer is a virus that is very common, human papillomavirus, or HPV for short. HPV primarily spreads through close skin-to-skin contact, most often during sexual intercourse. The virus is so widespread that virtually everyone, both men and women, at some point in their lifetime, will be infected without even realising it. More often than not, the immune system gets rid of the virus without causing any damage.

New Delhi, Nov 23: The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Wacom India to strengthen India-Japan cooperation in animation, visual effects, gaming and other creative technologies.
The agreement was signed on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026. It aims to provide Indian students access to professional tools, industry-led training and international exposure.
Under the partnership, 18 students enrolled in IICT’s three two-year diploma programmes in Animation Film Design, Interactive Video Game Design and Development, and Post Production and VFX will receive 50 per cent tuition scholarships. Eligible students from outside Mumbai will also get accommodation assistance.
The collaboration will include 10 Wacom-branded creative contests and quarterly masterclasses on Manga, Anime and other creative disciplines, conducted by Japanese and Indian artists and experts until December 2027.
The two institutions will also jointly develop a global student portfolio showcase covering digital illustration, concept art, character design, animation and game art to help students build industry-ready portfolios.
IICT Founding Director Ashish Kulkarni said the partnership would connect young Indian creators with global creative ecosystems by bringing together Japan’s strengths in animation, manga and gaming with India’s diverse storytelling heritage.
IICT CEO Vishwas Deoskar said practical experience through contests, masterclasses and portfolio development would improve students’ employability in the AVGC-XR sector. Wacom Global Head of Creative Experience Unit Koji Yano said the collaboration would promote knowledge exchange and enable young Indian creators to participate in global creative partnerships.

From its origins as a racing game called Race ‘n’ Chase to billion-dollar sales records, GTA has a fascinating history. Here are 11 surprising facts about the franchise, including Hollywood connections, hidden ghosts, clever anti-piracy tricks, celebrity lawsuits, and its Scottish roots.
After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar Games has finally launched perhaps the most anticipated game in the recent history of gaming. Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6). It has been barely a few days since the game hit the stands and the Web, and it already has the world (gaming and non-gaming too) in its grip, and is setting sales records.
Its release means saying goodbye to the legendary “we got (this/something) before GTA 6” meme, but GTA 6 is already carving a place for itself in the franchise’s history, a history marked by crime, cars, and chaos and a lot of other things that even diehard fans might not be aware of.
From celebrity lawsuits to ghosts and many controversies, the world of GTA is filled with insane stories. So even as you set yourself up for another session of GTA 6 or wait for your copy of the game to download, or just turn your nose up at “crazy gamers who will line up for anything”, here are eleven amazing facts you might not know (but should know) about the legendary Grand Theft Auto franchise.
Table of Contents
It was originally supposed to be a racing game (and called Race’n’Chase)
It may look completely different today, but GTA was originally supposed to be a fast-paced, addictive racing game called “Race ‘n’ Chase.” Development of the game got underway in the mid-nineties, but the developers did not quite get things right. Early models had car-crashing issues and coding glitches that made police cars ram into player cars aggressively, instead of just chasing them. This, of course, took away its traditional racing game feel. But during testing, players enjoyed this glitch and chaos, so the developers decided to move away from a “Race n Chase” sort of setup and decided to create an open world action-oriented game. They called it Grand Theft Auto (GTA). The rest, as they love to say, is history.
Play the OG GTA online and free of cost
Want to experience the original Grand Theft Auto that was released in 1997? Well, you can actually play it for free online in a browser at https://www.playdosgames.com/online/grand-theft-auto/. Just make sure you have a keyboard handy, as it struggles with touch controls.
Thank you, Tony Montana! GTA: Vice City was inspired by Scarface!
Even the greatest video games have to draw inspiration from somewhere, and in the case of GTA: Vice City, inspiration came from Brian De Palma’s 1983 crime classic, Scarface. The developers used the movie as a blueprint to showcase how Miami looked back in the 80s. The protagonist in the game also follows a very similar arc to the protagonist in the film, the iconic Tony Montana, and even has a location similar to that of Tony Montana’s (Scarface’s protagonist) infamous mansion in it.
GTA has a lot of Hollywood in it…but is not too fond of stars
GTA has not just drawn inspiration from Hollywood, but has also featured many famous actors from it. The game has cast a number of actors, comedians, and musicians to either play themselves or voice a character. A key reason for hiring musicians and comedians to play themselves in the game or be a part of an extensive radio or DJ set is to make the city in the game feel even more real and lived in. Famous actors like Ray Liotta, Samuel L. Jackson, Burt Reynolds, and many more have been a part of the franchise. This tradition lives on with GTA 6, as this time around actors Dylan Rourke and Manni Perez have voiced the two leads of the game.
That said, problems with a number of high-profile stars (most notably Burt Reynolds) led Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser to say in an interview with Vulture “We don’t bring in name actors anymore because of their egos and, most important of all, because we believe we get a better sense of immersion using talented actors whose voices you don’t recognize.”
The Ghost Town of GTA 3 that is ‘out of bounds’
Imagine having a small part of the game that you cannot explore? Well, that is exactly what the Ghost Town in GTA 3 is. It has nothing to do with gameplay, lacks the general collision mechanism of the game, and yet it exists. The ‘out of bounds’ area was actually designed as part of GTA 3’s opening cinematics and was put away from the main map, and kept in the game only for the intro scene. However, players found their way to the location using glitches and modifications, although they could not interact with it like the rest of the game. Before Vice City, there was Ghost City in the GTAverse.
Punishing pirates, the GTA way
By the time GTA 4 was released in 2008, the GTA franchise had become insanely famous. And with great celebrity and terrific sales comes…great piracy. As pirated and unauthorized units of the game became a problem, Rockstar Games used some very creative countermeasures to punish/ annoy those who bought pirated copies of the game. Unauthorized copies ended up with constant drunk effects on the camera, sudden and auto acceleration, broken mission scripts, damaged cars, and more, which were put in place to make the pirated game actually feel pirated. You do not pirate a gangster game easily!
Macabre and moving Easter eggs
The GTA franchise is laden with Easter eggs, but two of the most amazing ones are found in GTA 5. What makes them special is the attention to both detail and sentiment. These are not your run-of-the-mill “press this key and your car changes into Superman” or “use this key combo to start driving on Mars” kinds of easter eggs, but much more somber and sensitive ones.
In GTA 5 between 23:00 and 00:00, you can actually find a translucent figure at the peak of Mount Gordo. There is a flat rock where the ghost of “Jolene Cranley-Evans,” who was said to have been killed by her husband, Jock Cranley, appears around midnight. Jock had pushed her off the mountain peak, which is also why, when the player goes near the ghost, it disappears and “Jock” written in blood appears on the flat rock!
The other Easter egg is not as eerie but definitely heartbreaking. A small dog can be seen sitting quietly next to the grave of his owner in the Pacific Bluffs cemetery between 10:00 am and 11:00 am. This is the game paying tribute to a real grieving dog, Greyfriars Bobby, a 19th-century dog who guarded his owner’s grave for 14 years.
Watch the moon in GTA 5!
It was not just the easter eggs that were amazing in GTA 5. Rockstar Games upped their detail game (pun intended) by several notches, paying attention to the tiniest of details. The best example of this is the moon in the game. Yes, the moon. The moon in GTA 5 does not remain the same through the gameplay and actually goes through proper lunar phases– something many players might not even notice during regular gameplay. So you get full, crescent, waxing gibbous, and other phases of the moon while playing the game. Now, that’s one moonshot that worked.
GTA and controversies go hand in hand, and even the Guinness Book agrees
Ever since its release in 1997, the GTA franchise has been surrounded by controversies. And these have only gotten bigger with each new version. Celebrities like Lindsay Lohan, Karen Gravano, Michael Washington have filed lawsuits against Rockstar Games’ parent company Take-Two Interactive, for modeling its characters on them.
The game has also attracted a lot of criticism for its alleged glorification of violence and sexual themes – GTA: San Andreas was hit by the Hot Coffee controversy in 2004, when developers left explicit, sexual interactive code in the game instead of deleting it. They had disabled the code, but players used mods to access it, which allowed them to make the main character (CJ) have sexual encounters with characters after inviting them for coffee. The franchise had over 4,000 news stories published in July 2008, all related to violence, crime and misogyny perpetration. It is hardly surprising that it has been recognized as the most controversial video game franchise in history by Guinness World Records. Of course, millions still love it. But that is another story…
Generating the kind of revenues that make Hollywood envious
GTA games generate the kind of revenue that Hollywood blockbusters can only dream of. GTA 5 hit one billion USD in retail sales within three days, making it the fastest entertainment property overall to hit that milestone at that time. And GTA 6 seems to have followed in its footsteps. While no official figures have been released, it is estimated that nearly 25 million copies of the game were sold on the first day, and its earnings come to around 3.8 billion USD. Just for context, Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey has made USD 1.8 billion at the box office at the time of writing.
It is made in Scotland!
It might be released by a US company (Rockstar Games) and might feature US cities in its gameplay, but Grand Theft Auto is actually made in Edinburgh, Scotland, by Rockstar North, which was previously known as DMA Design, a company that was incorporated in Dublin. So yes, believe it or not, the game that many consider to be classically all-American was actually made by the Brits. And that too, by the ones that wear kilts. Bravehearts, truly.

India's cryptocurrency exchanges are facing turbulence on multiple fronts, with banking disruptions, regulatory scrutiny, and cybersecurity incidents exposing vulnerabilities across the industry. Over the past few weeks, Coinbase, CoinDCX, and ZebPay have reported delays or disruptions in INR withdrawals, each citing issues at banking partners. Separately, Unocoin disclosed estimated cryptocurrency losses of $0.2 Mn following a security breach, while CoinDCX reported a loss of 15.99 Mn USDT (Tether), worth approximately $16 Mn, from retired wallet infrastructure in October. The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has also intensified scrutiny of crypto-related financial flows, searching premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange in November over alleged unauthorised cross-border transactions. These developments expose different weaknesses across banking access, liquidity arrangements, and wallet security. Banking Channels Under Strain Coinbase India reported a banking partner outage on November 9 that disrupted its regular INR withdrawal facility. By November 20, it was processing pending withdrawals in batches through an alternative route, asking customers to contact support for transfers expected to take 48-72 hours. CoinDCX, meanwhile, warned users on November 19 that INR withdrawals were taking longer than usual because of processing changes at its banking partners. It initially said most withdrawals were being completed within four to six hours. Yesterday, the exchange said it processed 90% of withdrawal requests in under 90 minutes over the preceding 20 hours, with an average processing time of 68 minutes. It attributed the delays to ongoing system upgrades at banks but did not specify when real-time withdrawals would resume. ZebPay also reported INR withdrawal delays following a technical disruption at its banking partner. None of the three exchanges has identified the banks involved or confirmed whether the disruptions are connected. The disruptions come amid wider changes to banking infrastructure. Inc42 reported that Yes Bank’s upgrades to strengthen defences against AI-driven cyberattacks were disrupting payment service providers, with changes to its banking APIs delaying payment processing and settlements, according to industry sources. Industry participants Inc42 spoke to pointed to heightened scrutiny of intermediaries handling crypto-related financial flows as a possible source of pressure on banking and liquidity arrangements. Scrutiny Of Liquidity Channels In June, the ED searched six premises in Bengaluru linked to five platforms – Transak, Carret, Xpat, Onramp.money, and Onmeta – over alleged unauthorised cross-border transfers using virtual digital assets (VDAs). The agency alleged that the entities facilitated international money transfers through cryptocurrencies and stablecoins without the necessary authorisations under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA). In November, the ED searched premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange over alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto derivatives and real-world asset tokens. The agency alleged that the platforms used stablecoins to route transactions through overseas crypto platforms. The action had repercussions for domestic liquidity. Following the searches, market makers and liquidity providers reportedly pulled back from sourcing USDT overseas, tightening domestic supply. The stablecoin's premium on Indian platforms subsequently rose above 8.5%, compared with its usual 3-4% range. The ED's scrutiny continued in November, when it searched premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange India over alleged unauthorised cross-border financial transactions involving crypto derivatives and real-world asset tokens. The watchdog alleged routing of customer transactions through overseas platforms using stablecoins. These remain allegations under investigation. Exchanges rely on market makers and liquidity providers to facilitate trading. An industry executive familiar with crypto liquidity operations told Inc42 that enforcement action against intermediaries and heightened banking scrutiny are making it harder for exchanges to source liquidity through established channels. Dependence on external providers was also evident in October, when CoinDCX placed its futures platform in reduce-only mode, allowing users to reduce or close positions while restricting new ones. The exchange cited developments affecting a global liquidity provider, later identified as Binance. Binance separately disclosed an October 29 cyberattack affecting approximately $6.3 Bn in digital assets. The exchange said it had replenished 98% of the impacted tokens by October 31. The Binance breach highlights the security risks facing exchanges globally. In India, recent incidents at Unocoin and CoinDCX have exposed weaknesses in backup-key management and retired wallet infrastructure. Wallet Controls Under Test Unocoin detected suspicious activity on November 6 and suspended all services on November 9 while investigating a compromise of its infrastructure. In a November 14 update, the exchange said three operational hot wallets had been compromised, resulting in estimated cryptocurrency losses of $0.2 Mn. Hot wallets remain connected to the internet to facilitate transactions, unlike cold wallets, which keep signing keys offline. Unocoin said the unauthorised transactions used compromised backup signing keys associated with its multisignature wallets. It committed to covering the identified loss from its own resources without deducting it from customer balances. It also flagged potential exposure of customer information, including email addresses, residential addresses, encrypted passwords, account balances, and KYC-related details. The disclosure followed CoinDCX’s October loss from wallet infrastructure retired after its July 2025 security breach. The two incidents highlight risks extending beyond active trading systems to backup keys, retired infrastructure, and the processes used to move funds between wallets. AI Broadens Cyber Threats Preetam Rao, cofounder and CEO of blockchain security firm QuillAudits, said employees and third-party technology providers are increasingly becoming entry points for attackers. “The biggest risk today is an engineer’s laptop,” Rao said, citing fake freelance job offers, malicious software, and compromised developer tools used to access organisational systems. Separately, CERT-In issued a November 4 advisory warning of AI-assisted attacks targeting NBFCs, fintech companies, payment aggregators, payment service providers, and cryptocurrency exchanges. The agency identified a threat actor designated CRAFTY FALCON, which it said used machine intelligence to identify weaknesses and exploit payment and disbursement APIs to execute unauthorised transfers. In a fresh advisory on November 20, CERT-In also flagged unauthorised transactions involving service providers supporting government-linked payments and vendor payouts. Attackers manipulated business records and approval processes to move funds through legitimate payment systems. AI-assisted attacks are also widening the challenge for exchanges, putting pressure on them to strengthen defences beyond wallet security. Ritesh Bhatia, a cybersecurity expert and ransomware negotiator, said AI is increasing the speed and scale at which attackers could identify vulnerabilities. “The vulnerabilities which weren’t seen by the human mind are now being seen by AI” he said. Bhatia argued that organisations need stronger security resources and defensive use of AI to identify weaknesses. He also stressed the importance of incident response and disaster recovery, given the difficulty of preventing every attack. For crypto exchanges, losses can be particularly difficult to contain because blockchain transfers generally cannot be reversed unilaterally. Rao called for stronger controls over private keys, employee devices, wallet access, and third-party infrastructure. Stronger Rules And Safeguards The recent disruptions have sharpened the case for clearer rules on how India’s crypto exchanges hold customer assets, manage operational risks, and communicate when things go wrong. Rao recommended keeping the bulk of customer assets in cold storage, setting transaction limits, and requiring independent approvals for sensitive wallet transfers. He also called for backup keys and recovery passphrases to be stored offline. Such safeguards need to cover the entire custody system, including backup-key access and retired wallets that continue to receive deposits – weaknesses exposed by the Unocoin and CoinDCX incidents. Rao pointed to Hong Kong and Japan as examples of jurisdictions with more prescriptive custody requirements. Hong Kong requires licensed virtual asset trading platforms to keep 98% of customer crypto assets in cold storage, while Japan requires at least 95% to be managed offline. India’s crypto-specific framework primarily focuses on anti-money laundering compliance. A dedicated framework could establish consistent custody standards, independent audit requirements, customer notification timelines, and mechanisms for addressing losses and complaints. Clearer rules could also give banks, payment providers, and institutional liquidity partners greater certainty about working with exchanges, the industry executive quoted earlier said. For exchanges, the immediate task is to diversify banking and liquidity partners, strengthen source-of-funds checks, and tighten security controls. Regulation could set a common minimum standard, but exchanges remain responsible for ensuring those safeguards work when customers need to withdraw money or attackers find a way in.
